items.body:
Hello,

I happen to find a problem with the way supiOrSuci parameter is parsed. If I add enough hyphens I can crash UDM and make it restart.  Thanks to the compiler 's stack protection it the NF only crashes.

### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.7.2

### Steps to reproduce

To reproduce simply run this cURL
```bash
curl -X POST --http2-prior-knowledge http://127.0.0.11:7777/nausf-auth/v1/ue-authentications/deregister -d '{"supiOrSuci":"suci-0----------------------------------","servingNetworkName":""}'
``` 
I will also attach the logs of UDM and AUSF. The call will return a `500` code.



### Logs

```shell
Nov 09 15:41:13 open5gs open5gs-udmd[717]: *** stack smashing detected ***: terminated
Nov 09 15:41:14 open5gs systemd[1]: open5gs-udmd.service: Main process exited, code=killed, status=6/ABRT
Nov 09 15:41:14 open5gs open5gs-ausfd[701]: 11/09 15:41:14.111: [ausf] ERROR: [suci-0----------------------------------] HTTP response error [500] (../src/ausf/ue-sm.c:177)
Nov 09 15:41:14 open5gs systemd[1]: open5gs-udmd.service: Failed with result 'signal'.
Nov 09 15:41:16 open5gs open5gs-ausfd[701]: 11/09 15:41:16.225: [sbi] WARNING: [c6d5ceb8-9eb0-41ef-88f0-eb0d52d7a817] (NRF-notify) Not found (../lib/sbi/nnrf-handler.c:1171)
Nov 09 15:41:16 open5gs systemd[1]: open5gs-udmd.service: Scheduled restart job, restart counter is at 1.
Nov 09 15:41:16 open5gs systemd[1]: Stopped Open5GS UDM Daemon.
Nov 09 15:41:16 open5gs systemd[1]: Started Open5GS UDM Daemon.
Nov 09 15:41:16 open5gs open5gs-udmd[1522]: Open5GS daemon v2.7.2
```


### Expected behaviour

I expected to return 400 malformed input if a suci doesn't comply to standard.

### Observed Behaviour

 I  saw this bug happen in other routes that accept supiOrSuci like: 

```bash
# But in 2.7.2 seems to be fixed
GET `/nudm-uecm/v1/{ueId}/registrations/smf-registrations` 
```
This is why I think there is a problem in the function that parses the suci's. And as far as I could understand the issue could be solved as follows:

`lib/sbi/conv.c`
```diff
(...)
char *ogs_supi_from_suci(char *suci)
{
#define MAX_SUCI_TOKEN 16
    char *array[MAX_SUCI_TOKEN];
    char *p, *tmp;
    int i;
    char *supi = NULL;

    ogs_assert(suci);
    tmp = ogs_strdup(suci);
    if (!tmp) {
        ogs_error("ogs_strdup() failed");
        return NULL;
    }

    p = tmp;
    i = 0;
-    while((array[i++] = strsep(&p, "-"))) {
+    while(i < MAX_SUCI_TOKEN && (array[i] = strsep(&p, "-"))) {
        i++;
    }

(...)
```

Please let me know if there are any problems reproducing.  And if its okay to publish this kind of bug here, or rather through some other channels.

Kind regards,
Nicolas

### eNodeB/gNodeB

NA

### UE Models and versions

NA

items.title: Can't establish PDU session with srsran (ERROR: [1:0] No SmContextCreateError)
items.body:
### **Issue Description**
Hi everyone,
I am using **Open5GS** as the core network and **srsRAN** to set up the gNodeB and UE, with **ZeroMQ** for communication between the gNodeB and UE. However, after the UE establishes an RRC connection, it disconnects approximately ten seconds later. Upon reviewing the gNB logs, I discovered that the PDU session establishment is timing out. I seek guidance on resolving this issue to **enable the UE to successfully establish and maintain a continuous PDU session with the AMF**.

At first, the error in my amf.log file was:
```
03/05 10:44:33.963: [amf] DEBUG: amf_state_operational(): OGS_EVENT_NAME_SBI_CLIENT (../src/amf/amf-sm.c:81)
{"type":"/nnssf-nsselection/v2","title":"Cannot find NSI by S-NSSAI[SST:1 SD:0x1]","status":403,"instance":"/network-slice-information"}03/05 10:44:33.963: [amf] ERROR: [imsi-001010000000001] HTTP response error [403] (../src/amf/nnssf-handler.c:63)
```
Then, based on [Open5GS Issue #859](https://github.com/open5gs/open5gs/issues/859), I modified my nssf.yaml file and added the SD information. However, after this modification, I encountered a new error in amf.log:
```
03/05 11:14:45.102: [amf] DEBUG: amf_state_operational(): OGS_EVENT_NAME_SBI_CLIENT (../src/amf/amf-sm.c:81)
{"title":"(NF discover) No NF-Instance [nsmf-pdusession:AMF]","status":400}03/05 11:14:45.102: [amf] ERROR: [1:0] No SmContextCreateError (../src/amf/nsmf-handler.c:192)
```
I suspected an issue with the SMF, so I checked its status and found that it was not running:
```

```
So, is this issue caused by the SMF? How can I properly establish the PDU session?

### **Setup Details**
The setup consists of four virtual machines, each running Ubuntu 22.04. The details are as follows:

I am trying to connect a 3rd party SGW to the Open5GS SMF/PGW, and during the Create Session Request the SMF responds with "No Session" (Context Not Found).

Both in the smf.yaml and in pcrf.yaml the "Session" part is configured:

items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.7.0

### Steps to reproduce

Please set up the environment following the instructions at [https://github.com/s5uishida/open5gs_5gc_ueransim_sample_config](https://github.com/open5gs/open5gs/issues/url), we use just one UE and one UPF.
Our fuzzing tool found a possible bug when testing UE attachment process.
Just continuously run this script until SMF crashes.
```shell
#!/bin/bash
./open5gs/install/bin/open5gs-amfd &
ssh user@xxx.xxx.xxx.xxx /UERANSIM/build/runGnb.sh &
ssh user@xxx.xxx.xxx.xxx /UERANSIM/build/runUE.sh &
sleep 1.5
pkill open5gs-amfd
ssh user@xxx.xxx.xxx.xxx pkill nr-gnb
ssh user@xxx.xxx.xxx.xxx pkill nr-ue
``` 
This script means opening AMF and gNB, and initiating UE attach process when all other network elements are already up. It then terminates AMF, gNB, and UE before the UE attach process is completed.

After reviewing the source code, we found that the reason for SMF crashing is likely due to the failure to allocate an nf_instance from the nf_instance_pool during the ogs_sbi_nf_instance_add function. items.title: [Bug]: UE attached to 4G cell, terminates 4G connection, then attempts 5G cell attach with TAC update - fails connection

labels.description: Open5GS bug

labels.name: Housekeeping:ToClose
labels.description: Issues reviewed and closed. Old requests, issues which are not bug, feature or documentation request

items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

d0f628848471852c91b16dc5725cd604cd2d320d

### Steps to reproduce

This is a proposed one line change.  But a lot of information follows to explain the one line change.

Setup a UE on a 4G cell.  Also have a 5G cell available to the UE.

Next, disable the 4G cell.  The 4G connection terminates normally.

The UE scans the network and finds the 5G cell.

At this time the UE sends a registration to the 5G cell.  Open5gs sent back a reject with reason "Semantically incorrect message".  Then the UE did not try to attach again and lost the call forever.

Compare this scenario with a different core that we tested this scenario on.  With a different core (other than open5gs) the core sent back a reject also but with a reason "UE can't be derived by network".  Then the UE tried attach again and the 5G call was successful.  Although this was successful for the other core it could be suggested that not rejecting at all is good behavior.

There is a workaround which is that the Samsung UE could be put into airplane mode and taken out of airplane mode and at that point the UE is able to attach to the 5G cell.  But this is a lot of manual effort on the user of the UE which could be avoided with a simple open5gs change.

Note: Issue only happens when registration request + tracking area update occurs on 5G cell attach following LTE cell being disabled.  If only registration occurs without a tracking area update (such as the first time system is up) then it is ok with no rejection.

I am attaching a proposed patch for this issue for consideration.  With the patch in place the UE is able to attach in this scenario.

[4gcelldrops_5gcellregister_july.patch](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/16166835/4gcelldrops_5gcellregister_july.patch)

I am attaching a wireshark (pcap) logfile of the behavior which is described further in the logs section.

[tcpdump_5g4gswitch.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/16166868/tcpdump_5g4gswitch.zip)


### Logs

```shell
See wireshark log attached to the above description.

UE at 172.16.0.220 in logs, open5gs at 172.16.0.22 (S1AP/LTE) and 172.16.0.21 (NGAP/5G)

Messages #1 thru #17 in wireshark log are when LTE cell is being disabled and UE is trying to prepare for switching to 5G cell.

Message #18 is where the UE tries to register with the 5G cell after the LTE cell is disabled.

Message #19 is the issue…   We receive a “Semantically incorrect message” from open5gs.

Thereafter the UE will not attempt to register with the 5G cell.  The UE won’t restart cell search on the 5G cell due to the open5gs response.

The only solution is to take the UE in and out of airplane mode.   After that occurs (such as on message #22 of the wireshark log) then the UE is able to register successfully on the 5G cell.
```


### Expected behaviour

It is expected that in this scenario that the core either not reject at all or respond back with "UE can't be derived by network" rather than responding with "Semantically incorrect message".  If this is done it will allow the UE to reattach again in this scenario.

The proposed patch is for no rejection at all.

### Observed Behaviour

The core responds back with "Semantically incorrect message" which does not allow the UE to attach again following 4G cell teardown.

### eNodeB/gNodeB

_No response_

### UE Models and versions

A mixture of Samsung S22 and S23 models

### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

### Steps to reproduce

I am experiencing an issue where users are able to remain connected to services even after their accounts have expired, services have been restarted, and the users have been deleted from the databases. This behavior has been observed in the following scenarios:

Account Expiration: When a user's account expires, they should be disconnected from the network. However, in my case, users are able to continue using services even after their accounts have expired.
Service Restart: When services are restarted, any ongoing user sessions should be terminated. However, in my case, users are able to remain connected even after the services have been restarted.
User Deletion: When a user is deleted from the databases, they should no longer be able to access any services. However, in my case, users who have been deleted are still able to remain connected and access services.

### Logs

_No response_

After account expiration, users should be disconnected.
After service restart, all ongoing user sessions should be terminated.
After user deletion, users should no longer be able to access any services.

### Observed Behaviour

Users remain connected and can use services after account expiration.
Users remain connected and can use services after service restart.
Users remain connected and can use services even after being deleted from the databases.

- eNodeB A reinitiates the HO required procedure with the MME

items.title: UE IPv6 pool
items.body:
Hello

I'm having a play with assigning UEs IPv6 addresses for the first time. Finding some problems...! I'm not big on IPv6, so probably making some stupid mistakes. Wondering if anyone has any ideas what I need to change to get this working - thinking it is NAT related.

Configs are as follows:
```
smf:
    pdn:
      - addr: 10.45.0.1/24
      - addr: cafe::1/64
    dns:
      - 1.1.1.1
      - 8.8.8.8
      - 2001:4860:4860::8844
      - 2001:4860:4860::8888
```
```
upf:
    pdn:
      - addr: 10.45.0.1/24
      - addr: cafe::1/64
```
```
Phone Settings > APN > set to IPv4/IPv6
```

I get what appears to be a successful attach, UPF shows the phone is issused IPv4 and IPv6 addresses:
```
[upf] INFO: UE F-SEID[CP:0x1e UP:0x7] APN[internet] PDN-Type[3] IPv4[10.45.0.2] IPv6[cafe::2] (../src/upf/context.c:603)
[upf] INFO: [Added] Number of UPF-Sessions is now 1 (../src/upf/context.c:445)
```

Running the standard ogstun setups:
```
sudo sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_forward=1
sudo iptables -t nat -A POSTROUTING -s 10.45.0.0/16 ! -o ogstun -j MASQUERADE

sudo sysctl -w net.ipv6.conf.all.forwarding=1
sudo ip6tables -t nat -A POSTROUTING -s cafe::/64 ! -o ogstun -j MASQUERADE
```
Then try pinging // (PCAP addresses):

* UPF  `ping 10.45.0.2`  // sent from `10.45.0.1`, reply from `10.45.0.2`
* Phone  `ping 10.45.0.1`  // sent from `10.45.0.2`, reply from `10.45.0.1`
* Phone has WAN internet access via IPv4

but...

* UPF  `ping6 cafe::2` // sent from `cafe::1`, reply from `cafe::2`
* Phone `ping6 cafe::1` // sent from `cafe::16f:53b8:2dab:8380`, UPF replies; but phone doesnt get the reply
* Phone has no WAN internet access via IPv6

Phone IPs show as:
```
Phone Settings > About Phone > Status
10.45.0.2
cafe::6ead:c7da:152f:e904
```
This all seems a little odd to me... why is the phone sending pings with a different IPv6 address, and why does the phone show another different IPv6 address in settings?

```


### Expected behaviour

I expected the `amf_ue->mac_failed` flag to be cleared during security mode procedure but it was not. 
At this point, the only way to cleare the `amf_ue->mac_failed` flag is by UE Context Release.
But I'd like to connect UEs as fast as possible without UE Context Release.

I've tried to fix it on my own, but I'm not sure when the `amf_ue->mac_failed` flag should be cleared. 
I couldn't find any relevant suggestion in 3GPP.

Any assistance on this matter would be greatly appreciated. Thank you in advance:)

### Observed Behaviour

During Registration, UE sends Security Mode Complete as a response to Security Mode Command
but AMF ignores Security Mode Complete with the following log.
```
[gmm] WARNING: [imsi-450401362010032] No Security Context (../src/amf/gmm-sm.c:1603)
```

If MAC verification fails even once, Security Mode Procedure cannot be completed, and UE cannot be registered. 
The lines below block all Security Mode Complete messages.
https://github.com/open5gs/open5gs/blob/79d3c7078f04b4efefd21230f3f40acb28b174ea/src/amf/gmm-sm.c#L1676-L1679
You have to remove UE_CONTEXT to register the UE again.

### eNodeB/gNodeB

QCT OmniRAN

### UE Models and versions

QCT E3D

items.title: [Bug]: PDU session fails when changing the DNN configuration of a registered UE.
items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.6.4

### Steps to reproduce

1. Configure and deploy open5gs with two UPFs (1 UPF is on a remote location) and two DNNs (each DNN associated to one of the UPFs).
2. Register a UE to the core and assign it to DNN-1 (nomad).
3. Connect UE, set the APN setting to DNN-1, and test that the PDU session is up and there is external network connectivity.
4. On the core, assign UE to a different DNN, i.e. DNN-2 (aws).
5. On the UE, set the APN setting to DNN-2. (there is no internet connectivity, data connectivity/5G icon shows up)
6. On the UE, trigger airplane mode ON/OFF a few times. (there is no internet connectivity, data connectivity/5G icon shows up)
7. Restart the UE. (there is no internet connectivity, data connectivity/5G icon shows up)
8. Restart all core components. (Internet connectivity restored)

### Logs

_No response_

### Expected behaviour

Be able to change the DNN configuration of registered UEs without restarting the phone or the Open5GS services. The following operation is expected:

1. (When the DNN configuration is changed on the core); PDU session on the UE drops.
2. (When the new APN configuration is applied on the UE); a new PDU session is created which is also associated to a different UPF.

### Observed Behaviour

1. (When the DNN configuration is changed on the core); UE still shows that the PDU session is up and running.
2. (When the new APN configuration is applied on the UE); the UE shows that a new PDU session is established but AMF logs show "DNN Not Supported OR Not Subscribed in the Slice". There is no internet connectivity.
3. (When airplane mode is triggered ON/OFF for a few times on the UE); the UE shows that a new PDU session is established but AMF logs show "DNN Not Supported OR Not Subscribed in the Slice". There is no internet connectivity.
4. (When UE is power-cycled); the UE shows that a new PDU session is established but AMF logs show "DNN Not Supported OR Not Subscribed in the Slice". There is no internet connectivity.
5. (When Core is restarted); UE re-connects to the cell and successfully connects to the internet using the new APN configuration. No error/warning logs shown in the core.

### eNodeB/gNodeB

Nokia Airscale 22R4

### UE Models and versions

iPhone 14 Pro

items.title: [Bug]: NF does not clean up SBI's "client" context
items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

latest main

### Steps to reproduce



- To replicate the issue faster, modify amf.yaml and add/change
```
max:
  peer: 10
```

- Start NRF, SCP, AMF.

- Start UDM, wait for it to register to NRF, then stop it.
- Modify udm.yaml, assign a new IP address for UDM.
```
udm:
  sbi:
    - addr: 127.0.0.100
```

- Repeat a couple of times with starting the UDM, stopping it, and changing IP address to a completely new one.
- AMF receives a NF status notification from NRF each time UDM is started/stopped.
- On UDM deregistering, AMF does not properly clean up SBI's 'client' context,
so it crashes once it exhausts it's memory pool of clients

### Logs

```shell
10/18 06:19:04.261: [sbi] INFO: [3c730420-6d7e-41ee-b864-f35eef7b12ca] (NRF-notify) NF registered (../lib/sbi/nnrf-handler.c:725)
10/18 06:19:04.261: [sbi] INFO: [3c730420-6d7e-41ee-b864-f35eef7b12ca] (NRF-notify) NF Profile updated (../lib/sbi/nnrf-handler.c:735)
10/18 06:19:04.261: [sbi] FATAL: ogs_sbi_client_add: Assertion `client' failed. (../lib/sbi/client.c:111)
10/18 06:19:04.262: [core] FATAL: backtrace() returned 12 addresses (../lib/core/ogs-abort.c:37)
/usr/local/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libogssbi.so.2(ogs_sbi_client_add+0x22b) [0x7fcf01200ef5]
/usr/local/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libogssbi.so.2(+0x43e0f) [0x7fcf0120ee0f]
/usr/local/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libogssbi.so.2(+0x4421c) [0x7fcf0120f21c]
/usr/local/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libogssbi.so.2(ogs_sbi_client_associate+0x3eb) [0x7fcf0120fa77]
/usr/local/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libogssbi.so.2(ogs_nnrf_nfm_handle_nf_status_notify+0xc9e) [0x7fcf0121ca85]
open5gs-amfd(+0x37c1c) [0x56497605bc1c]
/usr/local/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libogscore.so.2(ogs_fsm_dispatch+0x119) [0x7fcf0172bc0c]
open5gs-amfd(+0xa2cc) [0x56497602e2cc]
/usr/local/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libogscore.so.2(+0x1197a) [0x7fcf0171c97a]
/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libc.so.6(+0x94ac3) [0x7fcf008edac3]
/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libc.so.6(clone+0x44) [0x7fcf0097ebf4]
Aborted
```
```


### Expected behaviour

`ogs_sbi_client_t` should be deallocated in case that noone references it anymore.

### Observed Behaviour

When NF receives info about a new registered NF from NRF, it allocates `ogs_sbi_client_t` from the memory pool.
Then it's reference counter is incremented via a macro `OGS_SBI_SETUP_CLIENT()` by a `ogs_sbi_nf_instance_t` and for each `ogs_sbi_nf_service_t`.

When NF instance is deregistered, reference counters for both `ogs_sbi_nf_instance_t` and `ogs_sbi_nf_service_t` is correctly decremented.
But noone decrements the ref counter of the `ogs_sbi_client_t` the final time, causing a `client` to remain active in the pool.

This works without a problem, in case that all NF's are given static IP's. `ogs_sbi_client_t` will be then reused, since the IP hasn't changed. But in the case of Kubernetes environment, each time that a NF restarts, it will be given a new Service IP, causing a client pool to exhaust of it's items.


Any suggestions on how to attempt to fix this issue?
Commenting out `OGS_OBJECT_REF(client);` in `ogs_sbi_client_add()` of course does not work, since it deallocates the context prematurely.

N/A

N/A

items.title: pgwtun occasionally stop functioning.

labels.name: Housekeeping:ToClose
labels.description: Issues reviewed and closed. Old requests, issues which are not bug, feature or documentation request

items.body:
I'd elaborate something I observed on pgwtun issues.

1. ubuntu 18.04 has multiple network configuring tools, the default netplan/NetworkManager must be disabled, leaving systemd-networkd as the only controller of the network.

2. When pgwtun fails, there will be no error message from nextEPC, and all UEs will not get any downlink traffic.  

3. During trouble shooting, I found that the two series of config files in /etc/nextepc are multually confusing.   For exmaple, when you run nextepc-epcd, it is supposed to read only one config file /etc/nextepc/nextepc.conf, however, I receive unexpected parsing error from other files like /etc/nextepc/mme.conf.   If you find your execution unpredictable or uncontrollable (such as server listening to unwanted IP addresses), it is probably interfered by the config files that were not supposed to be read.   Separating these interfering files solves the problem.   In my case, I move away all the config files from /etc/nextepc except nextepc.conf, now it works fine.

My working solution:  (setting up pgwtun from scratch)

apt-get install udev net-tools
systemctl start systemd-udevd

sh -c "echo 'net.ipv6.conf.pgwtun.disable_ipv6=0' > /etc/sysctl.d/30-nextepc.conf"
sysctl -p /etc/sysctl.d/30-nextepc.conf

F= /etc/systemd/network/99-nextepc.network &&\
echo [Match] >>$F &&\
echo Name=pgwtun >>$F &&\
echo [Network] >>$F &&\
echo Address=45.45.0.1/16 >>$F

systemctl enable systemd-networkd
systemctl restart systemd-networkd
ifconfig pgwtun down
ifconfig pgwtun up

items.title: [AMF] Unexpected UE Aggregate Maximum Bit Rate IE in the NGAP initial context setup request message

labels.name: Housekeeping:ToClose
labels.description: Issues reviewed and closed. Old requests, issues which are not bug, feature or documentation request

items.body:
Hi,

we experienced some issues in our 5G SA testbed (Quectel RM500 + Amarisoft Callbox + Open5Gs). Although being able to connect and obtain an IP address, it seems that the UE is not able to initiate a PDU session. It gets only fixed when restarting the gNB or after an UE context release. 

According to Amarisoft's support, it seems that the AMF is wrongly sending the UE Aggregate Maximum Bit Rate IE in the NGAP initial context setup request message while no PDU session is being present. 
[Initial context setup request.txt](https://github.com/open5gs/open5gs/files/6439805/Initial.context.setup.request.txt)

But as stated in 3GPP 38.413 chapter 9.2.2.1, this IE should be present if the PDU Session Resource Setup List IE is present, which is not the case. So the gNB ignores it. Later on when the PDU session is opened, the AMF does not send the UE Aggregate Maximum Bit Rate in the NGAP PDU session resource setup request message (maybe because it was already sent in the initial context setup request message). As a consequence, the gNB does not have an UE AMBR configured and so does not schedule the DL IP packets. 

[PDU session resource setup request.txt](https://github.com/open5gs/open5gs/files/6439806/PDU.session.resource.setup.request.txt)

If you modify the AMF to send the IE in the initial context setup when there is a PDU session present, and in the NGAP PDU session resource setup request message otherwise, things should work.

Best regards,
Miguel.

items.title: MME crashes with Assert on receiving unknown TEID in GTP2C
items.body:
If you operate a network with dedicated MME, S-GW, P-GW, etc. and the MME crashes or restarts for some reason, the S-GW will have state about existing tunnels, which the MME then has lost.

However, any S11 GTP2c message with unknown TEID will again crash the MME, resulting in a possibly extended series of crashes.

The MME should
* respond to any GTPv2C request with unknown TEID using cause = "Context is not found"
* drop any GTPv2C response with unknown TEID

I will try to work on a fix, just creating this for tracking the issue

items.title: AMF RM metric RegisteredSubNbr exposes wrong value

labels.name: type:bug
labels.description: Open5GS bug

labels.name: Help Wanted
labels.description: Maintainers are not working on this issue so community help is wanted.

labels.name: Housekeeping:ToClose
labels.description: Issues reviewed and closed. Old requests, issues which are not bug, feature or documentation request

items.body:
AMF RM metric AMF_METR_GAUGE_RM_REGISTEREDSUBNBR (RM.RegisteredSubNbrMean/Max - [ETSI TS 128 552 V16.13.0](https://www.etsi.org/deliver/etsi_ts/128500_128599/128552/16.13.00_60/ts_128552v161300p.pdf), 5.2.1 Registered subscribers measurement) does not expose proper value since **RM_State** removal in commit [9f4a9790e3cb1f7f05c8f97cf6a99c15752e05d5](https://github.com/open5gs/open5gs/commit/9f4a9790e3cb1f7f05c8f97cf6a99c15752e05d5).

AMF is not aware of UE RM state anymore.

- *amf_ue* keeps contexts of all UEs registered since startup regardless of their RM state.
- *ran_ue* keeps contexts of all CM CONNECTED UEs.
- UEs in CM IDLE state are RM REGISTERED but are not evidenced.
- GMM state of an UE, which is trying to register, always has value *gmm_state_initial_context_setup* regardless of its current RM state.

When AMF receives Registration Request due to (R)AN or UE restart, all the initial registration procedures are always carried out even if the UE has already been RM REGISTERED.
So the Registered subscribers metric is incremented unacceptably. The result is increasing of this gauge above number of all administered UEs.

Dear Sukchan,

I have made some testing against the Open5GS AMF recently, with a custom gNB and UE emulator. I am testing Open5GS version 2.5.6, from the Ubuntu package repository. I found 1 assert which can be triggered quite easily to crash the AMF, from an unauthenticated subscriber perspective. See below for the details.

Crash the AMF with a _NAS Registration Request_ containing an invalid SUPI/SUCI:

When a connecting UE initiates a 5G NAS Registration Request with an invalid SUPI/SUCI non-IMSI identifier, the AMF breaks due to an assert:
```
01/23 15:01:06.897: [amf] DEBUG: amf_state_operational(): AMF_EVENT_5GMM_MESSAGE (../src/amf/amf-sm.c:78)
01/23 15:01:06.897: [nas] ERROR: ogs_nas_5gs_suci_from_mobile_identity: Expectation `mobile_identity_suci->h.supi_format == OGS_NAS_5GS_SUPI_FORMAT_IMSI' failed. (../lib/nas/5gs/conv.c:70)
01/23 15:01:06.897: [amf] FATAL: amf_ue_find_by_message: Assertion `suci' failed. (../src/amf/context.c:1540)
01/23 15:01:06.897: [core] FATAL: backtrace() returned 7 addresses (../lib/core/ogs-abort.c:37)
/usr/bin/open5gs-amfd(+0x25d50) [0x55dcb70a3d50]

As this happens pre-authentication / security activation, it seems quite important to avoid that the AMF breaks and restarts due to a malformed or misencoded IE provided by a malfunctioning terminal, a proper error handling would be more appropriate to avoid down-time of the AMF.

items.title: Open5Gs forgetting the UE Radio Capabilities when UE is sending NAS "De-Registration Request" with "type = Switch-off"

labels.name: type:enhancement
labels.description: Enhance performance or improve usability of original features.

labels.name: Housekeeping:ToClose
labels.description: Issues reviewed and closed. Old requests, issues which are not bug, feature or documentation request

items.body:
The following description is the same for 4G S1-AP and 5G NG-AP.
If the eNodeB/gNodeB is sending to Open5Gs MME/AMF the "UE Radio Capability Info" message, then Open5Gs correctly remembers this for the UE.
So when UE is doing Service Request (for example) or other procedures, then the Open5Gs includes in the "Initial Context Setup Request" message also the "UE Radio Capability" IE. This is correct behavior.
However, the Open5Gs remembers forever the UE Radio Capabilities from the first time and always includes this in the "Initial Context Setup Request" message. So eNodeB/gNodeB are NOT querying the UE for its Radio Capabilities because it is already included in "Initial Context Setup Request" message.
The only way to cause "Open5Gs" to forget the UE Radio Capabilities is by rebooting the Open5Gs machine (or by restarting the services).
This can cause the following bad scenario in current Open5Gs implementation: 
1) UE Model 1 successfully ATTACHed to the Open5Gs the first time so Open5Gs has no knowledge of its Radio Capabilities.
2) eNB/gNB is sending to Open5Gs the "UE Radio Capability Info" message, then Open5Gs remembers this for the UE Model 1.
3) UE Model 1 is powered off, so sending to Open5Gs NAS message "De-Registration Request" with "type = Switch-off".
4) SIM Card is removed from UE Model 1 and placed into UE Model 2.
5) UE Model 2 is powered on and does ATTACH with Open5Gs.
In current Open5Gs implementation the "Initial Context Setup Request" message for the ATTACH of UE Model 2 is including the "UE Radio Capability" IE of UE Model 1. Hence eNodeB/gNodeB are NOT querying UE Model 2 for its Radio Capabilities.
This causes a mismatch that eNodeB/gNodeB are applying for UE Model 2 the Radio Capabilities of UE Model 1, even though UE Model 1 and UE Modle 2 have different Radio Capabilities.

The solution here is to fix Open5Gs implementation that in the case the UE is sending Open5Gs NAS message "De-Registration Request" with "type = Switch-off" then the Open5Gs forgets the UE Radio Capabilities.
This ensures 2 things:
1) that on the next UE ATTACH the eNodeB/gNodeB will query the UE for its Radio Capabilities
2) that Open5Gs will remember the UE Radio Capabilities and include it in "Initial Context Setup Request" message for the other relevant scenarios (like Service Request).

You can test by doing the following:

```
$ git clone https://github.com/open5gs/open5gs

Sukchan

labels.name: Housekeeping:ToClose

items.body:
Dear community,

I have been following the VoLTE tutorial using srsenb and open5gs. The RF board is a B205mini, srsenb runs on a physical machine with IP 192.168.1.88 and open5gs/kamailio/FoHSS run on a VM with IP 192.168.1.95. The USIM is from open-cells, I have programmed the USIM following section 20 in the VoLTE tutorial. 

I have tested two UEs, a Samsung S5 and a HUAWEI P30 but they both got the initial context setup failure. At first I was using the drb.conf from https://github.com/srsLTE/srsLTE/issues/435
to configure srsenb, when I tried to get the UE to attach, srsenb showed "The QCI 0 for DRB 1 is invalid or not configured.". I'm not sure why QCI 0 is needed, neither the internet apn nor the ims apn have the QCI 0 requirement. Then the enb sent the mme the "initial context setup failure, radio network cause=unspecified" message, after the "initial context setup request, attach accept" message it got from the mme. To get rid of the QCI 0 problem I added some arbitrary QCI=0 configuration into drb.conf (attached in the zip file) and run the enb again. The QCI 0 message has disappeared but nothing else has changed. 

I have attached my mme/hss log and the pcapng. What should I do to narrow down the actual cause of the problem? Any help would be appreciated.

[VoLTE.zip](https://github.com/open5gs/open5gs/files/4836720/VoLTE.zip)

items.title: UPF keeps sending GTP Tunnel Downlink traffic to the IP address of first gNodeB the UE did ATTACH on, even when UE is moving between gNodeBs

labels.name: type:bug
labels.description: Open5GS bug

items.body:
In my lab I have a setup of 2 X Airspan gNodeBs AirSpeed 2900 (from the list of "tested gNodeB with Open5Gs").
gNodeB #1 has IP address ending with 225, and gNodeB #2 has IP address ending with 221.
I am doing the following sequence:
Step 1) ATTACH 5G UE on gNodeB #1 --> this is successful and UE receives IP address of 10.45.0.8 (configured for this UE in Open5Gs webGUI)
Step 2) Initiate ping to 10.45.0.8 from the Open5Gs machine itself. This means ping from 10,45,0,1 (ogstun) to 10.45.0.8 --> ping is successful, UE replies to the ping.
Step 3) UE sends 5G-NAS "Deregistration Request" to Open5Gs which is successful.
Step 4) Attenuate RF signal of gNodeB #1 so RF signal of gNodeB #2 becomes much stronger
Step 5) ATTACH 5G UE on gNodeB #2 --> this is successful and UE receives IP address of 10.45.0.8 (configured for this UE in Open5Gs webGUI)
Step 6) Initiate ping to 10.45.0.8 from the Open5Gs machine itself. This means ping from 10,45,0,1 (ogstun) to 10.45.0.8 --> ping FAILS there is NO response from UE.
Looking at the wirshark capture I can see that the GTP Tunnel encapsulating the {Ping from 10.45.0.1 to 10.45.0.8} is actually being sent to IP address ending with 225 which is gNodeB #1 instead of IP address ending with 221 which is gNodeB #2.
The UE did a full DETACH from gNodeB #1 and NEW ATTACH to gNodeB #2 so it is not clear why the UPF still remembers the gNodeB #1 IP address for this UE GTP Downlink traffic.
It doesn't matter how many times I do for the UE the DETACH/ATTACH - the Open5Gs UPF is constantly sending the Downlink GTP Tunnel to the IP address of the FIRST gNodeB the UE did ATTACH to. 
The only way to get out of this situation is to restart the services of the Open5Gs so the Open5Gs will forget the IP address of the first gNodeB that the UE did ATTACH to.

The same behaviour from UPF occurs also if UE went to IDLE (user-inactivity) on gNodeB #1 and did Service Request on gNodeB #2. 
The UPF still sends GTP Downlink traffic to IP address of gNodeB #1

The same behaviour from UPF occurs also after 5G Handover (5G NG-AP Handover and 5G Xn-AP Handover). Even though the 5G Handover is successful, the UPF continues to send the GTP Downlink traffic to the IP address of the Source gNodeB.

[Open5gs_Logs_ATTACH_DETACH_Two_Airspan_gNodeB_28_April_2022.zip](https://github.com/open5gs/open5gs/files/8598536/Open5gs_Logs_ATTACH_DETACH_Two_Airspan_gNodeB_28_April_2022.zip)

items.title: feedback requested: PFCP synchronization?
items.body:
Hi everyone,

We have an architecture where the UPS (sgwu and upf) runs on a separate machine from the CPS (hss, pcrf, mme, sgwc, smf). Occasionally the UPS (or components on it) will crash and restart, and when this happens it creates all sorts of problems relating to the state mis-match between the CPS side (sgwc and smf) and UPS side (sgwu and upf). This generally stems from the fact that when the UPS side (sgwu and upf) restarts it loses all PFCP state. Already attached UEs cannot send traffic (since no session exists), UE disconnects fail, etc etc. I often end up having to restart the entire CPS to get everything back in sync.

I have dug through the relevant 3gpp docs for PFCP and GTPv2 and can't seem to find a great way to handle this situation in a clean, 3gpp-specific way. I think I have an okay idea for a solution, but want to hear ideas and collect as much input as possible before I start working on such a fix.

0) My main idea for a fix is to treat the CPS side (sgwc and smf) as authoritative. It handles all GTP traffic normally and stays in sync with mme, etc. Whenever there is a discrepancy, we assume that the CPS side is accurate. All fixes/modifications that follow are to help the UPS figure out the CPS'es state and get in sync with it.

1) From the CPS side, treat a PFCP de-association as if the UPS has crashed. "Save" all active sessions for that UPS element in a list somewhere. If we get any GTPv2 messages relating to these sessions (e.g. modify or delete), we can handle them directly, modify our saved sessions list correctly and send a successful response, but we don't forward these messages to UPS since we have no active association. New associations fail (as standard) due to lack of PFCP context.

2) From the UPS side (sgwu and upf), when you PFCP de-associate, destroy all active sessions that are associated with that CPS. This way, no matter what, when a UPS entity successfully creates a new PFCP association (either after extended network outage or a crash, it doesnt matter) the CPS can know that the UPS has zero active sessions from it.

3) When a UPS re-associates with CPS, the CPS sends create session messages for all the "saved" sessions mentioned in (1). Based on (2) we should know that at association time the UPS has no active sessions, so this should get us in sync.

4) Related, I would like to add some CPS/UPS code to handle other edge-cases by deferring to the CPS whenever possible, and keeping an eye towards state. e.g., if the CPS sends a Delete Session Request and the UPS has no session to speak of, don't error out, respond correctly, since technically the outcome is correct.

I believe this will take some work, but not too much. Please let me know what you think, or if there's another way to handle this that I haven't considered or found online - I'm super interested in finding the best way to fix this problem.

items.title: [FEAT] 5G Containerization Goals
items.body:
Hi @acetcom,

I am writing this to note down some features that I think maybe beneficial for open5gs within the 5G deployment method. I may be wrong but I think one of the core tenets of 5G is containerization and k8s (Kubernetes) has become the de-facto standard for container orchestration. 

To support Kubernetes some features of k8s needs to be put into consideration:

* k8s Pods are ephemeral, this is why pods are not to be referenced directly (Pod IPs often changes) instead they are abstracted away by placing a service (DNS name) in-front them, the IP of the service does not change except it is deleted or changed intentionally. This logic should be considered when the code is been developed, if a pod dies will other pods be able to support the ongoing traffic/communication..

Also on this point I think the UDSF component is designed to make the some components stateful so that in case when a pod dies, the replacement pod can pick up the state of those sessions.

* k8s has a concept of Horizontal Pod Auto-scaling whereby the number of pods can be increased with respect to incoming traffic like number of attached subscribers. Also when the number of subscribers drop below a certain threshold, the number of pods will be downscaled. I only used number of subscribers as an example, this can be other 5G component metrics (CPU utilization can also be used).

* When using service meshes tracing capabilities like Zipkin, Jaeger or OpenTracing, there is need to expose the headers (SBIs i.e. HTTP2) so that tracing can be done end to end.

* Possibility of producing the log files in JSON format, this can be useful for log processing using tools like Fluentd/Logstash/Loki..

* Performance metrics using formats that cab be scraped by Prometheus/Graphite/InfluxDB and graphed using dashboard tools like Grafana

* Configuration changes should trigger a graceful restart of the affected 5G components with little to no impact on the service (concept of configuration in k8s is configMap).

* One way to ease the lifecycle management of k8s application is the concept of k8s Operators but this does not negate that the above statements, it only makes some aspect easier. 

* If possible testing method should be able to simulate lots of UEs, this will be able to see how the deployment performs under load.

These are just what I think, I just want to put down my thoughts just in case there are plans to improve the features of open5gs 5G core.

This is also open to everyone to contribute especially if you can contribute code wise in this regard.

items.title: SA attach issue
items.body:
Hey @acetcom 

I've spent some time studying my SA attach issue, and have narrowed the problem down. It seems to be related to the session context...

Currently running tests with a Qualcomm x55 modem in SA mode. I get exactly the same results with the Huawei Balong 5000 in SA mode.

Fresh compile of git master; commit 22b09443ce41c34786df167916d603bd17771d69. I cleaned out MongoDB and recreated the USIM profiles.

Running all Open5GS components on the Amarisoft gNB computer, so all NFs using the default IP addresses. gNB is on `127.0.1.1`
____

### Clean Restart

- Completely restart the entire core network; ie power cycle all 5GC control plane functions + the UPF.
- Attach gNB
- Attach UE

Result = attach works first time
PCAP and all debug log files = [SA_restartAll.zip](https://github.com/open5gs/open5gs/files/6160460/SA_restartAll.zip)


After this initial successful attach,
* I can powercycle the UE and it reattaches successfully
* I can powercycle the gNB; after it does NGsetup, UE reattaches successfully

____

### Control Plane Restart

- Ok, so this time we assume something has happened with the control plane daemons, and they have restarted
- The UPF remains running (from the above test) - does not get restarted
- After the SMF comes back online, it re- PFCP associates with the UPF
- Attach gNB
- Attach UE

Result = attach fails
PCAP and all debug log files = [SA_restartAll_exceptUPF.zip](https://github.com/open5gs/open5gs/files/6160461/SA_restartAll_exceptUPF.zip)

After the UE sends `UplinkNASTransport`, SMF sends UPF a `PFCP Session Deletion Request` message. UPF responds with session context errors, then the control plane seems to stop doing anything, leading to the gNB timing out after 10 seconds and kicking the UE. The UE then goes into a cycle of failed attach requests.

This is totally repeatable, and occurs with both the Qualcomm and Huawei UEs. 

____

Not sure what you make of this? Is this expected behaviour?

Cheers
Kenny

items.title: 5GSA attach variations
items.body:
Hi Sukchan

I've been comparing SA attaches of Amarisoft AMF vs Open5GS AMF. There are some differences in the Open5GS NGAP messages, and this seems to result in SA devices taking much longer to establish a data connection. 

#### Setup
Huawei 5G CPE in SA mode
Amarisoft gNB `127.0.1.1`
Amarisoft AMF `127.0.0.1`  rel 15

Huawei 5G CPE in SA mode
Amarisoft gNB `10.10.0.101` (same config, just pointing to the different AMF)
Open5GS AMF `10.10.0.2`


#### Observation - Amarisoft AMF
Attaches to Amarisoft AMF, almost immediate data connection 
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/8739983/109984924-25a36480-7cfc-11eb-99a4-1e19169cce4a.png)

#### Observation - Open5GS AMF
Attaches to Open5GS AMF, but takes nearly 2 mins to establish data connection
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/8739983/109985049-4370c980-7cfc-11eb-8ba3-95dc628d570b.png)
... lots of waiting
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/8739983/109986838-04dc0e80-7cfe-11eb-8f8d-7d422ce9d687.png)


#### PCAPs

InitialContextSetupRequest and PDUSessionResourceRequest are different 
[pcaps.zip](https://github.com/open5gs/open5gs/files/6084746/pcaps.zip)

The Amarisoft AMF is rel15, so I am not sure if these differences are a result of the versioning. Do you have any ideas?

Thanks
Kenny

items.title: Uplink Data Rate Limit (AMBR) Default Units Break Baicells UE
items.body:
Version Introduced: somewhere between 2.1.7 and 2.2.6
Behavior: The AMBR applied to uplink traffic does not reflect the AMBR configured in the webui or present in mongodb

Details:
In a lab setup with a baicells nova-223 TDD basestation and open5gs 2.2.6, the uplink AMBR appears to be applied without the units modifier. I am not sure if the issue is with the overall subscriber AMBR, the slice AMBR, or both. When I set the uplink and downlink AMBRs to 1 Gbps (effectively unlimited in this low-bandwidth test network), the downlink is correctly able to use the entire band, but the uplink is limited to iperf throughput of ~200Kbps. I confirmed the subscriber entry in mongo lists the ambr as `"ambr" : { "uplink" : { "value" : 1, "unit" : 3 }, "downlink" : { "value" : 1, "unit" : 3 } }`. Changing the entry in the webui to 1Gbps in units of bps leads to a mongo entry of `"ambr" : { "uplink" : { "value" : 1000000000, "unit" : 0 }, "downlink" : { "value" : 1000000000, "unit" : 0 } }`, and in this configuration the UE again has the expected full bandwidth in both uplink and downlink throughput. I can confirm this issue is not present in 2.1.7 (which uses a different unitless db schema).

I am not sure if this is related at all to #806 and changes made to specify the unit, but it seems likely. I'll try and debug some more and add info here.

items.title: Unable to register with IMS in VoLTE testbed
items.body:
Dear all,

First of all, I would like to thank you all for this awesome and beautiful project. I've been working with LTE network prototypes for 2 years, and this EPC implementation is the best, especially when it comes to features, documentation and support.

I am currently working with a small VoLTE testbed at home which, if everything works well, will be deployed in a server for LTE learning courses and subjects at college. I've been following the official guide published in the documentation page related to this project. So far, I have been able to deploy Kamailio IMS and Open5GS until step 24. It's pretty much the entire guide. I have faced several issues that I have solved, mostly related with installation and execution tasks. But, right now, I am stuck with UE registration with IMS core/components.

My testbed consists of a desktop computer running Ubuntu 18.04.4 LTS and connected to my home LAN (_192.168.1.0/24_) with IP address _192.168.1.100_. This machine runs an Ubuntu 18.04.4 LTS virtual machine in VirtualBox, which has a single network adapter configured in bridged mode, so that it is connected to my home LAN and its IP address is _192.168.1.150_.

The virtual machine hosts and runs Kamailio IMS and Open5GS, and the Ubuntu OS in the bare metal machine runs srsLTE. The S1 interface is deployed through my LAN, so the eNodeB is located at _192.168.1.100_ and the MME/EPC/IMS is located at _192.168.1.150_. I have configured Kamailio and Open5GS with that IP address accordingly. I have defined 2 tun interfaces: **ogstun** with pool **_10.254.0.0/24_** for Internet connectivity to UEs; and **imstun** with pool **_10.254.1.0/24_** for IMS connectivity.

At the moment I have only defined and created one subscriber, since I wanted to test the VoLTE registration: if registration succeded, I would add another subscriber and test making a call.
The subscriber is added to the HSS database, and two APNs are defined: **internet** and **ims**, according to the guide. QCI, priorities and other parameters are set as instructed. Therefore, both APNs are configured in _pgw.yaml_ file and linked to respective tun devices. I am only using IPv4 addresses, so tun devices do not feature IPv6 pools (I have removed them). The subscriber is also added to the FHoSS HSS as explained in the guide.

I have downloaded the CoIMS app and followed all the instructions to load the SHA certificate to the USIM card. I have configured the two APNs in the device, and it successfully attachs to the LTE network and has Internet connectivity, but there is no IMS registration. The CoIMS app shows that it has carrier privileges (App has Carrier Privileges is true) and the parameter _carrier_volte_provisioned_bool_ is _true_. The device runs Android 8.1 so the parameter _SIM Carrier Id_ doesn't show. When entering _Test mode_, under _IMS status_, the device says that it is not registered with IMS.

I have done the attach procedure while capturing traffic with Wireshark, and I couldn't find any SIP message related with registration. I have configured the DRB file for the eNodeB as shown [in this srsLTE issue](https://github.com/srsLTE/srsLTE/issues/435), but I can't find the dedicated radio bearer setup message in the capture. Open5GS-PGW log shows that the UE has only a context for the **internet** APN, but not for the **ims** one.

The UE is a bq Aquaris V, running Android 8.1.0 as I said earlier. It's a mid-range device, but I think it should support VoLTE, since there is a VoLTE slider in the test mode, although I might be wrong.

Could you please help me troubleshoot the issue? I've been trying for the whole day and I don't know what to do now.

I have attached a _.zip_ file with the PCAP file and logs for all EPC components.

Thank you.
[open5gs_volte_test.zip](https://github.com/acetcom/open5gs/files/4954928/open5gs_volte_test.zip)

items.title: HSS and PCRF not working
items.body:
Hello,

I am working with nextepc and srsLTE for my testbed. Till yesterday everything was working fine. Today when I restarted the services of nextepc, I am facing problems in starting HSS and PCRF services.
 
I would like to post the errors and some more information here. 

Issue: 
epc1@epc1-VirtualBox:~$ sudo systemctl status nextepc-hssd.service
● nextepc-hssd.service - NextEPC HSS Daemon
   Loaded: loaded (/lib/systemd/system/nextepc-hssd.service; enabled; vendor preset: enabled)
   Active: activating (auto-restart) since Mi 2018-08-29 13:41:19 CEST; 6ms ago
  Process: 9252 ExecStart=/usr/bin/nextepc-hssd -f /etc/nextepc/hss.conf (code=exited, status=0/SUCCESS)
 Main PID: 9252 (code=exited, status=0/SUCCESS)

When I go through the hss.log, it says

File Logging : '/var/log/nextepc/hss.log'
[08/29 13:48:20.666] ERRR: Failed to conect to server [mongodb://localhost/nextepc] (context.c:339)
[08/29 13:48:20.666] DB-Client try to terminate
[08/29 13:48:20.667] DB-Client terminate...done

But, I have checked the status of mongobd using this:

epc1@epc1-VirtualBox:~$ sudo service mongodb status
● mongodb.service - An object/document-oriented database
   Loaded: loaded (/lib/systemd/system/mongodb.service; enabled; vendor preset: enabled)
   Active: active (running) since Mi 2018-08-29 13:04:01 CEST; 43min ago
     Docs: man:mongod(1)
 Main PID: 723 (mongod)
   CGroup: /system.slice/mongodb.service
           └─723 /usr/bin/mongod --config /etc/mongodb.conf

Warning: Journal has been rotated since unit was started. Log output is incomplete or unavailable.

P.S: I had an issue in running the mongodb service, because of the insufficient storage from the journals. So, I have edited the mongodb.conf and turned off journals. After this, mongodb service was up and running.

Please, let me know what should be done. Am i missing out something here. Any help is appreciated.

Thanks in advance.
Dinesh

items.title: OPc and OP used in FHoSS (Update 2)
items.body:
I am sorry that I close the previous issue accidentially. the UE can now send 2nd SIP REGISTEER throuf IPSEC tunnel.  I would like to know why we need to this action?


> > double check on that. I beleived it is due to the authorization is always null. so it never goes to that routine. In my setup, the HSS only serve for CX not ZH, not sure it is the root cause.
> 
> That is fine. I also use only Cx not Zh interface.
> 
> Regarding the authorization, you can try one more thing. In the FHoSS GUI, go to IMPI (Private identity) section and in that select the IMPI of UE you are trying to attach and in the IMPI details of that UE, you will find the below section
> 
> ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/4115839/84739591-3401f280-afac-11ea-9f8a-2c9c466edf2b.png)
> 
> In that select Reason as "Remove SCSCF" and then select the "RTR-All" button (while FHoSS is connected to SCSCF and ICSCF) and wait for some time..After this try to restart FHoSS and SCSCF and re-try.

items.title: ERRR: The certificate is expired
items.body:
Hi

NextEPC was working with no issues. While I was making some tests, I had to restart the mme, but I got these error messages:

> File Logging : '/var/log/nextepc/mme.log'
> Configuration : '/etc/nextepc/mme.conf'
> [08/21 16:26:39.636] MME try to initialize
> [08/21 16:26:39.867] ERRR:  - The certificate is expired. (fd_init.c:116)
> [08/21 16:26:39.868] ERRR: ERROR: in '((fd_conf_parse()))' :    Invalid argument (fd_init.c:116)
> [08/21 16:26:39.868] ERRR: ERROR: in '(fd_core_parseconf(conffile))' :  Invalid argument (fd_init.c:116)
> [08/21 16:26:39.868] freeDiameter[6]: Initiating freeDiameter shutdown sequence (1)
> [08/21 16:26:39.970] ASSERT: !(ret == CORE_OK).  (mme_fd_path.c:1100)
> [08/21 16:26:39.970] ERRR: Failed to intialize MME (mme.c:30)
> [08/21 16:26:39.970] FATL: NextEPC initialization failed. Aborted (main.c:152)
> [08/21 16:26:39.970] MME try to terminate
> [08/21 16:26:39.970] MME terminate...done


Same error when I restart pgw service:

> File Logging : '/var/log/nextepc/pgw.log'
> Configuration : '/etc/nextepc/pgw.conf'
> [08/21 16:31:47.825] PGW try to initialize
> [08/21 16:31:47.860] ERRR:  - The certificate is expired. (fd_init.c:116)
> [08/21 16:31:47.860] ERRR: ERROR: in '((fd_conf_parse()))' :    Invalid argument (fd_init.c:116)
> [08/21 16:31:47.860] ERRR: ERROR: in '(fd_core_parseconf(conffile))' :  Invalid argument (fd_init.c:116)
> [08/21 16:31:47.860] freeDiameter[6]: Initiating freeDiameter shutdown sequence (1)
> [08/21 16:31:47.962] ASSERT: !(ret == 0).  (pgw_fd_path.c:1021)
> [08/21 16:31:47.962] ERRR: Failed to intialize PGW (pgw.c:30)
> [08/21 16:31:47.962] FATL: NextEPC initialization failed. Aborted (main.c:152)
> [08/21 16:31:47.962] PGW try to terminate
> [08/21 16:31:47.962] PGW terminate...done

Any idea what is wrong? I checked the server date (no problem) and the expiry date of the freediameter certificate (no problem).

> $ openssl x509 -in /etc/nextepc/freeDiameter/cacert.pem -noout -enddate
> notAfter=Aug 14 13:40:41 2027 GMT
> $ date
> Tue Aug 21 16:36:13 UTC 2018

I am using v0.3.9

Thanks.

items.title: Different UEs can not reach each other
items.body:
I have successfully set up NextEPC with srs-eNB on a PC, which is now disconnected from the internet.
I have two UEs (45.45.0.2 and 45.45.0.3) attached, both can ping the eNB (45.45.0.1), and I can ping both from the eNB. But unfortunately I can not ping one UE from the other, which I need.
So to sum it up:
45.45.0.2 <-> 45.45.0.1 works fine
45.45.0.3 <-> 45.45.0.1 works finde
45.45.0.2 <-> 45.45.0.3 does not work
Any idea how to solve this problem?
